Incorporating laughter therapy into treatment plans could help ease respiratory difficulties in patients suffering from a widespread lung condition, new research indicates.

Scientists behind the study suggest that the "simple, low-cost" intervention performs on par with conventional breathing drills and may work to "complement existing care" for individuals living with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

In the UK alone, an estimated 1.7 million people suffer from COPD, including roughly 600,000 who remain undiagnosed.

The clinical trial evaluated 63 patients diagnosed with COPD who were receiving care at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital in Turkey.

Researchers assigned a third of the group to laughter therapy sessions, while the remaining participants were guided through pursed-lip breathing routines or received no specialised exercises.

open image in gallery Rather than relying on an inhaler, people could turn to laughter therapy ( PA )

After being shown how to perform the techniques, patients were asked to complete 30-minute sessions three times weekly over an eight-week duration.

Respiratory function was evaluated before, during, and after the intervention.

Results demonstrated that both laughter therapy and pursed-lip breathing achieved measurable improvements compared to the group receiving no intervention.

Dr Goncagul Aldan, a lecturer and nurse at Hacettepe University Faculty of Nursing in Ankara, said: "People with COPD often feel breathless, even during simple daily activities. This reduces their quality of life and makes them increasingly dependent on others for care.

"Managing COPD requires more than medication alone. Patients need a holistic, approach to help them cope with their symptoms, the physical burden of the disease, and its emotional and psychological impact.

"With this research, we wanted to explore whether additional simple, low-cost techniques could complement existing care.

"Laughter therapy had already shown promising results in a number of other chronic conditions. Its accessible, enjoyable nature suggests it could equally benefit COPD patients, not only in coping with the daily stress of living with a chronic illness, but also in directly supporting their respiratory health."

Symptoms of COPD NHS The main symptoms of COPD are: shortness of breath, particularly when you're active

a persistent chesty cough with phlegm – some people may dismiss this as just a "smoker's cough"

frequent chest infections

persistent wheezing

The positive impacts of both interventions persisted a month after the programme concluded, Dr Aldan noted.

She said: "These findings offer hope that simple, low-cost techniques which patients can practice at home – without any equipment or specialist support – may reduce breathlessness and improve daily wellbeing.

"Both interventions also showed promising results in improving overall health, suggesting that laughter therapy may be a worthwhile area for further investigation alongside pursed-lip breathing in COPD care.

"In COPD, the airways tend to collapse during exhalation, trapping stale air inside the lungs.

"Pursed-lip breathing creates a gentle back pressure that allows this trapped air to escape, slows the breathing rate, and helps patients feel more in control of their breathing.

open image in gallery Laughter therapy could help millions in the UK ( PA )

"Laughter may exercise the breathing muscles, promote deeper exhalation, and trigger the release of endorphins, offering both physical and emotional relief."

Further studies remain necessary to understand why laughter influences COPD symptoms.

Dr Aldan added: "Laughter therapy aims to evoke the effects of genuine laughter in the body. However, the mechanisms behind laughter therapy in COPD remain poorly understood, and more comprehensive research is needed."

The trial's findings will be presented at the European Respiratory Society (ERS) Congress in Barcelona.

Emma Rubach, head of health advice at Asthma + Lung UK, said: "This exciting study shows that laughter therapy is an effective way to control breathlessness for people with COPD.

"This research adds to growing evidence showing that innovative non-traditional therapies can improve people’s ability to manage lung conditions like COPD.

"While further studies with a larger number of patients are still needed, laughter therapy appears to be a fun, accessible and effective self-management technique to help people with COPD control their symptoms.

"While there is still no cure for COPD, which often leaves people fighting for breath, innovations like laughter therapy have real potential to provide genuine relief and improve the quality of life for the 1.7 million people in the UK who have the condition."

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

News.title: Kimi Antonelli’s stunning home Italian GP victory all but seals first F1 title
News.content:
The 20-year-old also benefited from a perfectly-timed (from his perspective at least) mid-race virtual safety car when Lance Stroll retired his Aston Martin, which allowed Antonelli a cheap stop to switch to fresh mediums while Russell stayed out on used hards. But at some point you just have to take your hat off to the youngster.

Antonelli was irresistible. He had already surged from 19th on the grid to 12th by the time the red flag came out at the end of lap 2. He was up to sixth a couple of laps after the race resumed. And by lap 18 of a 53-lap race, he had passed Russell for the lead for the first time. That is some going.

Having caught up to Russell, the two Mercedes drivers engaged in an entertaining battle for a few laps, the pair of them yo-yoing in and out of the lead before Russell got past Antonelli on lap 23 and managed to make it stick.

But the key moment of the race came on lap 27 when Stroll stopped at the first chicane and the VSC came out. For Antonelli, the decision to switch to fresh mediums was clear. He was going to struggle to make it to the end of the race. Far better to drop a few positions and fight back on fresh rubber.

For Russell, it was far trickier. He was in the lead of the race. He was on hard tyres which he knew could get to the end of the race. And he also had the problem of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who at the time he was struggling to shake off.

Mercedes chose to keep Russell out there. In hindsight, it may have been the wrong decision. Had he stopped at that point, he would at least have stayed ahead of Antonelli, and on the same tyres. By staying out, he kept the lead but found himself relentlessly hunted down by the Italian.

By lap 49, the Italian had caught up to him. Antonelli botched his first attempt at reclaiming the lead, going wide onto the gravel at the first chicane. But he made no mistake one lap later as Russell was once again left licking his wounds.

News.title: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling
News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: Relentless Springboks give All Blacks 15 minutes of hell to lead series
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ruthlessly ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes made Rassie Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South Africa coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before.

Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan. The old scoundrel knew that if he slowed it down and let his scrum walk round the All Blacks scrum that his backs would have the precious space.

Yet, however it might feel away from Springbok turf, New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

News.title: ‘It’s just a useless gimmick’: Telegraph readers react to Dyson’s latest gadget
News.content:
Would you spend over £400 on a toothbrush? Telegraph readers aren’t convinced.

The new Dyson CameraJet has just launched, retailing for £419.99, which brushes, flosses and mouth-washes in one, with the help of a camera.

After Rebecca Astill gave her verdict on the gadget, we asked Telegraph readers for their views and whether Dyson can convince them to trade in their old faithfuls.

They share the toothbrushes they swear by, from manual to electric models, and whether they see any reason to upgrade. Here’s what they had to say.

Why readers are unconvinced

The majority of readers seem unconvinced by the CameraJet, with John arguing that a toothbrush and a smartphone “sounds like two accidents waiting to happen. Squirted in the eye with mouthwash as you drop the phone down the toilet”.

“It’s just a useless gimmick,” argues reader Donald Mckie, a retired NHS dentist. “The average patient wouldn’t have a clue what they would be looking at in their mouth on a phone screen,” he adds.

“Dyson as a brand is an aspiration for many but I don’t know how this appliance would improve anyone’s oral health.”

In his view, “the tank for the mouthwash at 12.5ml is far too small, the industry average will be somewhere near 250-300ml” to last long enough and successfully dislodge sticky plaque.

He also questions the picture quality of the camera with water spray, saliva, lips, facial hair and toothpaste in the way. “People nowadays will expect pin sharp detail, which I doubt this will deliver.”

Sports.title: Arsenal fans tease Morgan Rogers with brutal chant as Chelsea star is subbed during 2-1 win at Emirates
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fans got their own back on Morgan Rogers by serenading him with a brutal chant as he walked off the pitch.

Rogers, 24, was the subject of serious interest from the Gunners during the summer transfer window.

But he ended up joining Chelsea for £117million, and needled Gooners by saying he had signed for “the biggest club in London”.



That clearly did not sit well with Arsenal supporters when the two sides met on Sunday as they belted out a pointed message while Rogers trudged around the perimeter of the pitch after being subbed.



The chant went: “Signed for a big club, you should’ve signed for a big club.”

Rogers even flashed some fans a cheeky smile as he made his way back to the dugouts.

It is no surprise that Rogers found himself in the firing line after an eventful battle at the Emirates.



The former Aston Villa star volleyed Chelsea ahead in the second minute and stuck his tongue out at a section of Arsenal fans while celebrating.

He also furiously confronted England team-mate Declan Rice after being tripped off the ball in the second half.

But for all of his individual quality and fight, Rogers came out on the losing side.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Kai Havertz starred for Arsenal as they came from behind to win 2-1 thanks to goals from the German and Martin Odegaard.

It is now 12 consecutive head-to-heads without defeat for the Gunners as Mikel Arteta improved his already incredible record against Chelsea.

Rogers said after the game: “We are disappointed. We came here with a job to try and win, and we didn’t manage that.

“But it’s a long season and a tough place to come. They are in a really good moment right now and feeling really good.



“We’re still new, with a new manager, trying to combine our ideas and get better and better. But we know we will.

“We know we’ve got the quality in the room. It’s just about working hard on the training field and putting things right.”

Sports.title: ‘I had his head in my hands trying to keep him awake’ – Paul Ince recalls horror of Glenn Hoddle heart attack
Sports.content:
PAUL INCE has opened up about the “worst experience of my life” when he was desperately trying to keep Glenn Hoddle awake after his old England boss had suffered a heart attack.

The pair were doing punditry for BT Sport on October 27, 2018 – on Hoddle’s 61st birthday – when the Spurs icon had a cardiac arrest.



A quick-thinking sound engineer with first-aid training performed continuous CPR on Hoddle for eight to nine minutes, as well as using an on-site defibrillator to deliver a shock, before the paramedics arrived.

Ince consoled Hoddle by talking him through their shared football experiences as he held his former gaffer’s head in his hands – before the former Chelsea chief, thankfully, made a full recovery.



Ince said: “It was probably the worst experience in my life.

“We were playing table football and the next minute he just keeled over and had a heart attack, a cardiac arrest.

“I had his head in my hands trying to keep him awake, talking about the World Cup in ‘98, about our time at Wolves.

“I was probably sat there for about an hour until the medical people came. Now when I speak to him it’s on the golf course!”

It underlined to Ince the importance of everyone, ideally, being able to use a defibrillator.

Which is why the former Manchester United star, 58, is part of the campaign Every Minute Matters, where Sky Bet and the British Heart Foundation have a mission to put a stop to fear of using the life-saving equipment.



Research commissioned by Sky Bet and BHF claimed that 69 per cent of football fans surveyed believe fear could stop them using a defibrillator.

Ince added: “It shows you how important it is to get to people as quickly as possible when they’re in serious trouble.

“The fact that the defibs are in all these communities, if someone was to collapse now, 200 yards away you’d be able to get a defib machine.



“The machine does it for you, it’s not hard to work, so it’s a great, great cause.

“When I think about Glenn and see what he’s doing now, it brings a smile to my face.”

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon joins two Premier League legends in history books as England star lays on ANOTHER assist for Barcelona
Sports.content:
BARCELONA star Anthony Gordon made history in only his FOURTH match with his new club.

Gordon, 25, joined Barca in May following a £70million deal with Newcastle and signed a five-year contract at the Nou Camp.



And the winger has hit the ground running with the Blaugrana as he has already registered a staggering four assists in as many LaLiga appearances.

The ex-Everton star completed that amazing record in Barcelona‘s dominant 5-0 win at Valencia as he set up Fermin Lopez’s goal.



And the England international became only the third player to provide four assists in his first four matches in Spain’s top flight this century.

The other two are fellow ex-Premier League stars Cesc Fabregas and Luis Suarez.



What makes this record even more special is that all three players achieved it while playing for Barcelona.

Gordon‘s arrival ended the Blaugrana’s interest in signing Marcus Rashford on a permanent transfer last summer.

Rashford enjoyed a successful loan stint with the Catalan giants last season that saw him amassing a total of 14 goals and 15 assists in 49 appearances.

However, Barcelona opted against triggering the versatile forward’s £26m option to buy him from Manchester United.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Thus, Hansi Flick’s side decided to sign Gordon to fill in on the left wing and his recent record proved this was a wise choice.

But Rashford has been enjoying sparkling return to United’s squad after another move away never materialised during the summer transfer window.

The England international has played in all of Man Utd’s three Premier League matches this season.

And the forward has started in two of them as he gears up for a busy season in the Premier League and Champions league.

Sports.title: Three points from Chelsea’s defeat to Arsenal as missing stars dent Xabi Alonso’s title ambitions
Sports.content:
CHELSEA suffered their first defeat in the Premier League this season at the hands of London rivals Arsenal.

The Blues, who were missing some key players, became the first team to score against the reigning Premier League champions, who picked up a clean sheet in both of their first two games in the top flight.



And it was Morgan Rogers – the man the North Londoners identified as a priority summer signing before Chelsea hijacked the deal with a record £117million – who opened the scoring just two minutes after kick-off.

However, Arsenal hit back with former Chelsea star Kai Havertz on 25 minutes before captain Martin Odegaard completed the hosts’ comeback in the second half at the Emirates to seal their third win on the spin.



That led to Xabi Alonso‘s first Premier League defeat with his new club after winning his first two games in charge.

SunSport’s Dan King looks at three talking points following a match that left a lot to ponder on:



HOLD YOUR HANDS UP, EMI

Emi Martinez was signed because Chelsea wanted a goalkeeper who was less gaffe-prone and better with his feet than Robert Sanchez.

Not all five goals Martinez has conceded so far were his fault but the failure to stop Kai Havertz’s shot for the equaliser was very poor indeed.

Maybe the kick in the head he took early on in the game from Gabriel Magalhaes was a factor. But probably not.

The Argentine, booed on his latest return to the Emirates, made an important save from Gabriel before Riccardo Calafiori’s “goal” was rightly ruled out for offside.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Martinez denied Bukayo Saka in the first half and the save he made from the England man in the second kept his team in the game.

The 2022 World Cup winner will rightly complain about what is going on in front of him, with Chelsea and especially Maxence Lacroix looking shaky. But he has to hold his hands up when he makes a basic error like this.

CAICEDO AND COLWILL MISSED

Chelsea lost due to a goalkeeping howler and one very good goal. And they did not snatch a draw because of an excellent save.

But the absence of two of their best players from their spine proved crucial. Reece James and Romeo Lavia did pretty well in the first half to stand up to Declan Rice, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard.

But neither of them is capable of Moises Caicedo’s high-energy, high-commitment, 90-minute displays.



Without the Ecuadorian midfielder, Xabi Alonso’s side will always find it hard against top opponents.

The loss of defender Levi Colwill to injury for most of last season was a huge factor in the team’s struggles.

Despite being just 23, he brings composure and leadership to Chelsea. They also missed his defensive skills and ability to pass out from the back.

The Blues struggled to handle Kai Havertz’s movement and needed Colwill to help Wesley Fofana fight fires.



COLE PALMED OFF

Just when it seemed the real Cole Palmer was standing up again, he endured a frustrating time.

The control Arsenal had over the game was a factor, just as it was when he was anonymous for much of the win over Brighton.

In the first half, he struggled to make any impression, with just one tame shot and one cute pass which almost teed up Joao Pedro.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Palmer’s day was summed up when he burst through but could only fire a shot well off target — he was perhaps distracted by Morgan Rogers being cynically tripped by Declan Rice.



Chelsea must help him more going forward but this was not good enough.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta’s staggering record against Chelsea revealed as Arsenal make Morgan Rogers eat his words
Sports.content:
WHEN Morgan Rogers picked Chelsea over Arsenal in July, he said he had joined “the biggest club in London”.

The £117million signing – and most expensive English player of all time – did have a say when the two sides clashed at the Emirates on Sunday.



Rogers opened the scoring with a volley after 77 seconds and stuck his tongue out at the Arsenal fans for good measure.

He showed he was up for the scrap by picking a fight with, of all people, his England team-mate Declan Rice.



But Arsenal got one over on their former transfer target by coming from behind to win 2-1.

That does not make the Gunners the biggest club in London.



That claim, and exactly how to judge it, is up for debate.

But what is crystal clear is that, with Mikel Arteta in charge of Arsenal, the head-to-head battle between these two capital heavyweights is completely one-sided.

Chelsea actually edged out Arsenal in Arteta’s second game in charge.

Since that festive fixture in 2019, though, it has been one-way traffic.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

One Chelsea win in the next 17 meetings makes grim reading for the club, and for Rogers as he looks to back up his bold remark.

Chelsea have failed to beat the Gunners in any of their last TEN Premier League ties.

Take cup competitions into account and that grows to 12 without victory.



Overall, it is two Chelsea wins, four draws and 12 wins for the Gunners during Arteta’s tenure.

Arsenal ratings vs Chelsea: Havertz reminds Blues of what they let go but Lewis-Skelly in second gear KAI HAVERTZ inspired an Arsenal fight-back as they beat London rivals Chelsea to continue their perfect start. The Gunners were chasing the game after their former transfer target, Morgan Rogers, volleyed the visitors ahead after just 77 seconds. But Arsenal kept their cool and equalised when Havertz fired inside the near post midway through the first half. Havertz then set up Arsenal’s second – even though he won’t get credited with the assist – as his excellent dummy created the space for Martin Odegaard to turn in from close range. Chelsea gave Havertz his break in Premier League football when they shelled out big money to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen in 2020. But he has enjoyed tormenting them – scoring four goals in seven head-to-heads – since he moved across the capital three years later. Here is the verdict of SunSport’s Simon Collings on how each Arsenal player performed…

The Arsenal boss may have failed to convince Rogers about a move to the Emirates during a face-to-face meeting in the summer, but he has his new club’s number.

Frank Lampard, Thomas Tuchel, Graham Potter, Mauricio Pochettino, Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior have all come and gone through the revolving Stamford Bridge door since Arteta landed in North London.

On Sunday, the Spaniard showed new Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso that he still has a chokehold on this fixture.



And with Arsenal the clear favourites to reclaim their Prem title, Rogers may soon find it hard to justify the comments that riled Gooners when he plumped for their cross-town rivals.

Sports.title: Ronald Koeman’s goalkeeper son scores TWICE including 101st-minute equaliser to rescue a point for his team
Sports.content:
RONALD KOEMAN’S son scored a stunning brace to rescue a point for his team – even though he is a GOALKEEPER.

Ronald Koeman Jr is the starting keeper for Dutch club Telstar in the Eredivisie.



Koeman Jr, 31, was between the sticks when his side hosted Cambuur at BUKO Stadion.

And Henk Brugge’s side played out a 2-2 draw that promises to be remembered for a very long time.



That is because both of the hosts’ goals were scored by the Dutch shot-stopper in an intense match that saw them playing with ten men for over 70 minutes following the dismissal of Nokkvi Peyr Porisson.

In fact, Koeman Jr proved to be the hero as he picked up Telstar when they were down by two goals.



And he did so by scoring two crucial penalties, which have proven to be his forte.

The Dutchman put his team up on the scoreboard on 63 minutes, shortly after Cambuur scored their second.

And Koeman Jr saved a point with a late pen in the 11th minute of stoppage time.

The goalie is following in his father’s footsteps albeit in a different position as Koeman Sr is known as one of the best sweepers in the history of the game.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

His dad reached legendary status with the likes of Ajax, PSV Eindhoven, Netherlands and Barcelona.

in fact, Koeman Jr was born in Spain back in 1995 when his dad played for Barca.

However, the keeper has spent his entire 14-year career playing in the Netherlands for the likes of Almere, TOP Oss and of course Telstar where he has been sine 2021 and counts a total of 164 appearances.

Koeman Jr is one of very few goalkeepers assigned as penalty takers in this day and age.

A number of legends made a name for themselves as the exception to the rule, such as Vincent Enyeama, Hans-Jorg Butt, Jose Luis Chilavert, Rene Higuita and Rogerio Ceni.



Koeman Sr has also made a name for himself as manager working for the likes of Ajax, PSV, Feyenoord, Southampton, Everton, Barcelona and the Netherlands.

Sports.title: Liverpool hero Georginio Wijnaldum set to join new club on free transfer just days after being tipped for Chelsea move
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL hero Georginio Wijnaldum is reportedly set to join Saudi Arabian giants Al-Ittihad on a free transfer.

The former Reds midfielder, 35, is understood to have agreed a one-year deal with the option of a further 12 months.



Ben Jacobs claims Wijnaldum is already undergoing his medical ahead of completing the switch.

The Dutchman has been available for nothing after leaving fellow Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq at the end of last season.



But his expected move to Al-Ittihad comes just days after he was tipped for a shock return to the Premier League with Chelsea.

Reports claimed the Blues had made contact over a possible short-term deal after Xabi Alonso was left short of options in midfield.

Chelsea sold Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125million before seeing a deadline-day move for Monaco ace Lamine Camara collapse.

That led to Wijnaldum emerging as a possible solution, with his huge amount of Premier League experience making him an attractive option.

The midfielder spent five years at Liverpool after joining from Newcastle in 2016, making 237 appearances and scoring 22 goals.

He became a key man under Jurgen Klopp and won the Premier League, Champions League, Club World Cup and Uefa Super Cup during a trophy-laden spell at Anfield.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Wijnaldum later joined Paris Saint-Germain before spending time on loan at Roma and then moving to Al-Ettifaq in 2023, where he enjoyed three seasons in Saudi Arabia.

And after scoring 17 times in 34 league appearances last term, Wijnaldum now looks set to remain in the Middle East with Al-Ittihad – ending any immediate hopes of a surprise Chelsea switch.

Sports.title: Three points from Man Utd’s draw at Everton with Michael Carrick putting himself in the firing line again
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have given their fans more food for thought with an eventful 2-2 draw at Everton.

The lead they took via Benjamin Sesko‘s 88th-minute header was wiped out deep into stoppage time by Ainsley Maitland-Niles‘ long-range stunner.



And that has left the Red Devils with just four points from their first three Premier League matches this term – all of which they went into as overwhelming favourites.

SunSport’s Samuel Luckhurst offers up his three talking points from Hill Dickinson Stadium…



TELL IT LIKE IT IS

Michael Carrick says United have not had a bad start, but he’s wrong.

When a United manager comes out with stuff like that, it is just going to wind up supporters.



Going forward, he needs to look after himself a little bit more and be a bit more critical of the team.

It’s just not going to chime with fans. He sounds a bit too compliant, like Ole Gunnar Solskjaer did during his tenure, and that didn’t really get him anywhere.



WATCH YOUR BACK

Defensively, United are in a state of disarray after conceding six goals in their first three games.

There is no defensive midfielder in that team at the moment because it took so long to sign Carlos Baleba, so there is no shield for the back-four.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But you look at the full-backs – Luke Shaw and Diogo Dalot first started together eight years ago – so there is possibly some backwards thinking there.

Harry Maguire looked a little bit leggy. He has never been the quickest, but at 33 he is only going to get slower.

Lisandro Martinez is not particularly quick either.



United look so open and gettable. Everton had twice as many attempts on target, so if they were a bit more clinical, maybe they’d have had an even better day.

LAM TO THE SLAUGHTER

Senne Lammens probably had his worst game for United.

He dropped a pretty straightforward cross in the first half, punched away a catchable effort, and was culpable for Tyrique George‘s goal.



His handling was far too feeble at his near post. For his sake, he has to hope that is just an aberration.

But going forward, Lammens, the state of the United defence, it is lacking.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Yes, they are probably going to address it next year.

But even when Carrick was asked about that, he said it was not guaranteed, which is also just going to wind up supporters.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta hails Arsenal evolution as Gunners boss pinpoints change from last season
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta hails Arsenal evolution as Gunners boss pinpoints change from last season

Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are looking to retain their Premier League title and the Spaniard believes his side have evolved their style following their latest win

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta believes Arsenal's style has evolved from last season

Mikel Arteta hailed an “exceptional” victory over Chelsea - and then insisted reigning champions Arsenal will be even better this season.

‌



Gunners captain Martin Odegaard scored a second half winner as Arsenal turned on the style at the Emirates to maintain their 100 per cent start to the campaign.

‌



It delighted Arteta who says Arsenal are determined to improve on last season and carry on winning more trophies after delivering their first title in 22 years.

‌



Arsenal boss Arteta said: “I think it's an indication for us of how capable we are to perform at an even higher level than last season, and it depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire, that humbleness and continue every day to try to find a better version of myself and the team.

“We still have a lot to grow and a lot to offer, and this is the ambition of the team. We know every week it's going to be like this, but that's what we prepare for.

“It was a joy to watch our team play, compete, some huge individual performances as well and the atmosphere in the stadium was great to witness. We demand another layer of dynamism, threat and aggression and you have seen that today.”

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho already 'disinterested' as ex-Man Utd star sets alarm bells ringing
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho already 'disinterested' as ex-Man Utd star sets alarm bells ringing

Alejandro Garnacho has been torn apart by former Liverpool left-back Stephen Warnock after struggling during Aston Villa's goalless draw at Hull City

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho in action for Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Former Manchester United and Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho has been told he looked "completely disinterested" on his third appearance for Aston Villa.

‌



The 22-year-old, who joined the Villans on loan with a conditional obligation to buy from Chelsea earlier this summer, came on as a second-half substitute during his side's 0-0 draw against Hull City on Saturday. The Argentine came on for Emiliano Buendia in the 75th minute as Unai Emery's men searched for their first win of the season.

‌



But Garnacho struggled when he was introduced and failed to make an impact. Indeed, he didn't have a single shot, create a chance, complete a cross and made just nine passes during 15 minutes plus stoppage-time.

‌



With Garnacho having a difficult cameo, ex-Villa and Liverpool left-back Stephen Warnock tore into the winger for his performance and believes he - and Tammy Abraham - did nothing when they came on the pitch. Abraham was brought on in the 85th minute by Emery with Nicolas Jackson coming off.

Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low READ MORE :

Michael Carrick points finger at Man Utd stars after late Everton draw READ MORE :

Speaking on co-commentary, Warnock said: "You may as well take off Alejandro Garnacho and Tammy Abraham. They have done nothing since they have come on the pitch. Garnacho going down. He looks completely disinterested. Unai Emery will be furious with his changes."

Garnacho exited United last summer after making 144 first-team appearances for the Reds, scoring 26 goals. He moved to Chelsea for £40million, though he endured a miserable debut season in west London.

‌



This prompted the Blues to sanction his exit, with Villa snapping him up in July. Since then, Garnacho has appeared in Villa's opening three Premier League fixtures this term, but has been kept of the side by teenager George Hemmings, who has been a standout performer for the Villans.

View 2 Images Garnacho has yet to start for Aston Villa this season (Image: Getty Images)

When asked about how Hemmings has cemented that position, Emery admitted after the Hull match that Hemmings is already operating at Premier League standard, while Garnacho still requires development.

‌



"George, he worked last year the whole year with us and played minutes," Emery said. "He is performing fantastic and getting better. He created one assist for Buendia. He is working in the intensity and kilometres we need. He is doing it. I think he is a player now, clearly, to be in the Premier League.

"Then, we have other players who joined who need to adapt to us in training, playing matches, and Garnacho is in this way. We need their performance to try to add things, working and getting numbers. Garnacho is in this way. How he is responding, George, is really fantastic."

Sports.title: Arsenal come from behind to beat Chelsea and lay down early title marker - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Arsenal come from behind to beat Chelsea and lay down early title marker - 5 talking points

ARSENAL 2-1 CHELSEA: Martin Odegaard scored the winner as the Premier League champions recovered from an early Morgan Rogers goal to pick up the three points

View 4 Images Martin Odegaard was Arsenal's matchwinner as they made it three wins from three

Arsenal recovered from going behind early on as they overcame their toughest challenge of the season to down London rivals Chelsea at the Emirates.

‌



Summer target Morgan Rogers opened the scoring inside two minutes as Xabi Alonso's side continued their habit of starting fast but, after seeing a set piece goal disallowed by VAR, Kai Havertz had the champions back level against the side he once scored for in a Champions League final.

‌



Martin Odegaard's fine start to the season continued as he fired home, what proved to be the winning goal, five minutes after the restart as Mikel Arteta's side remained perfect on nine points - keeping them level with Manchester City as the only teams with 100 percent records.

‌



Rogers' opening goal came after just 77 seconds as the Chelsea playmaker fired in a volley that trickled, rather than flew, past David Raya into the bottom corner to stun the Emirates crowd.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The champions thought they were level after just 11 minutes when another set piece looked to have struck gold. A Declan Rice ball into the box was stopped initially before it was bundled in by Riccardo Calafiori, but VAR ended the celebrations when Ezri Konsa was pinned for being offside.

‌



Chelsea have been tipped as outsiders to challenge Arsenal and in a pulsating first-half the Blues suggested they have it in them to go with their London rivals. They though were undone by their former player in Havertz, who cut inside to fire home the equaliser.

The German was key in Arsenal's second, dummying a Christos Tzolis cross to leave Odegaard one-on-one with the goalkeeper before thumping home as his stellar start to the season continued. Estevao came closest to firing in Chelsea's equaliser as he cut in from the right, forcing a stellar save from Raya.

Here's five talking points from the capital.

‌



London stays red

The early season optimism surrounding Chelsea may not have been lost on Arsenal, who have shown themselves to be London's dominant force once again. Every so often its good for those on top of the mountain to send a reminder than they remain the benchmark.

View 4 Images Kai Havertz scored Arsenal's equaliser against his former side

Arsenal did exactly that on Sunday against a Blues team that will firmly believe - and look to be - upwardly mobile. Despite their earlu lead they couldn't hold on against a Gunners team that won't have had to come from behind too often, but showed they're more than capable.

‌



It had to be Rogers

It was written in the stars that he would rock up in the Emirates, wearing blue, and silence the crowd. Few would've expected his impact on the game to come so soon but Rogers continued his bright start to life at Chelsea, no doubt leaving some questioning Arsenal's decision to bypass signing him.

Ultimately Chelsea won the race for his signature because the Gunners refused to veer from their valuation of the playmaker. Time will tell as to whether their decision was a shrewd or a stubborn one, but those in charge of the Chelsea recruitment, and Rogers himself, will have taken great satisfaction from seeing his 20-yard effort trickle in.

View 4 Images Morgan Rogers had given Chelsea an early lead

‌



Odegaard central again

There genuinely were those during the summer who questioned whether Odegaard's time at the Emirates should be considered such was the decline in his role. Once the central point of the Arsenal attack, injuries and constant new arrivals had seen other team-mates become major players in the final third.

The Norwegian wasn't always available last term, but when he was his starting berth wasn't guaranteed. This season Odegaard looks like a man determined to prove he should never have been doubted. Not only is he as influential as ever, he's scoring with regularity, and looks back to his effortless best.

Chelsea in the hunt - but not there yet

In a world where Arsenal have been semi-anointed by some as champions such is their continuity and the upheaval of their rivals, Chelsea have shown that their new era may not need years to come alive.

‌



View 4 Images Mikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso have an association that goes back decades

Of the traditional top six, five have managers taking charge of their team for a full season for the first time. Of all those new managers Alonso has more pedigree than any - and its not as if Chelsea have been shy when it comes to spending money in recent years. Put those things together and the Blues could well prove to be Arsenal's closest challengers. Sunday's clash was their litmus test and their performance suggested they could be a problem for Arteta and co, even if they still have another level to find as things stand.

Fast starters

The Alonso-era got underway at Fulham a fortnight ago with a goal inside 32 seconds thanks to Joao Pedro, and that fast start has become a habit for the Blues, who have been quick to take the lead against Brighton and Arsenal since then.

Article continues below

Rogers' goal at the Emirates meant that Chelsea became the first side in Premier League history to score inside five minutes in each of their first three games. The Blues haven't shown themselves to have the sternest of defences this year, but they're showing they're always good for a goal, and the first goal in any game is a huge boost.

Sports.title: Gary Neville issues on-air apology as VAR statement released on Arsenal goal vs Chelsea
Sports.content:
Gary Neville issues on-air apology as VAR statement released on Arsenal goal vs Chelsea

Arsenal saw a goal ruled out in the cruellest fashion during their Premier League clash with Chelsea on Sunday, with Gary Neville apologising to VAR in the aftermath

View 2 Images Arsenal had a goal ruled out against Chelsea on Sunday (Image: Getty Images)

Gary Neville apologised to VAR and Pro Ref as Arsenal saw a goal chalked off against Chelsea for offside on Sunday afternoon. The Gunners found themselves a goal down at the Emirates Stadium through a Morgan Rogers wonderstrike just two minutes into the Premier League match.

‌



However, Mikel Arteta's men were quick to put the pressure on their London rivals as they launched wave after wave of attack on Chelsea's area. Riccardo Calafiori thought he had levelled matters around 10 minutes after Rogers' opener, tapping home from close range after a frantic scrum in Emiliano Martinez's area.

‌



Declan Rice provided a mid-height cross from the edge of Chelsea's box from a free-kick, Joao Pedro hashing a routine clearance as the ball bundled to Gabriel at the back post. While Martinez made the initial save, Ezri Konsa rattled the upright on the follow-up, with Calafiori latching onto the loose ball and firing from close range.

‌



Celebrations in North London were short-lived, however, as a result of Konsa being in an offside position in the build-up, with VAR quickly ruling out the goal. Speaking on Sky Sports' coverage of the game, Neville was quick to criticise the decision, in the belief that officials had made a mistake.

He said: "He is going to disallow it...all hell's going to break loose. I disagree with it. There's no doubt that he's [Konsa] in an offside position, but for me, Emi Martinez has a clear chance to save it.

"I don't think he's interfering with him. If he did [get a touch on it] that would bring him into play."

‌



As replays showed, Neville added: "So there now, there's no interference there and Konsa is offside at that point," before spotting his own error, prompting an apology from the pundit.

View 2 Images Arsenal saw an equalising goal disallowed

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



He added: "Oh, he touches it. Correction. Apologies to VAR and the PGMOL."

With the PGMOL no longer going by that name, Peter Drury was quick to correct his broadcasting partner for the afternoon. He explained: "Pro Ref now, Gary," as Neville added: "Absolutely. Pro Ref is it? Oh right, okay. Excellent."

Arsenal, however, did manage to equalise 25 minutes into the match through former Chelsea man, Kai Havertz.

Article continues below

The versatile forward picked the ball up on the right-hand side of the box, before cutting in on his left and curling low past an outstretched Martinez at his near post.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick points finger at Man Utd stars after late Everton draw
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick points finger at Man Utd stars after late Everton draw

Manchester United thought they were on the way to back-to-back victories at Everton only for a late Ainsley Maitland-Niles goal to steal a point for the home side late on

View 2 Images Michael Carrick saw his Man United side drop points late on at Everton (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has claimed that poor decision making from his players contributed to Sunday's late draw with Everton.

‌



The Red Devils thought they were heading for back-to-back wins at Hill Dickinson Stadium after a dramatic match. Bryan Mbeumo had given United the lead, only for Tyrique George to level matters late on.

‌



Benjamin Sesko's header seemingly snatched victory for the Red Devils. But there was still time for Ainsley Maitland-Niles to crash home a stunner right at the end of stoppage time.

‌



The draw leaves Carrick's side with just one win from their opening three league games of the campaign after a summer in which they spent around £150m.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

In assessing his side's display, Carrick said some wrong decisions from his players made the game more difficult than it needed to be.

‌



Speaking to NBC, the United boss said: “There was a lot of good things in the game for us. We played some really good football, were dangerous at times.

"For the most part we defended well as a team. The longer the game went on there were a few more balls into the box and a few decisions we made it more difficult for us when we should’ve seen it out really. We’re disappointed we didn’t come away with a win.”

View 2 Images Man United were forced to settle for a late point at Everton (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Asked specifically what those mistakes were, Carrick was slightly more guarded. He replied: “I’ll keep them to myself a little bit but we should’ve seen the game out really so we’re disappointed with that.”

Carrick added: “There were two great strikes to be fair. We didn’t give them real clear chances. We defended well. They had a few bits that dropped around the edge of the box. We defended the box pretty well for the most part. We look to the reasons how they ended up getting those opportunities but those were really good strikes.

“There was a lot of good things. Especialy early on in the game and probably towards the end not so much. We looked dangerous. I thought we called a lot of problems. They got really good goals for different reasons and our second one should’ve been a winner.”

Article continues below

United are back in action at Old Trafford on Thursday as they host Azerbaijani side Sabah in their Champions League opener. Their next Premier League game pits them against rivals Manchester City at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish makes 'nightmare' claim after completing Man City exit
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish makes 'nightmare' claim after completing Man City exit

Jack Grealish has reunited with David Moyes after heading to Everton for a second straight season as the Manchester City outcast seeks to resurrect his career

View 2 Images Jack Grealish has talked up his relationship with David Moyes

Jack Grealish has confessed that David Moyes will probably see him as "a nightmare" after his second return to Everton on loan.

‌



The playmaker spent last season at the Toffees and had proved influential in the final third until injury curtailed his season. The Manchester City star headed back to the Etihad in the summer, but it quickly became apparent that he was set for a peripheral role.

‌



Grealish had been gradually cast aside by Pep Guardiola, who once spent £100million to sign him, and even after the Catalan left City and Enzo Maresca was hired the 30-year-old was set to remain on the outer.

‌



Everton returned to land him for a second time ahead of his contract expiring next summer and it will leave Moyes again looking to get the most from Grealish. The England international admits the pair have a great relationship - and that helps get the best out of him.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Speaking to Sky Sports he said on the Everton boss: "I get on really well with him. He’d probably tell you, sometimes he’d probably say: ‘Jack’s a nightmare,’ but we have this really good connection.

‌



"And like I was saying to you off camera, when I get on really well with a manager, it makes you want to do more for them. It makes you want to give everything for them, play well and succeed for them. And that’s what I want to do. I know a lot of the players are like that with him here.

"When I look back to managers that I’ve played my best football under, I always had a special connection with them as well. Three of my managers, Tim Sherwood, Steve Bruce and Dean Smith, I always speak to all of them now on text. I played such good football under all of them and I feel like that with the manager here as well."

View 2 Images Jack Grealish's days at Man City could be over (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Last season Grealish scored twice for Everton and was of interest to several clubs, including former side Aston Villa and Sunderland, before opting for a return to Merseyside.

Moyes and the Toffees endured a hectic end to their summer - winger Iliman Ndiaye made a £65m switch to City but Everton failed to add the striker they'd be eyeing despite being close to a £40m deal for Monaco and USA forward Folarin Balogun. They also failed with a bid to re-sign Brazil striker Richarlison from Tottenham.

Grealish came off the bench and had an impact as Everton came from behind to draw 2-2 with Manchester United on Sunday.

Sports.title: FIFA boss Gianni Infantino to stand for re-election despite failed coup and calls to leave
Sports.content:
FIFA boss Gianni Infantino to stand for re-election despite failed coup and calls to leave

Gianni Infantino has been under the cosh after his World Cup sale attempts but despite calls for the FIFA president to go, he's look to remain in his post

View 2 Images Despite calls to stand down, Gianni Infantino is looking to remain as FIFA boss (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election as FIFA president even after the World Cup scandal. Infantino has been under intense pressure to quit after his scrapped plan to sell stakes in the World Cup caused a massive backlash.

‌



UEFA have called on him to stand down and other nations across the world are also applying pressure on Infantino before the next round of elections in March.

‌



FIFA president Infantino said in April that he would stand again for re-election in 2027 - and that has been reiterated by world football’s governing body.

‌



FIFA said in a statement: “The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027,” read a Fifa statement. Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

That will not please UEFA and their member associations like the English FA who were hoping that Infantino would quit and a new candidate would step forward.

‌



Infantino’s position has even come under pressure internally after the plans were revealed to sell stakes which caused a high backlash. Infantino is in Poland for the women’s under-20s World Cup and was carrying on as business as usual this weekend.

On Saturday, Infantino arrived in Katowice and said on Sky: “There will be a lot to say" but "it's not today.”

View 2 Images UEFA have put huge pressure on the FIFA boss to stand down (Image: Masashi Hara, Getty Images)

‌



It is the first time Fifa has said he will run for a fourth term since the aborted sell-off plan was announced following the summer's World Cup. FIFA rules say a president can serve a maximum of four terms and if he is successful then he will serve until 2031. The deadline for candidates to lodge their nominations is on November 18.

FIFA this week accused UEFA of a “smear campaign against it and its leadership”, in a challenge to litigation over Infantino's plan.

Last week UEFA filed legal papers in the US requesting disclosure of evidence and documents from Fifa, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Raaheeb aims to resume progression at Windsor
Sports.content:
The Shadwell-owned Raaheeb returns to the racetrack on Monday afternoon, live on Sky Sports Racing.

4.15 Windsor - Classy Raaheeb aims to resume his progression

The classy Raaheeb aims to resume his progression in the Weatherbys Global Stallions App Winter Hill Stakes.

A brother to top class performers Baaeed and Hukum, Raaheeb began his career perfectly with a nice success at two, before taking the Classic Trial at Sandown in terrific fashion. He then ran creditably when fourth in the Irish Derby, travelling up like a genuine challenger before tiring late under Rossa Ryan.

The time given to help Raaheeb develop physically and mentally could set him up for a nice return to the track and he should be tough to beat in calmer waters, even under a penalty.

Venetian Prince goes for the in-form Andrew Balding yard, having won the Italian Derby in June. However, Jason Watson's mount will have to put a Royal Ascot no-show behind him, when he was outpaced over three furlongs out in the King Edward VII Stakes.

Conversely, Maho Bay ran creditably at the Royal meeting and connections could have considered themselves unlucky to have ran into trouble in the home straight. He remains unexposed and can provide the biggest threat for a yard going well.

Crest Of Fire and Harmonics have been progressing through handicaps but would need to take a significant step forward to win up in grade.

4.00 Newton Abbot - Improving duo Arctic Voyage and Edelak feature in cagey affair

The improving duo of Arctic Voyage and Edelak feature in a cagey Par Inn Handicap Hurdle.

Edelak resumed winning ways at Stratford in July after falling on his penultimate start when a likely winner. He has now won four of his last five - and doing so rather easily - with a small break after a busy period likely to see him put in a career best.

However, the opposition is tough with Arctic Voyage taking very well to hurdling since switching to the Michael Blake yard. He has won three of his last four and looked particularly good last time out when scoring with a fair bit in hand.

Although on a fair mark and back over hurdles, War Correspondent has not had the best preparation coming into this with two poor runs over fences, so Ellerton is the main threat to the former two with an encouraging win back over hurdles on his CV after a breathing operation.

6.30 Wolverhampton - Progressive filly Brunhilde steps up in trip

Progressive filly Brunhilde steps up in trip in the Follow @attheraces On Instagram Handicap.

George Boughey's filly has progressed with each run since making her debut in May and connections' patience was rewarded when she won by over five lengths at Lingfield when last seen. She is stoutly bred, being closely related to Godolphin's listed winner Ghostwatch, so the step up to one-mile and six furlongs should yield more improvement.

Last Verse won very nicely at Lingfield on his last start and remains relatively unexposed and on the right side of the handicap.

Level Look should be able to progress from his promising Chester second place after being at a disadvantage when too far back at the Shergar Cup last month.

Robusto won last time and can be competitive, albeit his higher all-weather mark means he has less scope in his mark than his more unexposed rivals.

Sports.title: The NFL is back! The race to Super Bowl 61 starts here
Sports.content:
285 games. Eight countries. Four continents. Six time zones. 22 weeks. 32 teams. One champion. And five gold rings - oops, sorry Jayden Daniels. The 2026 NFL season is here.

Seven months ago, discarded embers of confetti would pave the way for our meandering walk towards the exit at an emptying Levi's Stadium as the curtain closed on Super Bowl 60, footballing disciples reluctant to accept it was all over for another year as they braced for annual hibernation.

Sam Darnold had just crowned one of sport's great fairy-tale redemption stories, Aden Durde had just made British sporting history, Mike Macdonald's Dark Side defense had just tormented Drake Maye and Bad Bunny had just delivered a clinic in reggaeton rage-bait in the face of orange-tinged white-housed backlash over his landmark half-time show.

Seattle Seahawks players and coaches alike rejoiced over childhood dreams fulfilled in the company of loved ones, while for others the clock had already reset, for football rarely dwells too long on the present.

The countdown is finally over. From here on, there shall be no more football-less Sundays until February. The road to Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles starts here.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Super Bowl 60 as the Seattle Seahawks took on the New England Patriots in California

2025 NFL Honours MVP: Matthew Stafford, QB, Los Angeles Rams

Offensive Player of the Year: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks

Defensive Player of the Year: Myles Garrett, DE, Cleveland Browns

Comeback Player of the Year: Christian McCaffrey, RB, San Francisco 49ers

Coach of the Year: Mike Vrabel, New England Patriots

Rookie of the Year: Tyler Shough, QB, New Orleans Saints

A lot can happen in seven months, it turns out.

Odell Beckham Jr is back wearing No 13 for the New York Giants again after re-signing with the team that first drafted him 12 years ago. Mike McCarthy is back working with Aaron Rodgers again after succeeding Mike Tomlin as the new Pittsburgh Steelers head coach ahead of the four-time MVP's final season. Geno Smith is back with the New York Jets 13 years after the team drafted him. And Aaron Donald is back with the Los Angeles Rams after coming out of retirement at the age of 35 to team up with Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett in haunting offensive linemen across the league. The last time I checked, we hadn't gone back in time.

Garrett himself reigned as the most seismic mover of the offseason as he was traded by the Cleveland Browns to the Rams in a deal that saw Jared Verse head the opposite way. He is the greatest pass rusher of his generation; he is coming off a campaign in which he broke the all-time single-season sack record, and he is now credited for Sean McVay's side - led by MVP Matthew Stafford - entering as Super Bowl frontrunners. Cleveland relieving Garrett of any further pain was perhaps to be admired, before the Browns did what the Browns do best and set the franchise back even further by naming Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback. Some things don't change.

What else? Well, Adam Sandler officiated the wedding of the year between Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift at Madison Square Garden. New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel became embroiled in a textbook soap opera scandal involving NFL reporter Diana Russini following photos of the pair at an Arizona resort. A man named Daejon Love was arrested for allegedly pretending to be a San Francisco 49ers wide receiver in order to defraud at least 26 women of more than $1m. And on the topic of the 49ers, owner Jed York was arrested in a prostitution sting. If you are new to us, welcome to the NFL.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Seattle's defensive coordinator Aden Durde was in a buoyant mood after he became the first British coach to win a Super Bowl

Giants running back Cam Skattebo almost injured himself by trying and failing to land a backflip at Fanatics Fest, because of course he did. And elsewhere Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels prompted a wave of social media ridicule having sent LSU a cease-and-desist letter instructing his former college to stop using his name, image and likeness after giving the No 5 jersey, previously worn by Daniels, to sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett; Five Guys became Four Guys, while Adam Levine kindly renamed his band (disclaimer: neither really happened).

Word also has it there were still Fantasy Football owners drafting Kyle Pitts as their starting tight end, which might be as clear an indication as any that we are back; for what it's worth, this writer remains a Pitts believer, whether rightly or wrongly. Houston Texans pass rusher Will Anderson Jr, Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter, Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs and Seahawks corner Devon Witherspoon all also signed new contracts to become the highest-paid players in their respective positions in NFL history, Anderson the highest-paid non-quarterback ever with an average annual salary of $50m. Perhaps Mr Daejon Love was pretending to play the wrong position.

Most Super Bowl victories Team Wins Appearances Boston/New England Patriots 6 12 Pittsburgh Steelers 6 8 San Francisco 49ers 5 8 Dallas Cowboys 5 8 Kansas City Chiefs 4 7 Green Bay Packers 4 5 New York Giants 4 5 Denver Broncos 3 8 Oakland/Los Angeles/Las Vegas Raiders 3 5 Washington Redskins/Football Team/Commanders 3 5

Maxx Crosby almost became a Baltimore Raven but didn't become a Baltimore Raven, instead remaining in Las Vegas after a bizarre turn of events to greet No 1 pick quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who will begin his rookie campaign with the Raiders as backup to long-lost brother Kirk Cousins. There Klint Kubiak takes the reins as one of 10 new head coaches across the league, a reward for his role in orchestrating Seattle's Super Bowl-winning offense alongside Darnold last season.

Mass change along NFL sidelines meanwhile saw Joe Brady replace Sean McDermott as Buffalo Bills head coach and Jesse Minter replace John Harbaugh as the new Ravens head coach, as much amplifying the lasting impact of Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs' recent monopoly on the AFC as Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson's agonising Super Bowl wait drags on.

Following 18 seasons in Baltimore, Harbaugh subsequently landed with the Giants in view of a new era behind Jaxson Dart, Malik Nabers and a star-studded pass rush. Previously the mastermind of a shape-shifting Green Bay Packers defense, Jeff Hafley was another of the high-profile hires as he took his talents to Miami to head up a Dolphins rebuild that includes British representation via London's own Seydou Traore, who became the first player to have attended the UK's NFL Academy and later be drafted.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment the Las Vegas Raiders selected quarterback Fernando Mendoza as first pick at the 2026 NFL Draft and the player's reaction

Sticking to the globe-trotting theme, the league itself will be on the move more than ever and further than ever as the NFL stages a record nine regular-season games outside of the United States. A historic slate features maiden trips to Melbourne in Australia, Rio de Janeiro in Brazil and French capital Paris, while returning to Mexico City, Munich and Madrid alongside three more games in London.

It begins down under during kickoff week when the 49ers and Rams face off at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground on Thursday night. Before then the defending champion Seahawks open the 2026 campaign against the Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch on Wednesday, another first for the league.

Last season proved as wide-open as ever, culminating in the most unlikely Super Bowl in history, based on preseason odds. There is reason to believe that narrative resumes.

Patrick Mahomes returns following surgery on last December's season-ending knee injury, determined to inspire a Chiefs revival after Andy Reid's side missed out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014. Awaiting him is running back Kenneth Walker as his newest backfield partner after the Chiefs dipped into their pockets to sign the Super Bowl MVP to a three-year, $45m deal in free agency.

Sure last year became an ugly struggle, but, like it or not, Mahomes remains the story of the AFC having for so long been the unbudgeable Super Bowl gateway for Allen, Jackson, Joe Burrow and many more. On more than one occasion it has been Allen's 'time' and Jackson's 'time', until it wasn't, while Burrow has been fairly adamant in the offseason that this 'is' the time.

It is a season brimming with question marks.

Are Bo Nix, Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos the true class of the AFC? Are the Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams-led Chicago Bears true contenders? How will Drake Maye respond to his Super Bowl nightmare? Was the Daniel Jones comeback story real? Can the 49ers finally stay healthy to re-enter contention? What will the Jacksonville Jaguars do with Travis Hunter? How much will the Philadelphia Eagles miss AJ Brown? Is Tyler Shough the long-awaited answer at quarterback for the New Orleans Saints? Can this Rams super-team work?

Time to get some answers.

Sports.title: 'I'm back with a bang' - Littler topples Humphries to take glory in Prague
Sports.content:
Luke Littler beat rival Luke Humphries to win on his return to the European Tour at the Czech Darts Open in Prague.

Littler had not played in a European Tour event since March, but roared to glory with an 8-6 victory in Sunday night's final to end his opponent's hopes of winning this title for a third straight year.

Littler hit five 180s and averaged just over 95 as both players struggled in the heat at the PVA EXPO after a long day which had already seen The Nuke overcome Michael van Gerwen in the semi-finals, Danny Noppert in the quarter-finals and Krzysztof Ratajski in the last 16.

"It's good to be back and I'm back with a bang," said Littler after his victory.

World No 1 Littler won the first two legs against world No 2 Humphries in Sunday's final, only to see his rival, who has reached four of the last five finals in this tournament, reel off three straight legs to take the lead.

Littler fought back to move ahead with a 130 checkout in the ninth leg - the biggest finish of the game - and then won the next two legs to move 7-4 ahead in a race to eight.

Humphries rallied to win the next two legs and was millimetres away from sending the game to a decider, as he wired two darts at D16.

Littler recovered to pin D10 to win this tournament for the first time, taking home the £35,000 first prize and guaranteeing his place at the European Championship in Dortmund in October.

That's one of the titles that Littler wants to win as he eyes a clean sweep of major trophies in 2026 - and it means he's unlikely to play in any other regular European Tour events this season.

Image: Luke Littler celebrates at the Czech Darts Open (Pic: Sebastian Doppstadt/PDC Europe)

"I'm not sure now I've won this one," he explained. "I think I've secured my place in Dortmund. That's obviously the one I'm chasing.

"In two weeks time it's the World Series in Amsterdam. We'll have to see what happens, what the plan is and how busy I am."

Humphries had overcome Gerwyn Price, William O'Connor and Andrew Gilding earlier on Sunday to reach the final for the third year in a row, but he was not upset at missing out on a 'three-peat'.

"I can't be upset," he said. "The two darts I threw at D16 were right on the wire and if that goes in, it could have been a different game.

"That's just the way it goes. He's a fantastic player. I've been playing here and there, not so great. Maybe good sometimes. I've got to dedicate my life a bit more to get better and keep pushing him.

"I keep saying I'm not beating him in finals so I've got to change things to keep matching him.

"I think he enjoys the challenge and I love it as well. Hopefully over the next four months, I push him and if he does the clean sweep [of major titles] he has to do it the hard way."

Sports.title: Great Britain and Ireland claim historic win in Walker Cup thriller
Sports.content:
Great Britain and Ireland won the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015 after a nerve-shredding late comeback saw them beat the USA by a 13½-12½ scoreline.

Dean Robertson's side looked to be heading for defeat at Lahinch after suffering a clean sweep of defeats in the Sunday morning foursomes and with the Americans three points ahead going into the singles matches.

But the home side lost only two of the 10 matches and the competition eventually came down to the very last as Josh Hill won the 18th hole of his match with Tyler Watts to seal an incredible victory.

The USA will be left to regret the late turnaround after four missed putts to retain the Walker Cup.

Team GB&I needed a quick start to produce any sort of comeback and they delivered after Stuart Grehan, Luke Poulter - son of former Ryder Cup star Ian - Jack Whaley and Tyler Weaver all won their matches.

However, the Americans steadied the ship after securing halves through Miles Russell and Kihei Akina and wins courtesy of Ryder Cowan and Josiah Gilbert as it looked like they had thwarted the comeback.

As it looked like the Americans were about to take a firm grip on yet another win, Team GB&I responded once again. Eliot Baker overcame Stewart Hagestad on the final hole to ensure the Walker Cup would be determined on the final hole.

Hill and Tyler Watts were all square coming down the last at County Clare and Hill produced a stunning up-and-down from the bunker to complete a thrilling comeback and seal the unlikeliest of wins.

Image: Great Britain and Ireland celebrate after winning the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015

Speaking after securing the decisive point, Hill said: "This is absolutely unbelievable. It doesn't get better than this."

Captain Robertson added: "We are so elated. We're hardly able to put it into words. There's a lot of emotion, a lot of happy tears. But pride is the word I would use to describe this.

"There was most definitely a belief in the players and even though we were swept 4-0 this morning, there wasn't a despondency.

"The boys have delivered and I am incredibly proud of each and every one of them."

The victory by GB&I ends the streak of five victories in the Walker Cup by the USA and is their 10th win overall.

USA captain Nathan Smith refused to criticise his players, saying: "The match was incredible. It was definitely a tale of two days with what happened this morning and going forward now and how they played this afternoon.

"We knew how great their team was. They're a great team. They're a deep team. We knew they were capable of anything. Really at no time did we take the foot off the accelerator.

"All you can do is really tip your cap to them. They played great."

The morning session saw GB&I lose all the momentum they'd claimed on Sunday as the USA comprehensively won all four matches to move into a three-point lead.

Home captain Robertson stuck with his pairings from Saturday, but his players struggled to perform and failed to take the lead in any of the four matches.

The demise started as Grehan and Baker were beaten 3&2 in the opening match of the day by Stout and Fang.
