Sports.title: ‘Exceptional performance’: Arteta hails fightback win and says best yet to come
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after the Premier League champions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea on Sunday.

Arteta’s side were under pressure after conceding for the first time this season when Morgan Rogers struck early at the Emirates Stadium, but the response to the setback was outstanding. Kai Havertz equalised before conjuring a brilliant dummy for a rejuvenated Martin Ødegaard to make it 2-1, ensuring that Arsenal moved level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.

“It was an exceptional performance,” Arteta said. “I enjoyed every minute from beginning to end, and the beginning was tough. But the team responded in a spectacular way – the conviction, the determination, the quality. It was beautiful. It was a fascinating game.

“I think it’s an indication for us of how we are capable of ­performing at an even higher level than last ­season. It depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire, that humbleness, and continue every day to try to find a better version of myself and the team. We still have a lot to grow and a lot to offer. This is the ambition of the team.”

Arsenal and City are the only sides who have won their first three games, a statistic Arteta took as evidence that the league will be even harder this time. “It is going to be super hard, the margins you win games,” he said.

“We went to Villa Park a few days ago and it was really tough. Today again. We’ll go to Sunderland and it’ll again be so, so tough. We know every week is going to be like this but that’s what we prepare for.”

Arteta was delighted with an exceptional midfield display from Ødegaard. Arsenal’s captain looks fit after two years of injury problems and has started the campaign with three goals in four games.

“He feels, confidence-wise, I think one of the highest that I’ve seen him,” Arteta said of the Norwegian. “He has a point to prove from last season as well, missing so much football. Kai is the same. I don’t know how many times they played together in the last three years but probably not much. He is enjoying his football. He was running ­forward, having shots, creating for his teammates.”

Arteta, who hopes Cristhian ­Mosquera will make a swift recovery from a muscle problem, was similarly positive about Havertz after the ­German impressed against his old club. “He looks settled, he looks happy, in his personal life some great things have happened,” he said. “He looks fit, he looks happy and he is scoring goals.”

View image in fullscreen Kai Havertz (right) celebrates scoring Arsenal’s first goal with Christos Tzolis and Gabriel. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

While Arsenal celebrated, ­Chelsea reflected on coming up short. The Blues were exciting in attack but defensive shortcomings led to their first defeat under Xabi Alonso, whose new team have conceded seven in their first three league games.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“My priority is to win games and it’s easier when you don’t concede many,” Alonso said. “This is something that we need to address. We want to be tighter, to be more clinical, more balanced. But this takes time.

“We wanted to compete, we came to win. We were not that far, but it went their way. We could have scored to make it 2-1 and you never know what happens. But the result is the result, I’m not fighting against that. It hurts. But this is the first defeat, it is going to be a long journey and it doesn’t have a big impact in our mood.”

Chelsea are without a clean sheet in their past 19 league games but Alonso did not want to park the bus. “I want to compete in the best possible way to win,” he said. “Today we didn’t want to sit deep from the first minute and to wait and to make a long game. We wanted to be active, we wanted to be protagonists in the pressing, sometimes to go higher, sometimes lower, to have good possessions. And we have done many right things. We need to make it better.”

Alonso was optimistic that Moisés Caicedo is not enduring a long-term issue after the midfielder missed out with injury. Caicedo is yet to start this season and it is uncertain if he will be back for Chelsea’s Carabao Cup tie against Leeds on Wednesday.

“It’s about assessing the risk,” Alonso said. “Probably last week we took him on too early and I don’t want to make the same mistake again.”

Sports.title: ‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United draw
Sports.content:
David Moyes praised Everton’s resilient response to a troubled week after his side twice came from behind to salvage a point against Manchester United through Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s long-range strike.

The deadline-day signing, who was introduced in the 77th minute after James Garner pulled up with cramp, preserved Everton’s unbeaten start to the season with a 25-yard effort in the 96th minute.

Tyrique George also scored a superb equaliser to lift the mood at Hill Dickinson Stadium after transfer deadline day had left Moyes with a weaker squad and only one striker in Thierno Barry.

The Everton manager insisted it had been easy to keep the negativity away from his players. “It was the exact opposite,” he said of the potential negative impact on his squad.

“I said to the players there would be no excuses from any of us and the players all agreed. The players hugely bought into it. It can hurt you being a player down but it can also have the opposite reaction.

“Sometimes when you have less players it means everybody has to be ready and you have to find a way of making it work. Who knows how it will go? It will be difficult when we have three games a week.”

Sports.title: European football: Lamine Yamal’s double powers Barcelona to rout of Valencia
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal struck twice for Barcelona as they demolished Valencia 5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100% start in La Liga.

The reigning champions moved three points clear at the top of La Liga after Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday. Fermín López, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick’s swaggering visitors on a hot afternoon on Spain’s east coast.

Barcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia’s fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium.

“We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant and this is what I want from the team,” said Flick. “We stay calm and then if it’s possible to score we try to do it – it was a fantastic game for us. Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it’s perfect then you can stop working.”

Lamine Yamal opened the scoring with a clever lofted finish in the sixth minute after Fermín dinked a superb ball over the top for the teenage star. Fermín netted the second with a crisp finish in the 22nd minute after the former Newcastle winger Anthony Gordon teed him up. Barcelona suffered a blow when Eric García had to go off hurt midway through the first half after a collision with teammate Rodri’s shoulder, on the midfielder’s first start since arriving this summer from Manchester City.

Raphinha, starting again as the team’s centre-forward, tapped home his sixth goal of the season from close range after Fermín fed him. The Valencia goalkeeper, Stole Dimitrievski, saved from Rodri before Pedri netted Barcelona’s fourth after an exchange of passes with Dani Olmo. Gabriel Jesus came on for his Barça debut as a substitute in the final 10 minutes and sent a low effort just wide. Lamine Yamal stayed onside to collect another Olmo pass and put away Barça’s fifth.

In Serie A, Ruben Amorim’s Milan were pegged back by a 92nd-minute equaliser from Juventus in a 1-1 draw in Turin on Sunday. Teenage sensation Alphadjo Cisse had given Milan the lead but the Juve centre-back Federico Gatti came off the bench to head home and earn a share of the spoils in stoppage time.

Milan took the lead on 69 minutes ⁠with a superb finish from Cisse, who controlled Samuel Chukwueze’s crossfield pass with a deft touch in the box. The 19-year-old showed quick feet to create space to shoot ⁠and fired the ball low into the far corner, adding to his debut goal away ​at Torino on the opening day. But the visitors could not ‌hold on and when Teun Koopmeiners delivered a cross from the left, Gatti rose highest to score ‌with a powerful header.

View image in fullscreen Juventus’s Federico Gatti takes the acclaim of the Turin crowd after levelling against Milan at the death. Photograph: Marco Alpozzi/LaPresse/AP

The ⁠draw leaves both sides ⁠on seven points ​from their opening three games, with Milan fourth on the table, ahead of fifth-placed Juve on goals scored.

Giorgi Kvernadze scored a winner seven minutes from the end to secure all three points for Frosinone at home to Venezia after the latter had rallied from two goals down but went home with nothing. Bologna twice came from behind to secure a 2-2 draw at home to Sassuolo, a game that ended with the hosts’ head coach Domenico Tedesco receiving a red card. Artem Dovbyk netted his first goal for the ​home side to equalise in stoppage time.

The English 19-year-old Jay Robinson gave Monza a 1-0 lead in the first half at Parma, but 18-year-old Simone Lontani equalised on the hour-mark, with the game finishing 1-1. For both players it was their first Serie A goals, and for both clubs their first point of the campaign. Forward Robinson is on loan at Monza from Southampton.

Meanwhile, Ronald Koeman Jr, the goalkeeper son of the former Netherlands player and manager Ronald Koeman, scored two penalties for Dutch side Telstar to rescue a point in their Eredivisie match with Cambuur. His second spot-kick was converted in the 11th minute of added time.

Koeman Jr, 31, converted his first penalty on 63 minutes before his ice-cool equaliser. He previously scored from the spot at the end of last season to ensure his side avoided relegation from the Dutch top flight.

View image in fullscreen Telstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr is hugged by a teammate after his late penalty rescued a point. Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock

In Germany, Mainz ignited their Bundesliga season with a thumping 5-0 win over hapless Hamburg, while Augsburg climbed ⁠to the top of the table following a 4-1 win at Eintracht Frankfurt on Sunday.

Mainz took the lead on 19 minutes as Sheraldo Becker was played in on goal by ⁠Kaishu Sano and picked out the bottom corner. Becker then turned provider as his low cross was converted at the back post by Phillipp Mwene for ⁠a 2-0 half-time lead.

Becker was again involved with the next goal as he set up ​Phillip Tietz to bundle the ball home. Tietz ‌then added a fourth ‌as he beat Heuer Fernandes, before Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer punished his former employers ‌with a fifth.

Augsburg have a haul of six points following ​their excellent win at Frankfurt, where they had to come from behind, having trailed 1-0 at half-time. Jonathan Burkardt headed the home side in front inside six minutes.

Arijon Ibrahimovic ​headed in at the back post ​on debut inside the first minute of the re-start for the equaliser. Within a minute, ‌Augsburg were 2-1 ahead ​as the ball ​fell to Robin Fellhauer in the box and he converted to turn the game on its head. Alexis Claude-Maurice and Fabian Rieder added further goals

Augsburg lead the Bundesliga on goal difference ahead of Freiburg, Borussia Dortmund and Elversberg, who all have two wins from two.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League: Shaw doubles up to give Manchester City winning start
Sports.content:
Some things just feel inevitable. Some strikers just feel inevitable. Despite a new season, a fresh start and new opponents, it is still the same storyline for Manchester City: Khadija Shaw wins them the game. The Jamaica striker began the campaign exactly how she finished the previous league season, with two goals, and demonstrated why it was so crucial that the club eventually persuaded her to sign a new contract in the summer.

Last season’s Golden Boot winner in the Women’s Super League could have scored at least twice in the first half had it not been for an excellent debut performance from Sophie Baggaley in goal for promoted Birmingham.

Shaw, though, was not to be denied and she rose highest to head in twice from second-half corners, taken first by Kerstin Casparij and then by the debutant Beth Mead, to score her side’s second and third goals in a 3-1 victory. By then, Mary Fowler’s low finish had already opened the scoring with Manchester City’s 1,000th goal as a professional women’s side.

Birmingham grabbed a late consolation goal through Océane Hurtré, who capitalised on a defensive lapse from Jade Rose and rolled the ball home in the 90th minute, and there were plenty of encouraging signs overall for the second-tier champions of last season.

Quick Guide Palace face scrutiny over substitutions Show Crystal Palace could face a points deduction or potentially be forced to replay their game against Everton on Sunday, which Palace won 1-0, after it emerged that the hosts breached the rules around substitutions by making changes at four separate moments in the second half of the Women's Super League match. The WSL, Pro Ref and both clubs have all launched investigations into the incident. The newly promoted Palace brought on Kirsty Howat to replace Shannon O'Brien in the 97th minute, having already made three previous substitutions across three separate second-half opportunities. A WSL spokesperson said: "We can confirm there was a breach of competition rules in the Crystal Palace versus Everton match. Crystal Palace used a fourth substitution opportunity during a fourth stoppage in play, when the rules permit a maximum of three substitution opportunities per match. We will now conduct an investigation alongside both clubs and Pro Ref and update in due course." Jo Potter's side were already leading the match thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith's 34th-minute opener. There were eight minutes of stoppage time indicated for the end of the second half, so the substitution in question came with merely seconds remaining. The consequences could be significant for Palace, depending on the outcome of the investigation and the verdict of any potential tribunal. The WSL's rules regarding the fielding of an ineligible player list the potential punishments in rule 7.13.2, which include the possibility that the points gained from the match be deducted or that the match be replayed. It is understood that the team of match officials who worked on that Palace-Everton game will not be appointed to the next round of games in WSL/ WSL2 on the weekend of 12-13 September, in light of this incident. Teams are permitted to use no more than three substitution opportunities per match, in addition to being able to make replacements at half-time and for concussion substitutions. Tom Garry Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The Blues were playing on the same ground where they were relegated in 2022 after a 6-0 loss to City, but on Sunday Amy Merricks’s side look far more competitive than the Birmingham team that said goodbye to the top tier four seasons ago, having kept the scoreline goalless until after half-time.

Nonetheless, on the day of Lauren Hemp’s 200th City appearance it was a dominant start from the defending champions, whose head coach, Andrée Jeglertz, said: “We created a lot of scoring chances. The first half [we were] a little bit hesitant on the ball, not determined with or without the ball, but the second half was better.”

View image in fullscreen Arsenal’s Lisa Baum fires in the only goal at Brighton. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

Merricks, who hailed Baggaley’s debut as “exceptional”, said: “We got into some good areas and lacked just a bit of anticipation that we would get there. That’s just down to belief, that’s not quality. I’m really pleased with the performance. I’m disappointed with the result but really pleased with the platform we’ve given ourselves to build on.”

Earlier, Lisa Baum marked her Arsenal debut with an exquisitely taken goal and her early strike was enough to secure a 1-0 victory at Brighton and inflict a defeat on their new head coach, Arturo Ruiz. The 19‑year‑old Germany youth international created room to shoot inside the area in the 10th minute and rifled home a clinical finish from a tight angle, in off the underside of the crossbar, to make an immediate impression on the delighted, travelling Arsenal fans behind that goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Baum, who arrived this summer from RB Leipzig, was one of four new signings to start the game for Arsenal, alongside Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodríguez. Arsenal had failed to win at Brighton in the past two league campaigns and will have been very satisfied to open their title bid with a victory as they seek to hunt down a first league title since 2019. Ruiz, who has been in charge at Brighton for nine days, saw some encouraging signs from his new team with Kiko Seike and Fran Kirby both going close.

It was a day for important debut goals as Lexi Lloyd-Smith slotted home on her first appearance for Crystal Palace to give the promoted side a priceless 1-0 win against Everton to start their campaign. Another debutant quickly impressed at Tottenham as their new striker Kirsty Hanson scored twice to help them to beat West Ham 3-1.

Liverpool were the day’s most emphatic winners as they cruised to a 4-0 win at promoted Charlton. The Germany striker Vivien Endemann scored on her debut for Liverpool after Grace Fisk had scored twice. Cornelia Kapocs added a stoppage‑time penalty to make it a poor start for Charlton, who did not register a shot on target and recorded just two efforts off target.

Sports.title: Embattled Fifa president Infantino declares intention to stand for re-election
Sports.content:
The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has reiterated his desire to stand for re-election next year despite the continuing controversy surrounding his leadership.

Infantino refused to answer questions about his future when asked by reporters at the Women’s Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday. The 56-year-old Swiss is under severe pressure to resign after trying to sell stakes in Fifa tournaments, including the World Cup, to private investors.

Uefa, the European governing body, has led calls for Infantino to step down with further opposition coming from the Asian confederation and Concacaf, which represents countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean.

But for the first time since the plan became public, Fifa has reiterated Infantino’s intention to run for a fourth and final term in next year’s elections. Should he be re-elected, he will continue to serve as head of world football until 2031.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027. Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election.”

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is widely seen as the likeliest challenger to Infantino. Montagliani, a Fifa vice-president, had long been regarded as a close ally of Infantino, but there were signs, even before he distanced himself over the now-scrapped plan to allow private investment into World Cups, that he viewed Fifa’s purpose somewhat differently to the Swiss.

However, Infantino is not without friends – Saudi Arabia, the 2034 men’s World Cup hosts, came out in support last month, with African football’s governing body, Caf, and South America’s Conmebol also supportive.

As the only declared candidate so far for the election due to take place in March 2027, Infantino will need a simple majority of votes from the 211 federations affiliated to Fifa to extend his term of office, which began in 2016. Candidate nominations for next year’s election must be submitted by 18 November.

Sports.title: Armstrong spurns golden chance to win derby as Birmingham and Wolves draw
Sports.content:
If only Adam Armstrong, the Wolves striker presented with a golden chance in the 87th minute, had shot into the same corner of the net at the Railway End that his teammate ­Jackson Tchatchoua had located when scoring one of the most ­memorable own goals at the end of the first half, then César Peixoto’s team would surely now be second in the Championship.

Instead Armstrong, one of the Football League’s most proven goalscorers, lifted his shot over an open goal from 10 yards when played in by Fer López at the end of this implausibly open derby. Birmingham ultimately deserved to extend their unbeaten start to the league season.

After their 4-2 defeat at West Ham on Tuesday, Wolves look as vulnerable defensively as they can be devas­tating going forward. Only Burnley, relegated with them last season, have conceded more than their 10 goals.

Tom Wagner, the ­Birmingham chair, was back in the St Andrew’s directors’ box for the first time since a stroke in February and was treated to a thrilling game. Spoils were shared but Chris Davies was happy with his side after they twice came from behind. “I’ll always be content when the players put in that heart and spirit,” the ­Birmingham manager said. “When you look at the quality of their team, I’ll be astonished if they’re not in the top four. Second half, we put them to the sword.”

López scored in the third ­minute for Wolves and, after Jay ­Stansfield equalised in controversial circum­stances, Ladislav Krejci gave the visitors the lead again. But then came the moment that could haunt ­Tchatchoua. The Cameroon right‑back was under no pressure as he went to turn a long diagonal from Phil Neumann back towards his ­goalkeeper – but instead looped the ball wide and over José Sá into his own goal.

That moment set the tempo for the rest of a game. Wolves, despite ­retaining the majority of their ­Premier League squad after the transfer deadline, know sheer quality of player alone will not mean promotion.

View image in fullscreen Adam Armstrong (left) reacts to his missed chance to win it for Wolves at Birmingham. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Peixoto called for video assistant referees to be brought in to the Championship after Stansfield appeared to handle when bringing down Patrick Roberts’s brilliant chip before hammering home Birmingham’s first equaliser. “If the referee doesn’t see it, then what can you do?” Stansfield said.

Peixoto said: “I don’t know why they don’t have VAR in the Champion­ship. It’s very important to help the refe­rees to take the best decisions. I saw a handball and in the screen we saw a handball.” The ­Portuguese coach also confirmed that in a pre‑season meeting with Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL), ­managers were told that grappling at corners would be penalised. “But it’s not happening,” he said.

While the home side dominated the second half, Wolves could have put the game to bed before Birmingham got going. López was involved in the buildup before advancing to side‑foot home Rodrigo Gomes’s right‑wing cross to the near post for his third goal of the season.

Then in the 19th minute, ­Christoph Klarer’s poor touch invited Raúl ­Jiménez to steal the ball and put in Gomes who allowed James ­Beadle to save his dinked attempt.

Krejci is one of the elite players surprisingly still at Wolves. The Czechia captain’s bullet header, after André flicked on Hugo Bueno’s corner, gave Wolves another endorphin boost. It was short-lived, however, as Tchatchoua lobbed home his tragicomic own goal. Jiménez hit the crossbar, as he did in defeat at West Ham, but then Neumann headed against the same woodwork midway through the second half.

Wolves had the clearest of many chances both teams had to win the game. López dispossessed Demarai Gray inside the area and, faced with the goalkeeper, squared for ­Armstrong. Somehow he contrived to lift the ball over the empty goal. “The way Jack[son Tchatchoua] committed his mistake, Adam committed the mistake in the opposite side,” Peixoto said. “We have to take the confidence to them and keep fighting and work hard for the next game.”

There was still time for ­Birmingham to think they had won it as Marvin Ducksch arced a free-kick towards the top corner. There, however, was Sá to show why he was awarded a new contract, as he tipped the ball aside to ensure this pulsating match finished even.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy takes party to Burnley after signing deal with Championship strugglers
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy has returned to English football after signing for Burnley in the Championship as a free agent.

Vardy, who will be 40 in January, has signed a contract until the end of the season, having spent last season at Cremonese in Italy. A return to Leicester, where he spent 13 years and was a Premier League champion in 2016 and an FA Cup winner in 2021, was mooted in the summer, only for Vardy to rule out a reunion.

His podcast, Jamie Vardy’s Having A Party, made the news last week for Mike Dean’s lifting of the lid on his antics as a Premier League referee and has secured broadcast rights for a Bundesliga watch-along. He has also, with his wife Rebekah, starred in an ITV reality series, and been the subject of a Netflix documentary.

Despite those wider interests, Vardy’s intention has been to carry on playing, having been a late starter, making his Football League debut at 25 after signing for Leicester.

Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last term and, with Nicky Hayen as their manager, remain without a win after their opening five games of the Championship campaign, losing to Bristol City on Saturday. Vardy joins a team bottom of the division.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town,” Vardy said. “I can’t wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.”

In June, he said of Leicester, now in League One, currently struggling under the management of Russell Martin: “I think that’s gone. I’ll always support them, always follow them. I think that’s the best thing I can do now.”

Sports.title: Richard Hughes confirmed as Al-Hilal sporting director after Liverpool departure
Sports.content:
Richard Hughes has been appointed as the sporting director ⁠of Al-Hilal, the Saudi Pro League club confirmed on ⁠Sunday, following ⁠his ​departure from Liverpool.

Hughes, 47, joined Liverpool in 2024 from Bournemouth. ⁠He appointed Arne Slot as Jürgen Klopp’s successor as head coach, ⁠a decision that paid immediate dividends ​as the Reds ‌claimed the ‌Premier League title in 2024-25. Slot ‌was sacked and replaced by Andoni Iraola in June.

“The appointment of Hughes came as part of Al-Hilal’s efforts to strengthen its football system ‌and develop its sporting structure with specialised expertise,” the Saudi Pro League leaders ​said in a statement.

The appointment highlights Al-Hilal’s drive to tap into English football, with Hughes the latest ⁠former Premier League figure to join ​the ​Riyadh-based club. Hughes follows players Gabriel ​Martinelli, Crysencio Summerville and ​Ollie Watkins, ‌who joined ​the ​Saudi club this summer from Arsenal, West Ham United and Aston Villa, respectively. Al-Hilal’s manager is Simone Inzaghi, formerly of Inter.

Two members of Liverpool’s recruitment department are set to follow Hughes to Al Hilal. Mark Burchill and Craig McKee, who joined Liverpool from Bournemouth with Hughes two years ago, are now poised to team up with the Scot in Saudi.

Sports.title: Journey to Wembley: A huge victory for Witton Albion at one of the great names of British aeronautical engineering, in part three of our FA Cup odyssey
Sports.content:
Journey to Wembley: A huge victory for Witton Albion at one of the great names of British aeronautical engineering, in part three of our FA Cup odyssey

FA Cup First Qualifying Round: Avro 0-2 Witton Albion

One of the great names of British aeronautical engineering is alive and well as the teams run out to the sound of an air raid siren and a Lancaster bomber, in Greater Manchester.

Avro, the aircraft manufacturing company which made the legendary World War Two flying machine, has long gone, but its football team remain, with a propeller mounted on the wall of their bar and a magnificent image of the RAF plane in their boardroom.

Witton Albion, who play a league below them and are travelling to face this powerful seventh-tier side on their 3G pitch in the FA Cup First Qualifying Round, do not feel quite so sentimental.

The club's collective disappointment at drawing Avro was evident on the players' WhatsApp group, soon after we'd left them celebrating their FA Cup Preliminary Round victory over Lancashire club Nelson.

That was the second part of our journey to Wembley told in 13 instalments, following a club as far as they go and then picking up with the team who knock them out, all the way to the final. 'Avro away is as tough as it gets,' groaned one of their staff.

Avro hosted Witton Albion in the FA Cup first qualifying round this weekend

A propeller mounted on the wall of Avro's bar serves as a reminder of the aircraft manufacturing company which made the legendary World War Two flying machine

Visiting supporters watching the action n the FA Cup first qualifying round at Avro

Preparations on the Witton training pitch which they call 'Little Bernabeu' – a joke name which somehow stuck - do not seem to augur well, either, when we arrive to see how the Cheshire club are approaching this tie. A rainstorm of biblical proportions is battering them and water is pouring into the stadium corridor through an overflow pipe. Someone sends for a plumber.

After the drenched players have headed back to the dressing room, striker Freddie Garbutt, on whom many of Witton's hopes will rest at Avro, wades up. He's 22 and 6ft 6in: a player who Halifax Town and Fleetwood Town have both watched and for whom National League North side Chorley have lodged an unsuccessful offer. He also provides evidence of the fruits of intelligent, painstaking British scouting at the end of a grotesque Premier League transfer window in which so little of that quality has been evident.

A friend of Witton assistant manager Mike Alcock who'd first seen Garbutt in the Under 21s at nearby Runcorn Linnets told him to take a look. Alcock watched the young forward play multiple games for Pilkington FC in St Helens. He found a raw 21-year-old with good feet and heading ability who, just as significantly, seemed receptive to advice and didn't have an entourage.

Even eighth-tier managers like Witton's Benny Harrison will get agents cold calling them to push former academy stars, these days, but Harrison generally prefers young non-league prospects, like Garbutt, who don't think the world owes them a living. 'You get lads from academies who think they're too good for this level,' says Harrison. 'And agents or interfering fathers, who can be the bane of your life. We've just had an ex-academy lad with us who expected to go straight into the team, didn't and announced he was off. We don't want that sort.'

Garbutt displays how bruising the game can be down here. There's evidence of his having a tooth knocked out in an accidental clash with a team-mate against Liverpool side Vauxhall last season and multiple bruises to his ribcage. He also broke his nose last season. He must juggle his dreams of a professional football career with a job as a tennis and padel coach at the Grappenhall Sports Club half an hour away.

'It can take its toll. Especially when we're playing twice a week,' Garbutt says of juggling the day job. He's one of only two players Witton have signed to a contract, protecting his match fee if he's injured and the club if someone else tries to sign him. But when he lost his place after the injuries, he couldn't immediately regain it. Amid the myriad uncertainties, he holds on to hopes of a football career.

Honorary life member Malc Todd emptying a bin in the changing room before Avro play Witton

Witton's striker Freddy Garbutt Garbutt is used to a bruising, challenging for the ball here

'You have to take something from the levels other players have reached after starting in the non-league,' Garbutt says, above the noise of the local brass band, who are practicing in the next-door room. 'The fact that Jamie Vardy had that happen to him gives you a little hope, I guess. It's a long way off - a dream - but I'm still only 22 and I do have ambitions.'

Garbutt arrives at Avro around 1pm, wearing a broad grin as he steps into the compact, modern ground, set within a former council estate on the outskirts of Oldham.

It might not be bucolic but grounds nestling with housing developments were a hallmark of the early rounds of Journey to Wembley, written by Daily Mail Sport's Brian James with Brian Bould's photography 50 years ago, which our odyssey is inspired by. There's a beauty in that.

Avro were forced to move here because the stadium which they'd occupied for 80 years was sold off for housing by Oldham Council. It took the intervention of Sport England, who'd supported the club financially, to insist the council relocate them, and in an area thick with strong non-league sides, Avro find themselves trying to re-establish a fanbase.

They're five miles from where they used to be and the nomadic existence has created a distinctly underdog mood. 'People look down their noses at us and say, 'They come from a council estate in Oldham,' says the club's Liam Bainbridge. 'They have nothing else to shoot us with.'

In the boardroom before kick-off, Avro's John Breedon, who's supplying tea, tells how old bombers made at the local Avro factories often fly past on their way to airshows. 'It connects us to the club's past now the factory's gone.'

Visiting striker James Steele gives Witton the lead - and Avro could not come back

Home supporters vent their frustrations during the second half of the game

Witton's Kev Wright, whose work is the glue that binds the club together, admits to some nerves but his social media post encouraging a travelling support has worked, with the Witton contingent making up fully half of the 325 crowd. The talk all week has been of how this is the 60th anniversary of Witton making the First Round Proper. They were 2-0 up against Football League side Bradford Park Avenue in 1966, with a Witton team including goalkeeper Peter Mellor, who played for Fulham in the 1975 final, and Chris Nicholl, later an Aston Villa and Southampton legend, only to lose 3-2.

The players have been asked for intensity from the off and they go all out to land a first blow, knowing how the 3G surface can soon wear you down on a day with an intermittent brilliant sun like this. The bouncing ball doesn't spin into touch as much, so there are fewer breaks in play. The hard, unyielding surface also jars. Teams who play on grass generally loathe 3G.

JOURNEY TO WEMBLEY, SO FAR Extra preliminary round, August 8: Nelson 3-2 Stockport Georgians Preliminary round, August 22: Witton Albion 1-0 Nelson 1st qualifying round, September 5: Avro 0-2 Witton Albion

Garbutt is a part of the early pressure, winning aerial duels, putting his foot in, sending on passes from balls played into his feet, and it begins to tell. Avro don't get a look-in. A loose ball is seized on by Witton's James Steele, another young striker, who thumps it into the roof of the net. Tom Hoyle's shot loops in after taking a deflection off a defender and inside 22 minutes Witton are 2-0 up.

This kind of deficit doesn't usually affect Avro. A huge save is drawn from Witton keeper Cameron Terry, clawing a ball away from under the bar after it has pinged off the insides of his right and left posts. This will prove just as significant as those goals. Avro push on again in a second half during which Witton are marshalled by the game's outstanding player – their Italian-born centre half Geffry Ebhote, a quiet but indomitable leader who joined them from Avro last year. There's no way back. By non-league football standards, this is a huge victory.

Witton have dreams of being more than a football club. They aspire to get funding to lay several 3G pitches of their own and use what would be a relatively modest investment to create a community football facility for their area.

'If football can find millions for individual transactions, contracts and agents, surely we can find a way to invest a fraction of that wealth to support the game at its foundations,' says Kev Wright.

Defeating the Lancaster Bomber team just might provide the beginnings of a new momentum. The FA Cup and its magic have a way of making things happen like that.

Sports.title: How Mikel Arteta ditched the safety-first approach to blow Chelsea away: The major shift in playing style, the key man who is making up for lost time... and the signs Arsenal could race to another Premier League title
Sports.content:
How Mikel Arteta ditched the safety-first approach to blow Chelsea away: The major shift in playing style, the key man who is making up for lost time... and the signs Arsenal could race to another Premier League title

If Chelsea turn out to be real title challengers, Arsenal have already proved they have the capacity to run away with the league. No hyperbole.

On another day, the scoreline could have been wider for the Gunners.

A solid backline against a prolific attack was how this contest had been billed, Chelsea’s CPR trio of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers out there to take the game to Arsenal’s defence.

Yet the dominant way in which Arsenal picked Chelsea apart reflected a team who see a door wide open to capitalise on the state of flux currently troubling the rest of the Big Six.

The failure to land a marquee forward before the transfer window closed did not blunt Mikel Arteta’s side. They created plenty, and were hellbent on attacking in the final third.

Despite lifting the title last season, Arsenal were often accused of being too defensive, afraid of putting their foot on the throat when ahead because of the risks it entailed.

Arsenal produced a dominant display as they picked Chelsea apart after a shift in playing style

Mikel Arteta appears to have ditched the safety-first approach that won them the league title

The opposite transpired here. Gaps were left on the counter for Chelsea to exploit, but the home team cared little.

They kept marching forward in the belief that goals would come. Two did, eventually, through Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz. Many more will arrive in future matches, if this style of play is embraced going forward.

Riccardo Calafiori struck, his goal ruled out for offside, while Arsenal also squandered a number of chances. Most of these fell to Havertz in the first half, who rebounded well to put in a strong performance across the match.

It had shades of the 2022-23 campaign, in which Arsenal would blitz opponents when the opportunities presented themselves.

It is certainly a much more exciting brand of football than fans have been accustomed to in recent seasons, a safety-first approach the ploy which ultimately led Arteta’s team to a first league title in 22 years.

The desire Arteta has to build upon last season’s triumph was clear in his words afterwards.

He said: ‘I think it's an indication for us of how capable we are to perform at an even higher level than last season. It depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire, that humbleness and continue every day to try to find a better version of myself and the team.

‘We still have a lot to grow and a lot to offer, and this is the ambition of the team.’

The evidence points to a shift in playing style. The psychological burden of constantly finishing second is no longer there. The Arsenal players and staff know and believe they have the capacity to become champions again.

We could now see a more free-flowing side that punish opponents whenever they can. And that is a rather exciting prospect for Arsenal fans and neutrals alike.

If Arteta’s men do achieve this going forward, the number of teams capable of stopping them thin out dramatically.

Their watertight defence is well-documented, and further bolstered by the acquisition of Ezri Konsa.

He had the crowd on their feet with a crunching tackle on Rogers after 56 minutes, the forward’s eyes lighting up with the space ahead of him — before being fairly cleaned out by an accurate sliding challenge.

Arteta would later describe the action as a ‘very English tackle’; it stopped Rogers dead in his tracks.

Martin Odegaard scored the winner for Arsenal and is a key man for Arteta this season

But let’s go back to the attack. On paper the lack of depth on the left wing may not be ideal. That issue can be papered over, though, when Arsenal play like this.

Just as promisingly, Martin Odegaard’s form has continued. He has already doubled his league goal tally from last season. The stop-start nature of the previous couple of seasons— largely due to injury — look to be behind him.

There’s almost a hunger to make up for lost time, constantly looking for intricate pass to assist players, and a desire to try get into the box. If Arsenal can keep him ticking along, that will be a massive boost.

A final word on Rogers, who exited the field on 87 minutes to cries from the home fans of ‘you should’ve signed for a big club’.

He had looked sharp, threatening Arsenal’s backline on breaks forward. His strike on two minutes was an early reminder of just why the Gunners chased him across the summer.

But, as Arsenal demonstrated, they may already have enough artillery to blow the rest of the league away.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury claims Anthony Joshua fight is OFF in another social media rant: Gypsy King accuses AJ of 's***ing his pants' in talks over Battle of Britain deal
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury claims Anthony Joshua fight is OFF in another social media rant: Gypsy King accuses AJ of 's***ing his pants' in talks over Battle of Britain deal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tyson Fury has suggested he will no longer be fighting Anthony Joshua in another social media rant as rows over the location and contract surrounding the fight continue.

The two British heavyweights had seemed set to finally face off later this year, but Fury had suggested his rival was stalling over the contractual agreements.

Joshua's promoter, Eddie Hearn, claimed last week that talks had 're-opened' – but things, if Fury is to be believed, seem to have again gone backwards.

'So it looks like AJ has s*** his pants yet again,' Fury said on social media on Sunday. 'After 11 years, he's finally s*** his pants yet again.'

The bitter tug-of-war over their heavyweight superfight has largely centered on a debate around hosting it at London's Wembley Stadium or broadcaster Netflix's choice of Madison Square Garden in New York City.

Last week, Fury, who regularly takes to social media to express his views on potential opponents, was keen to make clear he feels Joshua is not motivated by a love of his country. Earlier this year Daily Mail Sport revealed Joshua had in fact quit the UK to move to Dubai – even as thousands tried to flee amid rising panic in the Middle East warzone.

Tyson Fury (pictured) has claimed Anthony Joshua has bailed on their potential fight

Joshua (pictured) is still yet to sign the deal to fight Tyson Fury, Frank Warren has revealed, with a deadline for Sunday

And Fury, a tax exile to the Isle of Man himself, brought up a 2020 speech at a Black Lives Matter march, where Joshua read out a letter from his friend Reece Campbell to urge attendees to stop spending money with white-owned shops and businesses.

'Show them where it hurts', Joshua had said. 'Abstain from spending your money in their shops and economies, and invest in black-owned businesses.'

Fury re-posted the video of the speech, writing: 'This is the man who loves England, absolute s*** bag! Total piece of s*** bully with zero guts! Don't let them deceive you! & Living in Dubai.'

In an address to camera, Fury accused Joshua of trying to derail their fight to avoid being embarrassed: 'If I agreed to tie both hands behind my back and wear solid cement boots, Anthony Joshua would never get in the ring with me because I'll annihilate him.

'And he's a piece of s*** bully, and that's his game—bullying people like he tried to do to Daniel Dubois, and he got knocked spark dead out.

'The latest news from them is, 'Tyson don't want to fight in England'. Why the f*** wouldn't I want to fight in England, you sausage? 'Tyson only wants to fight in America'. Are you joking or what?

'Tyson is not in charge of this fight. Tyson didn't put the money up for this fight. Tyson is not the paymaster. Netflix are and Turki Al-Sheikh. Lovely. If it's in England, even better. I'll knock the motherf***er out even quicker. Prime time England, 10 o'clock, Wembley Stadium, 100,000 people. Why the f*** wouldn't I want it in England? Doesn't make any sense, does it?

'Like I said, who do you think you are? You and your little pathetic puppet Eddie Hearn trying to save you. There's no escaping, you know. I'll come to Watford (Joshua's hometown) and I'll set about you. I'll batter you in your own front garden, you piece of s***.'

Joshua's 2020 Black Lives Matter speech was brought back up by his great boxing rival Fury

'There is no getting out of this one. There is no getting out of this one. Get ready for this fight. I've had enough of your sauce to last me 11 years. I'm battering the f*** out of you, you useless dosser, piece of s***. That's what you are. And you know it as well, and everybody else knows what you are: a coward.'

Roaring out his title of the 'Gypsy King,' Fury added: 'You's are going down, and the cash cow is getting knocked out. Because after this, he won't be able to show his face in public ever again.

'You're a useless dosser, a big bodybuilding piece of s***. Too many weights, not enough speed. When I crack a big right hook off it, you'll go over like spaghetti legs Deontay Wilder. But he's 10 times the man you'll ever be, because he's got a pair of b*****ks like King Kong, and you've got a pair of b*****ks like two f***ing garden peas, you piece of s***.'

On Sunday, Fury revealed he has turned his attention to trying to fight Oleksandr Usyk for a third time – on the back of two defeats.

'So this would only lead me to a fight with Oleksandr Usyk,' he said. 'Let's do it again. Let's run it back in November. The ball is now in your court, Oleksandr.'

He added: 'Do you want to fight me this year, 2026, or are you calling it quits? Let me know, because I'm now looking for a new opponent.'

Fury's promoter Frank Warren, who suggested that in reality boxing's longest hatching deal had to be finalised by Sunday, told Daily Mail Sport last week: 'AJ hasn't signed yet.

'Tyson signed in January. He's training in Miami for the fight in early November and doesn't care where it takes place.'

There is debate around the contract and location of the fight, with Fury supposedly agreeing the match-up earlier this year

The original agreement stipulated England, putting Wembley Stadium on alert.

But Netflix, the mega-paymasters for the broadcast, have joined their Saudi partners in insisting on New York's fabled Madison Square Garden so as to maximise US revenue.

Joshua will need at least a two-month training camp for a fight of this magnitude and ideally nine to ten weeks.

It comes after Joshua was given ten days to agree a deal on August 26 with Warren previously warning: 'Unless AJ commits by the end of next week I'm afraid this will slip away like so many of those great fights which never happened.'

He added: 'At some point everyone has to say the most important thing is that it happens. Not this bulls*** about money.

'That everyone wants the fight. Does AJ really want it? I don't know. He's been through that tragedy of the car crash which killed two of his closest friends. Only he knows what he wants.'

Much of the discussions around Wembley centre on a willingness to allow a late start time – and late curfew – to suit the American TV market. Mayor Sadiq Khan this week stated that he is keen to host the fight and find a solution.

Sports.title: Why Nottingham Forest are yet to hit their stride under Oliver Glasner: Morgan Gibbs-White has another gear to find - and £50m signing Liam Delap must discover his speciality
Sports.content:
Without a win or even a goal at the City Ground this season, Nottingham Forest are still to splutter into life. They look solid enough under Oliver Glasner but the Austrian’s highly-structured training regime and tactical plan is squeezing Forest’s flair players a little. Glasner is a fine coach and will surely get it right. However, he could do with a victory, ideally at Aston Villa on Saturday. Daily Mail Sport looks at the challenges facing Glasner after Forest’s slow start. Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest side have yet to splutter into life this season Forest’s Delap gamble There is nothing about Liam Delap that screams ‘£50million centre-forward’. Indeed, the price tag is unfair on the player as it creates a level of expectation that he is unlikely to be able to fulfil. Delap is a competent No 9. But for that fee – and please ignore the ‘market forces’ justification – a player surely needs to have at least one special quality. What is Delap’s? He is no slouch but nor is he particularly quick. If he has been bought for his aerial ability, then his lack of impact against Jan Paul van Hecke and Micky van de Ven was worrying. Technically he is OK, nothing more. He’s strong, yes, but so are most Premier League players. His highest goal tally in a league season is 12 for Ipswich in 2024-25. Delap is probably not as good as Igor Jesus, who cost Forest only £10m from Brazilian club Botafogo a year ago and managed 16 goals in his first campaign in England. Put Delap in Botafogo’s team and there is no guarantee he would reach that tally in his opening season. More than most, Delap’s valuation reflects the madness of the summer market and if Delap thrives despite it, all credit to him. Nothing about Liam Delap suggests he is a £50m forward and the price tag has set an unfair expectation on him Gibbs-White seeking lift-off Forest’s No 10 was desperately unlucky not to make England’s World Cup squad and the club did well to hang on to him this season. He is their best player and talisman. Right now, Gibbs-White looks like a player who just needs a spark to bring him to life. He played well at Liverpool last weekend and scored a penalty in the 2-2 draw. He was perfectly good against Tottenham without ever reaching the heights he scaled during last season, especially under Vitor Pereira. There was an interesting moment after full-time when Gibbs-White shared a warm greeting and a chat with Allan Dixon, the Brad Friedel lookalike who is Tottenham’s long-serving player liaison office. Spurs came close to signing Gibbs-White last summer when they thought they had triggered a £60m release clause in his contract, only for the 26-year-old to sign a new deal with Forest instead. Morgan Gibbs-White looks like he needs a spark to bring him to life, as he is so far yet to scale the heights of his form last season Glasner revealed post-match that Murillo 'did not come back from Brazil in the shape he should come back' Glasner puts Murillo on notice One of the joys of covering Glasner’s press conferences is that he will suddenly produce a zinger from nowhere. Delivered in his calm, even tones, it catches the listener by surprise even more. Asked why his star defender Murillo had come off late in the came, Glasner let slip that the Brazilian – who had been out injured for four months – ‘did not come back from Brazil in the shape he should come back, maybe.’ Pressed on Murillo’s fitness, Glasner understandably decided not to stick the boot in, but spoke more generally about the level of conditioning required to play in his team. But the message was clear. Murillo has been largely undroppable since he joined Forest three years ago. With Glasner’s signing Ousmane Diomande waiting for his chance, perhaps that is no longer the case.

Sports.title: Gary Neville reveals why he has a 'big fear' about Man United's defence after draw with Everton and names THREE stars at fault for Ainsley Maitland-Niles' stunning 96TH-MINUTE equaliser: 'I was screaming at the TV!'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville reveals why he has a 'big fear' about Man United's defence after draw with Everton and names THREE stars at fault for Ainsley Maitland-Niles' stunning 96TH-MINUTE equaliser: 'I was screaming at the TV!'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gary Neville has torn into Manchester United's defence, admitting he can't see a way out of his former side regularly conceding goals after they shipped two more to Everton on Sunday.

The Red Devils have conceded twice in each of their three Premier League matches so far this season, and they were held to a 2-2 draw with Everton after a last-minute Ainsley Maitland-Niles stunner.

It's an issue manager Michael Carrick is going to have to fix if his side want to be competitive this year – they are currently 11th in the table with one win, one draw and one defeat to their names so far this term.

And Neville has concerns. Questions were raised after the transfer window closed with the club failing to add to their defensive ranks, and the full back-turned pundit is worried it may come back to bite them.

'Manchester United are conceding two goals a game,' he said on the Gary Neville Podcast. 'From a United perspective you can't concede two goals a game, they're on track to concede 76 goals.

'They won't do, but the one thing that I think needed to happen beyond the transfer window with the questions that have been asked about the defence was that Manchester United needed to win today and secondly they couldn't concede goals.

Manchester United shipped two more goals against Everton as they drew 2-2 on Sunday

Gary Neville has admitted he has a 'big fear' that his former side will continue to concede goals

'That last goal is a really bad one. There's a lot that happens before that goal goes in the back of Manchester United's net. When you're playing against a team, it's 2-1, you're away, you've got to push up, you've got to make sure you don't have players sprinting off and doing stupid things.

'Dorgu sprints forward, the ball gets played past him and Everton just drift down that left side so easily. Santos doesn't get across and when he doesn't get across quickly enough Yoro is deep and narrow, almost playing like a third or fourth narrow centre back waiting for the ball to go into the box.

'So they could have stopped it at source. That to me is a real error in the lead-up, and I was screaming as it happened because you know full well you're going to get the ball pumped into the box and you're going to get a team behind desperate in the last few minutes so you have to make sure you're organised and United weren't organised in that last couple of minutes.'

The Red Devils will take on local rivals Manchester City next weekend in the Manchester derby, but first face Azerbaijan side Sabah FK in the Champions League.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez played at centre back against Everton, and it was the same partnership last week in the 5-2 win over Ipswich.

Maguire played with Ayden Heaven on the opening day 2-0 defeat by Hull.

'Teams think they've got a chance against them,' Neville continued. 'I thought they were a little bit complacent and I was saying it after the first goal, they lacked that killer instinct before that period when Everton equalised and then they react again.

'Everton weren't at it at all in that first half – United were the better team and didn't have that killer instinct up top and certainly from 1-0 up to 1-1 they let Everton back in the game. It's not going full throttle when you've got a team down, putting them away and then this liability of conceding goals.

United manager Michael Carrick has expressed his own concerns about the goals they have been conceding

'I don't think it's going to go away and that's my big fear. I think conceding goals is going to chase them and hunt them down the road and I don't know how Michael deals with it because he's got his best back four on the pitch. I don't know why Luke Shaw went off with five minutes to go – hopefully he's not injured. I don't know why Dalot went off with five minutes to go.

'To be fair, Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag used to change their back four a lot as well – you can't be changing your back four. If you've got Hincapie to come on for Calafiori maybe you can, but United have got a back four of Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and Lisandro Martinez and they've not got much behind that. So you can't really change your back four at 1-0 or 2-1.'

Carrick himself was critical of his defence in the wake of the result.

He doesn't have too many options to change things in terms of personnel – with Matthijs De Ligt still missing with a long-term injury. Therefore, Carrick insisted, it's down to his current crop to do better.

'Obviously we can't ignore it,' he said about Maitland-Niles' equaliser. 'We need to concede fewer goals to give us a better chance of winning games. We'll certainly look at that and keep improving.

'There's obviously things we need to get better at as a team. There's been two strikes from distance really, two really good strikes from their point of view. Sometimes they fly in the top corner and more often than not they probably don't.'

Sports.title: Inside Michael Jordan's secret pep talk to inspire his most satisfying championship after bitter legal fight... as familiar face stands in his way
Sports.content:
Michael Jordan's last championship came in 1998, but that fierce competitive drive has never left him. And now, less than 12 months after a bitter legal fight, he has a different kind of championship firmly in his sights.

He's waited nearly three decades, so it is no surprise he wants to make this count. Given his six NBA Championships and Finals MVP awards, and his reputation for an unrelenting excellence down the stretch, there is perhaps nobody in sports who could be better placed to pass on pearls of wisdom.

'He's the best guy for it,' Tyler Reddick tells the Daily Mail. This weekend, Reddick begins the NASCAR Chase, the new, 10-race postseason format that will decide the NASCAR Cup Series champion on November 8 at the end of a long, arduous season.

He enters as the third seed and, although teammate Bubba Wallace also made the cut in 14th place, he represents the best hope Jordan has of adding one of his most long-awaited and also most satisfying triumphs.

Less than a year ago, Jordan was traveling from his lakefront North Carolina mansion to Charlotte for a trial at the U.S. District Court. Jordan was ever-present in the courtroom in the Charles R. Jonas Federal Building, giving testimony in a bitter lawsuit as his team and another, Front Row Motorsports, filed an antitrust lawsuit against NASCAR.

After eight long days, on December 11, he stood side by side with NASCAR chairman Jim France after the two sides agreed a settlement and ended their fierce dispute.

Michael Jordan is closing in on a long-awaited championship, this time as a NASCAR owner

Jordan settled a bitter antitrust lawsuit with NASCAR last December in a court in Charlotte

Last month, Jordan instead made the short trip to Airspeed, the state-of-the-art headquarters he built for his race team around 10 miles north of Charlotte in Huntersville, North Carolina.

Instead of needing to win over a jury, he simply had to win over his own employees and deliver some inspiration before their quest for supremacy begins, knowing he is 10 races away from becoming a NASCAR champion team owner.

'For me, anytime I get to spend that time with Michael, it leaves a huge impact on me,' Reddick says. 'I really do love it when he comes to 23XI, to Airspeed, because I have an opportunity to see the impact that he has on the men and women that work here.'

Jordan is far from a passive owner. He regularly attends races, less so when he's vacationing in the summer months, but never misses tuning in wherever he is in the world.

While he tends to keep a low profile at the track, granting the very occasional Fox interview to his trusted reporter, Jamie Little, he is a familiar face these days for the limited number of his employees who travel the country and attend each race.

For the drivers, he is always just a text message away, offering words of congratulations or encouragement after every single race, depending on the result. Sometimes, the text drops before they've even got out of the car.

But every so often, he'll drop in to speak to everyone back at their base, just as he did last month.

Sometimes he gives a heads up, meetings are booked in, the red carpet is rolled out. But often he just stops by, largely unannounced, surprising everyone with his unmissable, 6ft 6inch frame strolling through the front doors.

Tyler Reddick told the Daily Mail about Jordan's recent visit to the 23XI Racing facility

Reddick hopes to drive his No.45 car owned by the NBA legend to a NASCAR Championship

'When he came in here to address the company, he's just a great speaker,' Reddick says. 'He knows how to get the point across, he knows how to get people excited, and he knows how to make it relatable. Just an amazing leader, a great speaker, and for us, it was great that he made the time to come see us, come talk to us.

'Just anytime he makes time for us, it goes a long way.'

At one stage, it all seemed too good to be true for Jordan and Reddick. They won the Daytona 500 - the sport's biggest and first race of the season - in February, then rattled off wins in the next two races. He became the first driver in Cup Series history to win the first three races, with some baseless suggestions even claiming it must be rigged for Jordan's team.

By April 19, Jordan had seen his No.45 car in victory lane five times in the first nine races, the best start to a season since the legendary Dale Earnhardt in 1987. The regular season championship seemed a foregone conclusion, and the top seeding to go with it, bringing a points advantage to start The Chase.

Instead, things started to unfold. Reddick dropped to third in the standings, plagued by just as much bad luck as good luck he had in the first few weeks in a sport where circumstance and fortune are never far away.

It made the timing of Jordan's visit perfect, and Reddick is confident it can help unlock another level of performance, insisting he feels 'really good, honestly,' about where they stand.

'I guess you could look at it one way and say we didn't have a great summer, we dropped from first in the standings to fourth, but the things that were happening in the races for us, like, as catastrophic as they were, for us to not lose more ground, for us to fight through it and still get some amount of points and finish out of those days... it's a really good fight, you know?

'I think everyone wants to go into this Chase and have 10 flawlessly executed races, no mistakes, but...there's gonna be thousands of laps ran. Tens of thousands of decisions to make.

Jordan and Reddick celebrated winning the Daytona 500 in February, NASCAR's biggest race

Jordan was again on hand when Reddick won the third race of the year in a red-hot start

Reddick's team will look to recapture that early season momentum after being inspired by MJ

'People are gonna have mistakes, people are gonna have bad days, and I feel like when they come our way, we've been through just about everything. We know how to handle it, we know how to get through it, we know how to reset for the next week.

'On the other side of it, the majority of the racetracks in The Chase, we've had a lot of speed at, we've won at, we've led laps at, so got a lot of tracks that are strengths for us.

'It's been a really strange way for it to balance itself out, but I think you can look at it one way and say, man, the results really, really went off the edge, just bad, but, within those races, there was many good decisions made, there was a lot of fight, a lot of grit in the team, and trying to dig out of those holes.

'On one hand, it's no fun and not great to have days like that, but for us to push through those days and still make something out of them, was really, really good on our team's part.

'I think for us, yeah, we want to go into this and be as clean as possible, stay out of trouble, have good results, good stage finishes, but again, things are gonna happen.

'It may happen. One driver may go through this whole thing flawlessly, but, it is so hard to do over the course of two and a half months, 10 races. Just being able to stay in it mentally this whole Chase is gonna be super important, and I feel like we had to stretch longer than 10 races where we had just crazy things happened to us, but no one fell out of the fight. We just kept resetting and showing back up the next week, so… in a lot of ways, I feel good about it.'

Reddick has 15 other drivers still hoping to lift the Cup Series Championship at Homestead-Miami Speedway on November 8. But the man to beat, who surpassed him to top the regular season points standings, is Denny Hamlin, Jordan's business partner and co-owner of the team.

While Hamlin is integral to building Reddick's team into a Championship contender, for the next 10 races, he is fully focused on winning his own long-awaited first title at Joe Gibbs Racing as his glittering driving career nears the end.

'I think the battle that was on everyone's mind much of this season is still there,' Reddick admits. 'I think the 11 (Hamlin) will be really strong.'

Joe Gibbs Racing driver Denny Hamlin co-owns 23XI Racing as Jordan's friend and partner

Hamlin and Reddick are fighting one another for the NASCAR Cup Series Championship

But it is clear some of Jordan's mindset has rubbed off on Reddick and his team. They are ready to roll with the punches, focus on themselves and exhibit a mental strength and toughness in line with their boss during his Bulls dynasty.

'I think in a Chase format, your biggest rival, your biggest challenger will be yourself,' Reddick declares. 'It's gonna be really important to stay in it mentally this whole stretch. Again, there's gonna be things that happen, things that don't go according to plan, it's just gonna be super important to stay in it the whole way, mentally.

'We can look at other drivers that will have speed, performance, but, I think it's gonna be important for us to focus on how we maximize each day, and not let the one standout car this week or that week just spin us out with how fast they are. Making the most of each day is gonna be so critical.'

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy returns to England! Striker and wife Rebekah to move back from Italy as he signs surprise deal at Burnley - who are rock bottom of the Championship
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy will be playing his football in England again after signing a contract at Burnley until the end of the season. The 39-year-old has been a free agent since leaving Italian side Cremonese in the summer following their relegation to Serie B. Vardy, who moved to Italy with his wife Rebekah and their family, scored seven goals and provided three assists in 29 appearances in Serie A last season. Burnley will be hoping Vardy's experience can help them improve after a poor start to the season – with the Clarets bottom of the Championship after five matches. They want him to be their No1 striker and his deal has an option for a further year if Burnley are promoted. It is understood he turned down offers from MLS, Serie A and the Premier League. The scale of his task is clear with the club yet to win a game in the English second tier so far this season – drawing two and losing three of their matches, scoring six and conceding 12 across those matches. Upon signing for the club, Vardy – who had a Netflix documentary about his career in May – expressed his desire to propel them back up the table. Jamie Vardy is back in English football after signing a deal at Burnley until end of this season The move sees Vardy and his wife Rebekah return to England after he played a year in Italy He scored seven goals and provided three assists in 29 Serie A games for Cremonese He told the club's website: 'I'm really happy to now be here at Burnley. 'This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town. 'I can't wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.' Burnley head coach Nicky Hayen is excited about what his new striker will add to his struggling squad. He said: 'We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley. 'His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign. Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt.' Vardy scored 200 goals in 500 matches for Leicester and won both the Premier League and FA Cup with the club. He is regarded as one of the club's greatest players of all time. The striker also scored seven goals in 26 appearances for England and was part of the Three Lions squad for Euro 2016 and the 2018 World Cup.

Sports.title: Goalkeeping son of former Premier League manager scores TWICE to save a draw... but can YOU guess who his famous father is?
Sports.content:
A goalkeeper stepping up to rescue a point for his side by scoring in the 11th minute of added time would be an impressive story in most matches – but to do it with his second goal of the game is simply incredible. Yet that is exactly what happened in the Dutch top tier this weekend, when Telstar’s No1 kept his cool to dispatch two penalties and earn a draw for his 10-man side after going 2-0 down at home to Cambuur. And the goalkeeper’s name will be well known to football fans across the globe – Ronald Koeman Jr is the son of the Netherlands and Barcelona legend and former Southampton and Everton manager. Unsurprisingly, the 31-year-old became the first goalkeeper to score two goals in one Eredivisie game. The drama came after their striker Nokkvi Thorisson saw red for a knee-high challenge in the 22nd minute, leaving the hosts facing playing well over an hour with a man down. Cambuur then took a two-goal lead just after the break before Telstar were awarded a penalty in the 67th minute. Koeman Jr stepped up to bury the ball past Thijs Jansen and halve the deficit. RONALD KOEMAN JR. SCOORT ZIJN TWEEDE VANDAAG EN REDT EEN PUNT 🤯🔥#telcam pic.twitter.com/A3SG3QkHQb — ESPN NL (@ESPNnl) September 6, 2026 Ronald Koeman Jr buries his second spot-kick of the game to earn a 2-2 draw for Telstar The Dutchman has now scored three spot-kicks this year for the Eredivisie side Ronald Koeman, 63, resigned as Netherlands boss after their World Cup exit in the round of 32 A crazy final ten minutes saw Telstar get awarded another penalty, but following a VAR review, referee Joey Kooij reversed his decision to award the spot-kick – only to award another one in the final seconds. He scored his first penalty for Telstar back in May – their final game of last season – after which he revealed he was the club’s first-choice keeper. ‘Back in my youth, I used to take it sometimes and I missed,’ said Koeman Jr after securing a win against FC Volendam. ‘But now I’m shooting it well.’ ‘In the first half of the season, we got two penalties and we missed both of them. Then at Sparta away, Anthony (Correia, then manager) came up to me at half-time and asked if I wanted to take it if we got one.’ ‘So then I said: “Yes, of course, why not?”'

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Double boost as new arrival eyed and star set for new role after £80m decision
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Double boost as new arrival eyed and star set for new role after £80m decision

Liverpool have been handed a double boost after picking up their first Premier League win of the season on Friday

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has plenty to smile about (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool have picked up their first win of the season, giving Andoni Iraola some welcome breathing space after a difficult start to his reign. The Reds had opened the campaign with successive draws, conceding four goals in the process.

‌



A point at Newcastle on the opening day was followed by another frustrating draw against Nottingham Forest at Anfield. But Friday's trip to Portman Road provided the clearest indication yet that Liverpool are beginning to find their feet under their new manager.

‌



Two goals from Alexander Isak inside the opening nine minutes were enough to secure a 2-0 victory over Ipswich, taking the Sweden international's tally to three goals in as many games. Liverpool now face a sterner test on Wednesday when Atletico Madrid visit Anfield in the Champions League, before Fulham head to Merseyside on Saturday.

‌



With the dust settling on a busy transfer window, Iraola can now focus on getting Liverpool moving up the table. And there could be further developments on the way, with the club considering a new arrival while one of their established stars looks set for a fresh role. With that in mind, here are the latest Liverpool-related headlines.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Richard Hughes' 18 Liverpool transfer ranked with best and worst deals decided READ MORE :

Richard Hughes replacement eyed

Liverpool have begun their search for a new sporting director after Richard Hughes officially stepped down from the role over the weekend.

‌



Hughes joined from Bournemouth in 2024 and oversaw a significant period of recruitment, including last summer's £450million spending spree. Liverpool broke the British transfer record twice during that window, signing Florian Wirtz for £116m before bringing in Isak for £125m.

According to The Athletic, Liverpool technical director Julian Ward is among the candidates being considered. The former Manchester City scout joined Liverpool in 2012, initially working in the club's scouting department, before being promoted to assistant sporting director in 2020. Two years later, he succeeded Michael Edwards as sporting director.

View 3 Images Liverpool technical director Julian Ward is being eyed for the sporting director role (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Ward spent two years in the role, overseeing the arrivals of Luis Diaz, Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai. He was also involved in the £75m signing of Darwin Nunez, which has since failed to deliver the expected return on Liverpool's substantial investment. In 2024, he was appointed as the club's technical director.

Assistant sporting director David Woodfine and FSG director of football development Pedro Marques are also understood to be under consideration. Liverpool have not ruled out looking beyond the club either, with an external appointment also a possibility.

Gakpo tipped for new role

Former Liverpool star Jason McAteer believes Cody Gakpo could have an important part to play in Andoni Iraola's plans this season, despite appearing to face an uncertain future at Anfield for much of the summer.

‌



Gakpo had been heavily linked with the exit door, with Tottenham and Manchester City both showing a strong interest in the Netherlands international. Liverpool ultimately rejected an £80m bid from City towards the end of the transfer window, a decision which now looks increasingly significant given the way Gakpo has started the campaign.

The arrival of Bradley Barcola had appeared to push Gakpo further down the pecking order, with the £123m signing expected to make the left wing position his own. But Gakpo has responded in the best possible fashion, scoring once and providing three assists in his opening three games.

View 3 Images Cody Gakpo has made a strong start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

‌



McAteer believes that form, coupled with Liverpool's need for options across the forward line, means there is still a prominent role for Gakpo to fill.

"It's been framed as Gakpo needing to find a way back, but I wouldn't say it's like that at all," McAteer told TEAMtalk. "He's had a fantastic start to the season, scoring goals and being heavily involved in Liverpool's best moments in their games so far.

"Barcola predominantly plays on the left... Cody started on the right against Forest, and while it didn't quite click, he's far more suited to the left or down the middle, where we've seen his quality for the Netherlands and Liverpool.

Article continues below

"But there is a role for him at Anfield this season, make no mistake... that right-hand side is still up for grabs. Nobody has cemented it. Gakpo will get plenty of game time, either filling in down the middle if Isak is out, or operating on the right."
