Turning Point’s leaders privately acknowledge there is no replacing Kirk, who will be honored one year after his death at Trump’s midterm convention in Dallas on Thursday. Instead, they have focused on what they can preserve and expand: the organization he built around himself.

“Yes, we don’t have Charlie’s social media anymore, which is a big loss. And we don’t have his voice — huge deal,” a person involved in the organization told CNN. “But the actual machinery of Turning Point has never been bigger.”

As evidence, they pointed to a recent training for 150 new staffers. Online job boards show dozens of openings to work for Turning Point in battleground states.

“We’re going to be even bigger this election than we were in 2024,” Bowyer said.

Turning Point’s Super Bowl

Attendees observe the National Anthem during AmericaFest, the first Turning Point USA summit since the death of Charlie Kirk on December 20, 2025, in Phoenix. Cheney Orr/Reuters

Political memorabilia adorns the shelves of Bowyer’s office — a Calvin Coolidge pendant, a bust of Teddy Roosevelt, and a framed print of Newsweek’s never-published 2016 “Madam President” cover of Hillary Clinton next to Time’s cover featuring Trump as Person of the Year.

Among them is a painting of Kirk, whose face is inescapable throughout Turning Point’s Arizona campus.

There, Bowyer oversees the organization’s voter turnout machine — the “pinnacle” of Kirk’s legacy, as he described it.

“It’s kind of like the Super Bowl,” Bowyer said. “It’s pointless to educate hundreds of thousands, if not millions, of young people, for them just to go, ‘Oh, you know, don’t use that.’ Right?”

He added, “Charlie really believes in that,” slipping into present tense to describe his deceased friend and former leader — not for the only time during a 90-minute interview with CNN.

Bowyer is now expanding a program piloted in the 2024 election. Then, the group embedded staff and volunteers in neighborhoods throughout Arizona to mobilize potential Republican voters. Rather than send canvassers to knock on as many doors as possible, Turning Point instructed its organizers to make genuine connections, build relationships, show up at local events and, at least initially, avoid talking politics.

It’s a strategy built around quality, not quantity, Bowyer argues.

By Election Day, organizers are expected to have a plan for getting their assigned households — about 600 to 1,000 people — to the polls or to vote by mail. “Ballot chasers” are tasked with ensuring they follow through. Each organizer’s goal is to turn out about half their designated voters — a much higher threshold than traditional canvassers.

The effectiveness of the operation is difficult to measure, and there are Republican skeptics, including within Trump’s own political operation. But Turning Point emerged from 2024 with a compelling result to point to: Trump won Arizona by 5.5 percentage points, his largest victory of all the battleground states.

President Donald Trump waves as he leaves the stage after addressing a Turning Point USA event in Phoenix on April 17, 2026. Jim Watson/AFP/Getty Images

The victory emboldened Turning Point to double down in 2026. Even before the midterm map had fully taken shape, the organization was deploying staff and hiring in key battleground states. Maps of those states line the walls inside Turning Point Action’s headquarters with heat maps of voters and detailed breakdowns on “chaseable votes.”

This spring, the operation had a dry run when it joined the White House’s retribution campaign against Republican lawmakers in Indiana who resisted Trump’s calls to redraw the state’s congressional boundaries. Trump-backed challengers defeated seven of the eight GOP holdouts.

Indiana Lt. Gov. Micah Beckwith, a Trump ally, said Turning Point mobilized quickly despite little history in his state and noted the group left behind manpower for future political battles.

“The proof is in the pudding. Critics could say, ‘This is the first year. What good are they going to do?’” Beckwith said. “I don’t know how you break down the pie chart of who deserves credit, but we won and won in a big way.”

Republican operatives in key states say Turning Point is already making its presence felt. Former New Hampshire GOP Chairman Chris Ager said the group arrived on the ground far earlier than usual for a grassroots organization, hired experienced local activists and their visibility has been “extremely high.”

Jason Roe, a veteran Michigan strategist, said Turning Point’s organizers have been more “engaged and impactful” than the college-age men and women he typically encounters in groups for young Republican.

“Turning Point is made up of true believers,” Roe said. “They’re griding because they care, not because it’s the first step on a journey to getting involved in politics.”

In Iowa, Turning Point’s growing influence has already been tested against the most powerful endorsement in Republican politics.

The organization supported businessman and farmer Zach Lahn in the state’s closely watched Republican primary for governor. Trump backed Rep. Randy Feenstra.

Lahn won.

“We were so busy talking about the Trump endorsement,” said Jeff Angelo, a prominent conservative radio host in Iowa, “that we missed the most important endorsement: Turning Point Action.”

Trouble in the desert

Tyler Bowyer speaks during the public memorial service for Charlie Kirk in Glendale, Arizona, on September 21, 2025. Patrick T. Fallon/AFP/Getty Images

No one needs less convincing of Turning Point’s sway with GOP voters than Julie Spilsbury.

Last year, Bowyer made it his stated mission to oust Spilsbury, a registered Republican who supported Kamala Harris for president over Trump, from the City Council in Mesa, where he resides. Turning Point helped lead an effort to recall her, and in December 2025, Spilsbury lost the seat she had held for five years by about 700 votes.

“It was devastating and heartbreaking and made a lot of people mad,” she said.

Spilsbury considers herself a casualty of Turning Point’s growing clout in the Arizona GOP — and what she and others described as its vindictive approach to intraparty politics. The organization has aggressively intervened in primaries and endorsed dozens of candidates, stacking up wins and bruising fellow Republicans along the way.

The clashes have become increasingly public. Bowyer faced blowback in July after he questioned on X whether Arizona state Rep. Quang Nguyen, a Republican who escaped communist Vietnam as a child, can speak English. When Republican state Rep. Nick Kupper came to Nguyen’s defense, Bowyer threatened to back a challenger against Kupper in 2028 and later announced Turning Point was withdrawing its endorsement.

Reached by CNN via email, Kupper declined to revisit the episode. Attempts to reach Nguyen through his office were unsuccessful.

Such tactics might go overlooked by Republicans in the Trump era if Turning Point was consistently turning its primary success into general election wins. In Arizona, it has not.

The organization played a key role in the unsuccessful 2022 campaigns of Republican gubernatorial nominee Kari Lake and GOP Senate candidate Blake Masters. Lake lost a Senate race two years later.

A Turning Point official noted the organization didn’t endorse Lake in her primaries but jumped in to help after she became the GOP nominee. Still, Bowyer contended they were “on the path for Kari to win” in 2022. The lesson from the loss, he argued, was that the organization needed more manpower.

“If we would have kept going and chased more votes, I think we could have won,” he said. Lake lost the governor’s race by roughly 17,000 votes.

The defeats have spread to far smaller Arizona contests. Earlier this year, Turning Point jumped into races for the Salt River Project, a local utility board whose elections typically draw little public attention. The group’s involvement drove a surge in turnout from both sides, but clean-energy candidates ultimately won a majority of seats for the first time in recent memory.

The Turning Point official argued that the group secured the two most critical positions leading the board “amid national headwinds that have impacted local races.” But progressives claimed victory after the election, and even local Republicans have acknowledged the board’s leftward turn was a significant setback.

“I think (Turning Point) is bombing hard, and it’s excellent for everyone else. I hesitate to say too much because we don’t want them to stop,” said Autumn Johnson, executive director of the Arizona Solar Energy Industries Association. “They have absolutely no idea what they’re doing, and they don’t know they don’t know what they’re doing. And it turns out a lot of people hate them.”

Their presence is causing divisions within the GOP at a time when the party is losing power across the state, argued Nick Myers, a member of the Arizona Corporation Commission, a state utility board. A Turning Point-backed challenger defeated Myers in a primary earlier this year. He said he lost the organization’s support after a back-and-forth on X with Bowyer a few years ago.

“As soon as they started getting involved, Republicans started losing,” Myers said. “It’s not because we’re becoming a purple state. Voters can’t stand the candidates Turning Point is nominating. Their days are limited if they don’t start putting up candidates who can win.”

The organization is betting on Biggs, the gubernatorial nominee, to reverse the party’s recent fortunes. The Turning Point official noted that Biggs was one of Kirk’s final and most passionate endorsements, viewing him as “a transformational and generational leader for Arizona — somebody who could turn Arizona into the Florida of the West.”

Bowyer said Biggs is a more seasoned politician than his predecessors and is better positioned to take on Katie Hobbs, the nation’s most vulnerable Democratic governor this year. Turning Point is now more experienced in campaign work, too, he added.

Some Republicans in Arizona view the race as a referendum on Turning Point as much as Biggs. Barrett Marson, a longtime GOP operative in Arizona, said if Biggs wins, many Republicans expect Turning Point to effectively take over the state GOP. A loss, though, would have its own consequences.

“Turning Point is all in on two people: Andy Biggs and JD Vance,” Marson said. “If both of those guys lose their upcoming elections, I predict they won’t be around much after 2028.”

Vance-Turning Point 2028?

Erika Kirk greets Vice President JD Vance during Turning Point USA’s AmericaFest in Phoenix on December 21, 2025. Jon Cherry/AP

Turning Point recently doubled its staff in Iowa and is rapidly deploying organizers in New Hampshire ahead of key midterm races in both states. When the elections are over, the teams will remain — and wait for Vance to make a decision.

Erika Kirk sent one of the first shockwaves through the 2028 presidential race in December when she endorsed Vance — getting ahead not only of the vice president, but of Trump, who is widely expected to play a decisive role in choosing his successor. Since then, Turning Point has set out to demonstrate that a turnkey organization will be waiting for Vance if he launches a White House bid.

Ager, the former New Hampshire party chairman, said Turning Point could present a “significant organizational advantage out of the gate” for Vance in 2028 when Republicans there vote in the GOP’s first presidential primary. Iowa, meanwhile, will hold the party’s first nominating contest.

“It’s still up to the candidate to convince voters,” he said. “But a good organization absolutely helps.”

Vance has remained close to Turning Point, appearing at several events and guest-hosting Kirk’s podcast.

The mutual loyalty is “downstream of the genuine close friendship that JD had with Charlie,” a source close to the vice president told CNN. Kirk helped propel Vance within the party and into his current role.

Though he remains reticent to publicly discuss his political future, Vance privately views Turning Point’s support as a key to his future ambitions, the source said. The organization offers Vance a connection to “America First” stalwarts in Trump’s coalition and a well-funded political infrastructure separate from the president’s political operation.

“They are specifically a MAGA power center, versus a traditional power center,” the source said. “They are distinctly different from the old guard establishment that wouldn’t necessarily support JD, and that serves as a true home for the MAGA voters.”

Bowyer said he expects Vance to closely watch the midterm results before he finalizes his plans. But he added, “If people want you to run, and you decide not to run, you usually don’t ever get a chance to run again.”

For Turning Point, delivering Republican victories this fall, particularly in Arizona, would give Vance reason to trust the organization Kirk left behind could help carry him to the White House.

Failure would bring its own reckoning, and Bowyer said Turning Point would judge itself more harshly than any outside critic if the group fell short.

Said Bowyer: “Charlie felt that way.”

World.title: Parents of San Diego mosque gunman say a mental health facility failed to heed FBI warning
World.content:
LOS ANGELES AP —

Just days before two teenagers carried out a mass shooting at a San Diego mosque, federal law enforcement officials warned the parents of one of the shooters that their son was making concerning comments about school shootings on the dark web, according to new details included in a recently filed lawsuit.

The mother of Caleb Vazquez alleges in her lawsuit that Park Mental Health Treatment of San Diego failed to intervene despite signs that her 18-year-old son posed an imminent threat to himself and others. Vazquez was living there and receiving treatment for a range of mental health conditions, including depression and psychotic episodes, the lawsuit says. The court filings follow a number of high-profile convictions of guardians who provided teenagers with weapons that were later used in mass shootings.

The FBI called Vazquez’s mother on the evening of May 14, and she said she immediately left a message with the treatment facility to notify its staff, according to the lawsuit, filed in a San Diego court on Aug. 31. Vazquez’s mother again shared the FBI’s warnings with her son’s therapist on May 15 and with a program director later that night.

On May 18, the morning of the shooting, employees at the facility contacted Vazquez’s mother to tell her that he was missing. Video surveillance footage subsequently showed Vazquez leaving the property at 8 p.m. the night before.

Vazquez’s parents were driving around looking for him on the morning of the shooting. Vazquez and another teenager killed three people at the San Diego mosque that day before taking their own lives.

It is unclear whether Vazquez was allowed to leave the previous evening or whether he broke facility rules by doing so. Park Mental Health offers a range of treatment options, some of which advertise 24-hour surveillance, while others provide more limited counseling.

The center did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment Saturday afternoon. In a previous statement to radio station KPBS, Park Mental Health disputed the assertions in the lawsuit.

“While it is understandable that his parents might seek to blame someone in their time of loss, this lawsuit is misguided in that neither Park nor its employees are responsible for Mr. Vazquez’s actions,” the statement to KPBS read. “Only he and his coconspirator bear responsibility for their conduct and, ultimately, his death.”

Three people were killed in the attack. Nelvin C. Cepeda/The San Diego Union-Tribune/MediaNews Group RM/Getty Images

An FBI spokesperson declined to comment Saturday, citing agency policy.

The FBI’s alleged contact with Vazquez’s parents was not the first sign of his mental deterioration.

Vazquez had been hospitalized for roughly three days in January 2026 after telling a classmate that he wanted to carry out a school shooting.

Almost exactly a year earlier, Vazquez was flagged to law enforcement for exhibiting alarming behavior and idolizing Nazis, prompting police to confiscate 26 guns from his father under a 2014 California law allowing firearms to be taken from people considered dangerous.

Authorities have said Vazquez met the other shooter, Cain Clark, 17, online and that both were radicalized there. Police have not shared more details about how they knew each other or specified whose weapons were used in the shooting.

The lawsuit was filed on the same day that North Carolina authorities announced the indictment of a 17-year-old in connection with the shooting.

World.title: Witkoff and Kushner arrive in Kyiv for second leg of US diplomacy push
World.content:
US envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner travelled to Kyiv on Sunday after concluding intensive talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, as Washington renews its push to end the war in Ukraine.

It marks their first visit to the Ukrainian capital since the war began and comes amid near-constant Russian missile and drone strikes on the Ukrainian capital.

After greeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the US envoy was taken on a tour of a cathedral in central Kyiv damaged in Russian attacks. St. Sophia’s Cathedral, which is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, has had its windows and window frames damaged. On Friday, CNN reported on a Russian strike hitting Ukraine’s Security Service headquarters in Kyiv, which also affected the cathedral.

Ahead of their meeting, the Ukrainian president thanked US President Donald Trump for allowing the trip to happen “from a security standpoint,” adding that Ukraine had been “waiting a long time” for Witkoff and Kushner’s visit.

Earlier, Zelensky wrote on Telegram, “We are ready for talks. Ukraine has always been and will continue to be constructive.” He added, “We are committed to bringing the war to an end. Peace is needed. Security guarantees are needed. A dignified post-war peace is needed. Our proposals are ready.”

Zelensky has previously stressed said that an acute shortage of air defense interceptors has left Ukraine vulnerable to ballistic missile attacks.

Kyrylo Budanov, Head of the Office of the Ukrainian Presidency, said that representatives from France, the UK and Germany were also in Kyiv. “We have a busy day ahead of us, filled with important talks,” he said.

The delegation was taken for a tour to St. Sophia Cathedral, which has been damaged by a Russian strike. Ukrainian Presidency

Witkoff and Kushner made a stop in the Polish city of Rzeszow en route from Moscow to Kyiv, Russian state media outlet TASS reported. The plane landed at 1:31 a.m. local time. The US envoys most likely continued their journey by rail, it reported.

Russia and Ukraine have enacted a 72-hour temporary truce for the duration of the US envoys’ visits, specifically halting airstrikes on each other’s capitals, Kyiv and Moscow. The halt in strikes began at midnight on Friday into Saturday and will last for the duration of the weekend of diplomacy.

The truce applies only to the two capital cities, and overnight attacks into Sunday saw Russia continue its bombardment of Ukraine while avoiding Kyiv city. According to Ukraine’s Air Force, Russian forces launched 108 Shahed-type drones fired from Russia, while at least three people were killed in the latest strikes and infrastructure was hit in Kyiv region.

Russian airstrikes were recorded in 11 locations across Ukraine, while a large-scale fire has been extinguished at an infrastructure facility in Kyiv region as a result of a Russian strike.

In total, 10 Ukrainian civilians have been killed over the past 24 hours, and a further 65 injured.

Witkoff and Kushner began their whirlwind weekend of diplomacy with a three-hour meeting with Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday afternoon. The negotiations were followed by dinner with the Russian leader, according to a Kremlin press briefing.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov later described the talks as “useful” and said the American representatives had “prepared seriously for this trip.” He said the US team expressed interest in ending hostilities as quickly as possible and offered “a whole series of considerations regarding possible paths to a settlement.”

A White House official said both sides “discussed substantive plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks.”

World.title: The world is about to meet Apple’s new CEO. Here are his biggest challenges
World.content:
When Apple holds its annual iPhone event on September 9, it’ll be the first time in more than a decade that Tim Cook won’t introduce the company’s latest products.

Instead, John Ternus will debut as Apple’s new chief executive during the company’s most important event of the year.

Expectations are high. Ternus takes over as Apple faces pressure to evolve its products for the AI era. In July, the iPhone maker became the second company in history to reach a $5 trillion market capitalization, raising the bar for what analysts and investors expect from product advancements and financial performance.

Ternus’ background in hardware engineering led many to believe his tenure is likely to usher in a new age of innovation for Apple. Many will be watching for signals of Ternus’ vision this week, especially as the company is expected to follow rivals into a new product category with a foldable iPhone.

Ternus will need to quickly cement his direction for Apple beyond the fanfare of this week’s event. The company faces a string of pressing challenges, including regulatory obstacles in Europe and a memory shortage.

Apple’s AI troubles

Ternus’s engineering experience could be a big advantage for Apple, which has suffered criticism over its approach for the last two years.

Last year, the company delayed a new version of Siri that is now set to launch this fall.

“It was a huge miss,” Gene Munster, managing partner for tech investment firm Deepwater Asset Management. “Thankfully, they’re on the right path, but it could have been so much bigger of a win for them.”

The Apple Siri prompt bubble on an iPhone arranged in February. The iPhone marker delayed a new version of Siri until this fall. Jason Henry/Bloomberg/Getty Images

Apple often tailors its devices and chips for its own services and software, and Ternus’ deep background in hardware could be critical in designing new devices that are optimized for AI.

In the near term, Apple is banking on Siri to help gain ground in the AI race. The revamped AI assistant will leverage data – like text messages and photos – from a user’s iPhone to answer questions in a personalized way. For example, you could ask Siri to reference your text messages to find your upcoming doctor’s appointment or dinner reservation.

Apple says the new Siri will be able to complete tasks in certain apps and answer questions about what’s shown on screen, a feature that could help it catch up to Google’s Gemini.

Nabila Popal, a senior director for tech market research firm International Data Corporation, told CNN that two things could give Apple an edge: its traditional focus on user privacy as well as the way it incorporates AI directly into iOS tools like the camera and messages apps.

“(Consumers) just want a device that makes their life easier and takes it to the next level, and I think that’s what Apple will do,” Popal said.

Then-Apple CEO Tim Cook on March 21, 2016, in Cupertino, California. Apple reached a larger-than-live valuation of $5 trillion in the Cook era. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

Pressure to deliver hit products

More than anything else, all eyes will be on Ternus to deliver a new blockbuster hit.

Cook will be remembered for scaling the iPhone to a business that rakes in hundreds of billions of dollars every year. By launching a web of services and accessories, such as Apple Music, the Apple Card, the Apple Watch and AirPods, Cook made the iPhone feel essential to everyday life.

Yet investors and analysts are hopeful that Ternus’ will bring a fresh push into new products, such as the foldable iPhone. The IDC projects that Apple will capture 40% of the market for foldable phones by 2027, despite being years behind rivals Samsung and Chinese smartphone giant Huawei.

“Apple’s entry into the foldable market has done more than reignite growth in a category that was losing momentum,” Popal wrote in a recent IDC report, ahead of the foldable iPhone’s release. “It has fundamentally altered the market’s trajectory.”

Memory shortage

The tech industry has been rattled by an ongoing shortage of memory, critical hardware that devices need to quickly retrieve stored information. Data centers have led to a surge in demand for these components, making them significantly more expensive.

That’s caused tech companies like Apple, Nintendo and Microsoft to raise prices of their products. Apple in July increased prices for iPads, Macs and other devices but left iPhone price tags unchanged.

“We’re in what I would characterize as a 100-year flood on memory pricing, with exponential increases in memory prices,” Cook said during his last earnings call as CEO in July.

The iPhone 17 series is displayed at an Apple Store in New York City on September 19, 2025. Shannon Stapleton/Reuters

Consumers should brace for higher iPhone prices, some analysts say.

Mike Howard, vice president of memory coverage at research firm TechInsights. estimates Apple would likely have to increase its smartphone prices by about $250 to $300 to maintain margins.

“We should start thinking about a $1,500 iPhone instead of a $1,000 (or) $1,200 iPhone,” he told CNN in July.

European regulation

Apple likely has more obstacles ahead in the European Union’s crackdown on Big Tech.

The company recently announced changes to its App Store’s business terms to comply with EU regulations. And it won’t launch the new version of Siri on iPhones and iPads in the European Union because of the European Commission’s rules. Europe is Apple’s second-largest market after the United States.

The EC wants Apple and Google to give third-party AI assistants more access to iOS and Android systems. But Apple and Google have both argued that doing so would raise privacy concerns.

An Apple Store in Madrid, Spain, on October 30, 2025. Mateusz Wlodarczyk/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

And experts agree that consumers should be careful about giving AI agents broad access to content stored on their phones and computers.

An AI agent “could exercise the user’s delegated authority to do other things that maybe the user might not have wanted it to happen,” Michael Stokes, senior vice president of emerging technologies at Veilant, a company that sells secure infrastructure and communications products, previously told CNN.

But the EC allows companies like Apple to “implement appropriate privacy, security and integrity safeguards,” a spokesperson previously told CNN.

Ultimately, Ternus will have to navigate these challenges while living up to the larger-than-life valuation Apple reached in the Cook era.

“Apple is already so large, profitable, and deeply embedded in its customers’ lives that incremental excellence may no longer be enough to redefine the company,” Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan wrote in an August research note. “Ternus’s challenge will be to preserve the profitable machine Cook built while restoring a stronger sense of technological surprise.”

World.title: Egypt and seven key allies condemn Israeli ministers’ Gaza displacement proposals
World.content:
Foreign ministers from Egypt, Qatar, Jordan, the UAE, Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia issued a joint statement condemning comments made by Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Defense Minister Israel Katz regarding the displacement of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip.

The ministers denounced proposed plans and mechanisms aimed at forcibly removing Palestinians from their land, characterizing the provocative statements as a blatant violation of international humanitarian law, and a direct threat to the legitimate, inalienable rights of the Palestinian people.

In their unified declaration, the diplomats emphasized their absolute rejection and condemnation of any attempts or plans targeting the displacement of Palestinians—whether within or outside the occupied Palestinian territory—under any pretext.

Foreign ministers from eight nations warned of severe consequences if calls for forced displacement are translated into declared policies or actionable measures aimed at uprooting Palestinians from their land.

The ministers stated that such actions present a direct challenge to international peace efforts—most notably President Donald Trump’s comprehensive plan to end the conflict in Gaza, which includes an absolute rejection of forced displacement.

They added that these measures carry grave risks capable of undermining regional stability.

World.title: Sisi follows up on efforts to revive Cairo’s Islamic and historical landmarks
World.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi urged the relevant state agencies to continue their efforts to revitalize Cairo’s various historical and heritage landmarks and develop the surrounding areas to attract more tourists.

Sisi emphasized the importance of adopting the “greening Cairo” project, which aims to transform any vacated land into green spaces.

This came during a meeting between Sisi and Minister of Religious Endowments Osama al-Azhari, Cairo Governor Ibrahim Saber, Advisor to the President for Urban Planning, Amir Sayed Ahmed,and the Head of the Armed Forces Engineering Authority, Walid Aref.

Presidential Spokesperson Mohamed al-Shenawy said that the President followed up during the meeting on efforts to revitalize Cairo’s Islamic and historical landmarks.

The official spokesperson added that the Governor of Cairo highlighted the efforts to revitalize numerous Khedival, historical, and Islamic landmarks in Cairo, as well as the ongoing rehabilitation and development of infrastructure in and around historical areas.

The Minister of Religious Endowments reviewed the progress of the restoration and revitalization of several historical mosques and shrines, noting that these efforts extend to the development of more integrated tourist routes connecting various historical and heritage sites.

He continued that upon completion of all the ongoing work related to the revitalization of historical landmarks, the “heart of Cairo” will become an open-air tourist destination, attracting even more visitors.

World.title: The downfall of Sarah Khalifa – from TV host to death row
World.content:
She used to grace TV screens across Egypt – now she’s been sentenced to death.

Sarah Khalifa’s journey spanned many years, beginning with media appearances and program hosting, progressing through production, event organization, and private projects.

But a catastrophic downfall led to her conviction in one of the largest drug manufacturing and trafficking cases Cairo’s courts had ever witnessed.

Cairo Criminal Court, convened at the Fifth Settlement Court Complex, concluded the “Grand Drug Case” on Saturday September 5.

The court sentenced Khalifa and 11 other defendants to death by hanging, fining each of them LE500,000, and confiscating the seized drugs, cars, equipment, gold jewelry, and mobile phones.

The verdict was unanimous after the defendant case files were referred to the Grand Mufti of Egypt for his religious opinion.

TV Presenter

Khalifa was born in Cairo on March 29, 1994, and began her career in the media by presenting programs on the “ART” channel, before moving to work on the Iraqi Al-Sharqiya channel for a long period.

Over time, she moved into production and event planning, launching her own company, “Sarah Production,” specializing in organizing parties.

She also participated in numerous events and artistic performances, expanding her presence on social media.

In 2024, she returned to the spotlight with the program “Sarah and Beka,” which she co-hosted with the popular singer Hamo Beka.

She also performed in Dubai and opened a beauty clinic in Agouza district, Giza, becoming a well-known figure on social media and among celebrities.

Downfall

In April 2025, Khalifa’s life took a shocking turn when security forces arrested her.

The New Cairo Public Prosecution began investigating her on charges related to possession of narcotics with intent to distribute.

At the start of the investigation, the prosecution ordered the summoning of witnesses and the review of surveillance camera footage from the vicinity of her residence to determine the movements of those frequenting the area, before expanding the investigation into the case.

Security services had been monitoring the group’s activities for approximately 40 days before obtaining an arrest warrant for the defendants on April 17, 2025.

The investigation revealed that Khalifa was leading the group, with the assistance of her brother and others, and that raw materials were being brought in from abroad before being smuggled into Egypt to manufacture and distribute narcotics.

The Trial

The case grew to become one of the largest drug cases in the nation, with the Public Prosecution referring 28 defendants to the Criminal Court.

The prosecution charged the defendants with forming an organized criminal group specializing in importing, manufacturing, packaging, trafficking, and distributing materials used in the production of synthetic narcotics, as well as possessing and carrying unlicensed firearms and ammunition.

Investigations revealed the seizure of more than 750 kilograms of synthetic narcotics and raw materials used in their production, along with weapons and ammunition.

The referral order was based on the testimonies of 20 witnesses and technical and digital evidence, including conversations, photos, and videos.

The trial of Khalifa and 27 other defendants began before the Cairo Criminal Court.

The case continued for months, with legal arguments from the defense focusing on the arrest and search procedures, the evidence presented, and the extent to which the elements of the crimes attributed to each defendant were met.

During the trial sessions, some defense lawyers maintained their clients’ innocence, arguing the invalidity of the arrest and detention procedures, the lack of connection between some of the defendants and the seized items, and the admissibility of the forensic evidence and investigations.

Referral to Grand Mufti

On August 4, The Cairo Criminal Court referred the case files of Sarah Khalifa and 12 other defendants to the Grand Mufti of Egypt for his religious opinion on the death penalty.

Death Sentence

The Cairo Criminal Court ultimately sentenced Khalifa and 11 other defendants to death by hanging.

The court also sentenced nine defendants to life imprisonment and a fine of LE 100,000 each, while acquitting seven others, bringing the total number of defendants in the case to 28.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Mohamed Salah in court over former lawyer’s fees
World.content:
The New Cairo Court will hold its first hearing on Sunday in the lawsuit filed by Amr Faragallah, Mohamed Salah’s former lawyer, demanding payment for legal and administrative services he claims to have provided to the player.

Salah in Court

The court scheduled Sunday’s hearing for Salah to appear in person and take the oath, the wording of which was determined.

The oath includes a denial that the former lawyer performed the services in question or that the player owes him any money.

Effect of Absence

The court clarified that Salah’s failure to appear, or his refusal to take the oath without a valid excuse, constitutes a breach of oath and entails the legal consequences stipulated by law.

Official Proxy

The details of the lawsuit date back to September 2015, where the former lawyer bases his claim on an official power of attorney issued to him by Mohamed Salah in 2012.

He is demanding financial compensation for legal and administrative work he claims to have performed on behalf of the player.

World.title: Liberia: What Comes Next for Jewel Howard-Taylor
World.content:
MONROVIA – Eleven days after she was led into Monrovia Central Prison, Jewel Howard-Taylor went home on Thursday — but not to freedom. Under an order signed by Criminal Court “C” Judge Ousman F. Feika, the woman who once stood a heartbeat from the Liberian presidency now lives under a regime nearly as controlled as the one she left. A single-family caregiver has been designated to look after her. Police are posted at the gate around the clock. A visitor’s log, modeled on the one the Bureau of Corrections keeps at the Central Prison, tracks everyone who comes and goes. She cannot step outside the compound on Tubman Boulevard in Sinkor without the court’s advance approval — and even then, only for a hospital appointment.

By Rodney D. Sieh, [email protected]

It is not vindication, and Judge Feika was careful to say so. The order releasing Howard-Taylor from pre-trial detention on medical grounds does not touch the case underneath it. Liberia’s first and only female vice president still faces trafficking, money-laundering and conspiracy charges connected to what prosecutors have called the largest cocaine seizure in the country’s history. What changed this week is where she waits for trial, not what she will have to answer when it begins.

HOW THE CASE REACHED THIS POINT

The case traces back to July 21, 2026, when Liberian authorities intercepted nearly four metric tons of cocaine in Duazon, east of Monrovia — a haul officials valued at roughly $317 million and described as one of the largest narcotics seizures in the country’s history. It followed a smaller but still significant bust in June, when 237.6 kilograms of cocaine worth more than $19 million was seized at Roberts International Airport. Taken together, investigators say, the two seizures pointed to a sustained trafficking corridor running through Liberia — consistent with warnings from the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime that West Africa has become a key transit route for South American cocaine bound for European markets. The July bust also implicated senior police and intelligence officials, widening the investigation well beyond the traffickers caught with the drugs.

Howard-Taylor was arrested on August 19 at Roberts International Airport. Her lawyers say she was intercepted while on her way to meet them, despite having agreed to report voluntarily to police headquarters — a procedural grievance that has since become part of her defense. A magistrate at the Monrovia City Court initially handled her first appearance, but on August 26, Stipendiary Magistrate Ben Barco ruled that his court had no authority over charges this serious and denied her request for humanitarian home confinement, finding medical assessments showed her “sufficiently stable” to remain in custody. She was transferred to Monrovia Central Prison. Her defense team then carried the fight to Criminal Court “C”, the tribunal with jurisdiction over major felonies, where a preliminary examination opened in early September — pushed back a day at the defense’s request so she could be seen by her personal physician. Days later, Judge Feika granted the compassionate release that now has her under house arrest rather than behind prison walls.

AT A GLANCE — CONDITIONS OF RELEASE

Travel documents surrendered to the Sheriff of the Court immediately upon release.

Confined to her Tubman Boulevard residence in Sinkor, under a single court-approved family caregiver.

Access limited to Howard-Taylor, her caregiver and her physician or physician’s assistant.

A visitor-logging system modeled on the Bureau of Corrections’ protocol at Monrovia Central Prison.

No movement outside the residence except by court order or for an approved medical appointment.

Round-the-clock security or police protection maintained at the residence, with a full visitor log kept on hand.

WHO IS JEWEL HOWARD-TAYLOR

Long before this case, Howard-Taylor had one of the more unusual résumés in Liberian politics. Born in Zorzor in 1963, she married Charles Taylor in 1997 and served as First Lady during his presidency until 2003. She later earned a law degree from the University of Liberia, was elected to the Senate representing Bong County in 2005 as a member of the National Patriotic Party, and chaired the Senate’s committee on health, gender and children’s affairs. In 2017, George Weah picked her as his running mate on the Coalition for Democratic Change ticket, and when the coalition won that December, she became Liberia’s first female vice president, serving from January 2018 until January 2024. More recently, she has clashed with the NPP’s current leadership over her endorsement choices in Liberian politics — friction her supporters now point to as part of the backdrop for a prosecution she calls politically motivated.

THE CASE PROSECUTORS SAY THEY HAVE

According to the writ of arrest, dated August 25 and signed by Clerk of Court Abel Kalay, the state’s narrative begins in 2021, when a man named Sheikh Bashiru Kante allegedly brought two foreign nationals — Taras Zadereiko, a Ukrainian known as “Tony,” and Mihovil Vrovac, a Croatian known as “Michael” — into Liberia to establish a cocaine pipeline between West Africa and Europe. The following year, Kante is accused of introducing the pair to Howard-Taylor at her residence in Congo Town, after which she was allegedly invited to Dubai to meet Nikola Ivancic, a Croatian the writ describes as the ring’s leader. There, prosecutors allege, she received $45,000 in cash. Investigators say further payments followed — $75,000 funneled through the Jewel Star Fish Foundation, a nonprofit associated with her name, and an additional $15,000 delivered through Kante as recently as this past August. On those allegations, she has been charged with importation and exportation of controlled drugs, unlicensed trafficking, criminal conspiracy, facilitation, solicitation and money laundering. Ivancic, Vrovac and Zadereiko have all been charged in absentia; none is currently in Liberian custody. Howard-Taylor and her attorneys — Laveli Supuwood, Kabineh Ja’neh and Finley Y. Karngar — have denied every allegation.

WHERE THE GOVERNMENT’S CASE LOOKS STRONG

Prosecutors are not starting from an informant’s tip; they are starting from four tons of cocaine physically seized and forensically verifiable, which gives the broader investigation a foundation that does not depend on anyone’s credibility. The alleged financial trail is also, in principle, the kind of evidence that outlasts witnesses: if the $75,000 said to have moved through the Jewel Star Fish Foundation left a documentary record — bank deposits, wire transfers, foundation filings — that evidence can be examined independently of what any single witness says on the stand, and money moved through a registered nonprofit is a classic and traceable laundering pattern once investigators have the paperwork. The case also has genuine international reach: two people were captured at the scene of the July seizure carrying Spanish-Colombian and Serbian passports, and three more suspects tied to the alleged Liberia-to-Europe pipeline are Croatian and Ukrainian nationals — a spread that has already drawn the attention of transnational-crime watchdogs and gives Liberian investigators avenues to seek corroboration, such as banking or travel records, from foreign counterparts that a purely domestic case would not have.

WHERE THE GOVERNMENT’S CASE LOOKS SHAKY

The prosecution’s most serious structural weakness is that its alleged ringleader and two of the alleged cash conduits — Ivancic, Vrovac and Zadereiko — are being charged in absentia and are not in Liberian custody. That means the version of events tying Howard-Taylor to a Dubai cash handoff and a foreign trafficking ring rest, for now, on the writ’s narrative and on Kante as the connecting figure, rather than on live testimony from the men prosecutors say ran the operation and paid her. Her lawyers have already signaled how they intend to attack that gap: they argue that meeting foreign businesspeople and traveling abroad were the ordinary furniture of high office, and that a writ describing contacts made “as part of her constitutional responsibilities” does not, by itself, establish criminal intent. The case has also stumbled procedurally in ways that hand the defense real ammunition — an initial prosecution at a court later found to lack jurisdiction, a magistrate’s ruling reversed only after Howard-Taylor was sent to Central Prison, and her lawyers’ still-unresolved claim that she was intercepted en route to meet counsel rather than formally summoned. Her legal team has separately alleged, without offering documentation, that government actors might manipulate audio or video evidence using artificial intelligence — an unproven claim, but one that puts prosecutors on notice that any recorded evidence they introduce will be contested on authenticity, not just content. And the timing lands amid a real rupture between Howard-Taylor and the National Patriotic Party’s current leadership over her recent political endorsements, which gives her camp a ready-made political-persecution narrative that will need to be answered with evidence in a courtroom, not simply asserted in the press.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

The house-arrest order is not the end of anything; it is a pause inside a case that is still being built. A grand jury term is expected later this month, and it is the grand jury’s indictment — not Thursday’s ruling — that will determine whether the charges against Howard-Taylor formally proceed to trial. Judge Feika still has a stack of preliminary motions to rule on, including defense requests to quash the arrest writ, a habeas corpus petition, a bail motion despite prosecutors’ argument that the charges are non-bailable, and a motion to suppress evidence. Until those questions are resolved, Howard-Taylor remains, in effect, a prisoner of her own address: watched around the clock, barred from travel, and permitted outside her gate only for the medical care that got her out of Central Prison in the first place.

However, the case resolves, it has already become a test of more than one defendant’s guilt. It is a test of whether Liberia’s judiciary can handle a politically connected defendant the same way it would handle anyone else, at a moment when the underlying seizure has implicated police and intelligence officials of its own. And it is a test, watched well beyond Liberia’s borders, of whether a small West African state sitting astride a major cocaine corridor can make a trafficking case against a former head of the executive branch stick — not just on the strength of a writ, but on evidence that survives cross-examination once the grand jury term begins.

World.title: Liberia: Gongloe Demands Disclosure of President’s Pay, Questions 40% Salary Cut, Constitutional Compliance
World.content:
Monrovia — Renowned Liberian lawyer Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe has challenged President Joseph Nyuma Boakai to publicly disclose his salary, raising questions about the legal basis, implementation, and transparency surrounding the President’s reported 40 percent voluntary pay reduction.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh, [email protected]

President Boakai pledged during his campaign and upon assuming office to reduce his salary by 40 percent as part of his commitment to responsible governance and fiscal discipline. The Executive Mansion has subsequently maintained that the President is honoring that commitment.

However, the actual amount President Boakai receives monthly or annually has not been publicly disclosed, prompting Cllr. Gongloe to demand clarity on what he describes as a fundamental transparency issue.

In his latest “Question for the Weekend” commentary, titled “Mr. President, What Exactly Is Your Salary?”, Gongloe said the reported 40 percent reduction raises a basic question: 40 percent of what?

“Liberians were told that President Joseph Nyuma Boakai voluntarily reduced his salary by 40%. But 40% of what?” Gongloe asked.

He pointed to Article 60 of the Liberian Constitution, which provides that the salaries of the President and Vice President are determined by the Legislature and shall neither be increased nor diminished during the term for which they were elected.

Against that constitutional provision, Gongloe is asking the administration to explain the exact salary legally established for the President and how the announced voluntary reduction is being applied.

He posed four specific questions: What salary did the Legislature legally fix for the President? What was President Boakai’s gross annual salary when he assumed office? How much does he actually receive after the announced 40 percent voluntary reduction? How is the voluntary reduction being implemented consistently with Article 60 of the Constitution?

Gongloe also invoked Article 15(c) of the Constitution, which guarantees citizens the right to be informed about the government and its functionaries.

He argued that disclosure of the President’s compensation should not be viewed through a partisan or personal lens, but rather as an issue of public accountability.

“This is not a personal question. It is not a partisan question. It is a transparency question,” Gongloe stated.

The lawyer stressed that the President’s compensation is ultimately financed by Liberian taxpayers and therefore, in his view, the public has a legitimate interest in knowing precisely how much the country’s chief executive is receiving.

“Mr. President, the Liberian people pay the President’s salary,” Gongloe said. “How much are they paying you?”

The call comes amid broader public debates over government spending, executive accountability and the need for greater transparency in the management of public resources.

Gongloe ran on the presidential ticket of the Liberian People’s Party in the 2023 presidential and legislative elections. He and the LPP subsequently threw their support behind then-presidential candidate Joseph Nyuma Boakai during the 2023 runoff election between Boakai and incumbent President George Manneh Weah.

Although Gongloe was offered a cabinet position in the Boakai-Koung administration, he declined the appointment. His vice-presidential running mate, Dr. Emmanuel Urey Yarkpawolo, was later appointed Executive Director of the Environmental Protection Agency.

Gongloe has, however, maintained an independent public posture toward the administration. While applauding the government for what he considers notable achievements, he has also consistently criticized policies and decisions he believes require greater transparency and accountability.

He said his latest inquiry into President Boakai’s salary should therefore not be viewed through a partisan lens, emphasizing that his concern is rooted in the broader principles of transparency, accountability and the public’s right to know.

According to Gongloe, his past political support for Boakai does not prevent him from questioning the administration when issues of public interest arise. His call for disclosure of the President’s salary, he stressed, is intended to promote openness in government and ensure that public officials remain accountable to the Liberian people.

While the Executive Mansion has maintained that President Boakai has fulfilled his pledge to cut his salary by 40 percent, the renewed challenge from Gongloe puts the spotlight on the actual monetary value of the reduction and the mechanism through which it is being implemented.

The questions now place the administration under pressure to provide a clear public accounting of the President’s legally established compensation, the amount he receives, and how the reported salary reduction squares with the constitutional provisions governing presidential remuneration.

For Gongloe, the issue is straightforward: if the public pays the President’s salary, the public should know exactly how much it is.

World.title: Liberia: Weah’s Opposition Unity Roundtable Kicks Off As Concerned NPP Partisans, Sen. Kogar Endorse Initiative
World.content:
Monrovia — Former President George Manneh Weah’s push for opposition unity is gaining momentum, with a group identifying itself as the Concerned NPP Partisans endorsing a consultative meeting convened by the Congress for Democratic Change despite National Patriotic Party Chairman George Mulbah’s position that the party will not attend.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh, [email protected]

The development adds a new layer to an emerging disagreement within the NPP over whether the party should participate in broader opposition consultations ahead of Liberia’s next political cycle.

Former President Weah, following his return from abroad, criticized what he described as the deterioration of democracy under the Boakai-Koung administration and announced plans to bring opposition political forces together for consultations.

Several opposition parties and political figures have since expressed interest in the initiative.

However, NPP Chairman George Mulbah has publicly stated that the party will not honor the invitation.

The NPP’s political leader, former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor, served alongside Weah during his administration. Against the backdrop of the party’s leadership dispute, the Concerned NPP Partisans have now publicly thrown their support behind the CDC-led consultations.

In a statement issued Saturday, the group, which describes itself as comprising a majority of members of the NPP’s National Executive Committee, said it supports “genuine unity” among Liberia’s opposition political forces and fully endorses the consultative meeting.

“The opposition cannot afford unnecessary division, personal ambitions, or attempts by individuals to speak as though they alone represent the collective interests of the NPP,” the group said.

‘NPP Is Bigger Than Any Individual’

The Concerned NPP Partisans directly challenged Chairman Mulbah’s position, arguing that no single individual should claim to speak for the entire party.

They also questioned Mulbah’s role in the political negotiations and coalition-building efforts that led to the formation of the Coalition for Democratic Change, which included the NPP and ultimately brought Weah to power in 2017.

The group said Mulbah joined the NPP at a later stage and was subsequently appointed to a government position by then-President Weah.

The statement accused him of attempting to undermine political relationships and forces that, according to the group, contributed to his political resurgence.

“The NPP is bigger than any individual. The opposition movement is bigger than personal interests,” the group declared.

Concerned Partisans Praise CDC

The group also commended the CDC and former President Weah for what it described as solidarity with the NPP and its leadership during what it called an “exceptionally difficult period.”

The Concerned NPP Partisans said Liberia’s political environment requires dialogue, consultation and cooperation among opposition parties.

“No single opposition political party can afford to approach the future in isolation,” the statement said, urging political leaders to sit together, negotiate in good faith and work toward a broad-based opposition platform capable of presenting Liberians with a credible alternative.

The group further expressed appreciation to Weah and the CDC for maintaining their relationship with the NPP despite the challenges confronting the party.

Jewel Howard-Taylor’s Situation

The statement also addressed the current challenges facing former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor, who has recently been at the center of a major legal and political controversy.

The Concerned NPP Partisans said some individuals within the NPP had contributed to the difficulties confronting Howard-Taylor and warned that history would judge those involved.

“We will not be distracted by those who have chosen to become the ‘Judas Iscariots’ of this moment,” the group said, while urging NPP partisans and opposition supporters to remain calm and united.

The group concluded by reaffirming its commitment to opposition unity and democratic principles.

Round One of Opposition Talks Held

Meanwhile, the first round of the opposition consultative meeting was held Saturday at Weah’s Jamaica Resort in Paynesville.

Several opposition political figures attended the gathering, which is expected to continue today.

Among the notable participants was Senator Samuel G. Kogar, who was recently expelled from the Movement for Democracy and Reconstruction (MDR).

The MDR was a key member of the Unity Party Alliance during the 2023 presidential election, which brought President Joseph Nyuma Boakai and Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung to power after their victory over Weah and his running mate, then VP Taylor, in the runoff.

More opposition leaders are expected to participate as consultations continue, with the talks likely to test the willingness of Liberia’s opposition parties to overcome longstanding political differences and pursue a common strategy.

World.title: Liberia: Vice President Koung’s ‘Godfather’ Remark Puts Senator Moye’s Political Influence in Bong County in Spotlight
World.content:
GBARNGA, Bong County — Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung has sparked fresh discussion about the political influence of Bong County Senator Prince Kermue Moye after publicly referring to him as the county’s “Political Godfather.”

Vice President Koung made the remark Saturday at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Far East Community Women Center in Gbarnga, where scores of women and community residents gathered to witness the launch of the facility.

During his remarks, the Vice President turned his attention to Senator Moye and declared: “I want to recognize Senator Prince Moye, the political Godfather of Bong County.”

The statement immediately generated excitement among women attending the program, with several applauding and expressing satisfaction over the Vice President’s public acknowledgment of Senator Moye’s political stature.

For some of the women, Vice President Koung’s description amounted to a significant endorsement of a politician they believe has established a strong connection with communities throughout the county.

One woman said the Vice President’s recognition was particularly important because it came from a senior member of the national government.

“We were very happy when the Vice President made that statement,” she said. “It shows that the work and influence of Senator Moye are being recognized beyond his immediate supporters. When someone of the Vice President’s position calls him the political Godfather, people will naturally pay attention.”

Another woman, Hajah Swaray, said the declaration reflected what she described as Moye’s longstanding political relevance in Bong County. “For us, this was not an ordinary statement,” she said. “Senator Moye has built relationships with people, and his name is known in communities across Bong. We appreciate Vice President Koung for recognizing his place in the political affairs of this county.”

Fanta Kromah, anotyher woman, linked the Vice President’s comments to the senator’s engagement with ordinary residents, particularly women and community groups.

“We welcomed the Vice President’s words because Senator Moye has continued to interact with the people,” she said. “Women want leaders who listen to them and understand their challenges. Hearing him recognized in such a manner made many of us proud.”

Another attendee said the reaction from the women demonstrated how strongly the senator’s supporters identify with his political leadership.

“You could see the excitement when the Vice President called Senator Moye the political Godfather,” she said. “The women applauded because they felt that someone at the national level had acknowledged what they have seen in Bong County. It was a moment of recognition for Senator Moye.”

Kula Bility said the title should not merely be celebrated as a political compliment but should also inspire greater responsibility from the senator.

“We appreciate Vice President Koung for recognizing Senator Moye, but recognition also comes with responsibility,” she said. “If he is being described as the political Godfather of Bong County, we expect him to continue standing with the people and supporting programs that benefit women, young people and communities.”

The groundbreaking ceremony itself was centered on the establishment of the Far East Community Women Center, an initiative expected to provide women in the community with a dedicated venue for meetings, organization and other activities.

The gathering consequently brought together community members and women leaders around an initiative focused on strengthening community participation and providing a space for women.

However, Vice President Koung’s unexpected political characterization of Senator Moye became a major talking point during and after the ceremony.

The phrase “Political Godfather of Bong County” quickly drew attention because of the weight attached to the description in Liberia’s political environment, where such titles are often associated with influence, networks and the ability to mobilize political support.

Vice President Koung did not elaborate extensively on the basis for the characterization during his remarks, but his public recognition of Moye placed the senator at the center of political discussion surrounding the event.

The women who reacted to the statement said they interpreted it as an acknowledgment of Moye’s influence and his relationship with constituents and community stakeholders.

They also expressed appreciation for the Vice President’s decision to make the recognition publicly rather than privately, saying the declaration gave greater visibility to what they consider Moye’s political contribution to Bong County.

Beyond the political symbolism, the event remained focused on the proposed women’s center, with participants emphasizing the importance of creating opportunities and spaces where women can organize and participate in community development.

For the women present, however, Saturday’s ceremony produced a second significant message: the public elevation of Senator Moye’s political profile by one of Liberia’s highest-ranking government officials.

Koung’s description has now added a new phrase to the political conversation surrounding Moye, as supporters and community members weigh the significance of being publicly identified as the “Political Godfather of Bong County.”

World.title: Liberia: Supreme Court Vindicates Labour Minister Kruah, Dismisses Ethical Breach Complaint
World.content:
Monrovia — The Supreme Court of Liberia has dismissed a long-running complaint against Labour Minister Cllr. Cooper W. Kruah, Sr., clearing him of allegations that he violated professional and ethical rules in his dealings with the Mano River Agricultural Rehabilitation Development Corporation (MARDCO).

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

The ruling, handed down by the Supreme Court’s Full Bench during its March Term 2026, brings an end to a legal dispute dating back to 2014.

According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Labour and signed by Acting Director of Communications and Public Affairs E. Frederick Baye, the complaint was filed by Edgar Sydney, Chief Executive Officer of MARDCO, against the Henries Law Firm, which was then headed by Kruah.

Sydney had accused Kruah of an ethical breach arising from legal services provided by the law firm to MARDCO. Kruah consistently denied wrongdoing, maintaining that monies received in connection with the matter were handled in the course of his professional responsibilities.

The Ministry said the Judicial Ethics and Grievance Committee previously investigated the complaint and found insufficient grounds to sustain the allegations. Sydney subsequently sought review by the Supreme Court.

In its opinion and ruling dated August 27, 2026, the Supreme Court upheld the findings of the Grievance and Ethics Committee, concluding that there was insufficient evidence to establish that Kruah had violated professional conduct rules governing the handling of client funds.

The Court acknowledged that monies connected to execution proceedings had passed through Kruah’s hands, but noted that he maintained the funds were either delivered to the complainant or represented payments associated with legal representation.

The Court stated that there was “no sufficient evidentiary basis” to conclude that Kruah violated Rule 15, which prohibits attorneys from commingling client funds with personal funds or using client funds for personal benefit.

The Supreme Court further clarified that a dispute between an attorney and client over monies collected, legal fees or the adequacy of an accounting does not, by itself, establish conversion, misappropriation, commingling or personal use of client funds.

“Wherefore and in view of the foregoing,” the Court concluded, “the complaint is hereby dismissed.”

The Clerk of Court was ordered to notify the parties, with the ruling formally entered by the Full Bench.

The Labour Ministry welcomed the decision as a vindication of Kruah, who, throughout the proceedings, maintained that the allegations were unfounded and that his actions were undertaken in fulfillment of his professional obligations.

The Ministry also linked the case to what it described as a sustained campaign by political detractors against Kruah, particularly during the early period of the Boakai-Koung administration, when he was reportedly considered for appointment as Minister of Justice.

Kruah currently serves as Minister of Labour and is National Chairman of the Movement for Democracy and Reconciliation (MDR), a political organization founded by the late Nimba County Senator Prince Y. Johnson.

The Supreme Court’s dismissal formally closes the ethical complaint that has remained unresolved for more than a decade.

World.title: Give the LACC Its Day in Court
World.content:
A prosecutor who asks three times for a trial date and never gets one is not the problem with Liberia’s fight against corruption. A docket that lets that happen is.

THERE IS A VERSION of this newspaper’s argument that would be easy to dismiss: that Liberia’s courts are conspiring to protect the powerful from the Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission. We are not making that argument, and the record, as best we can tell, does not support it. What the record does support is narrower and, in some ways, more troubling: that it no longer seems to matter whether the LACC does everything right. The outcome is the same either way.



CONSIDER THE CASE this paper detailed this week out of Margibi County. Prosecutors did not sit on their hands. They asked, in writing, for a trial date in May 2026. They asked again two weeks later. When the case was reassigned to a new judge, they asked a third time, in August. Three requests, three separate points on the calendar, and still no trial — not because a witness failed to appear, not because evidence was incomplete, but because the docket never made room. Now the defense wants the case thrown out entirely, under a law written to punish exactly the kind of foot-dragging that, in this instance, the paper trail shows the prosecution did not do.

A JUSTICE SYSTEM THAT CANNOT tell the difference between a prosecutor who asked and a prosecutor who didn’t is not neutral. It is broken in a way that happens to favor whoever is charged.

THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF. Corruption cases against former NOCAL chief Rustolyn Suacoco Dennis and former Bureau of State Enterprises head Arthur Massaquoi both went the same way — dismissed after sitting for terms at a time while the court’s attention went elsewhere. Add the Margibi case, and what looked like an unfortunate pattern starts to look like a design flaw. Liberia’s Criminal Procedure Law gives defendants a real and necessary protection: if the state doesn’t bring you to trial by the next court term, absent good cause, the case gets dismissed. That protection exists so people are not left to rot under an accusation indefinitely. It was never meant to be a technicality that rewards a court’s own scheduling failures at the expense of the public’s interest in seeing corruption prosecuted.

THE COST NOBODY IS COUNTING



EVERY DISMISSED CORRUPTION case is not a wash. It is a loss. Behind every indictment the LACC secures are months of forensic accounting, subpoenaed bank records, witness interviews and legal drafting, performed by an agency that does not have unlimited money or unlimited staff. When a case dies for lack of a docket slot, the state does not get that investment back for free. It either lets a serious corruption case disappear for good, or it asks an already-stretched commission to redo the work from scratch, against the same clock, in the same courts. Neither outcome serves the public that pays for the LACC’s work and is told, case after case, to wait for the accountability it was promised.



THERE IS ALSO A COST that will not show up in any LACC annual report: what the public concludes when it watches indictment after indictment vanish before a single witness is sworn in. Liberians do not need to believe in a conspiracy to lose faith that corruption prosecutions go anywhere. They only need to keep seeing this outcome. A court system does not have to intend to protect the well-connected for it to end up doing exactly that, term after term, simply by failing to prioritize.



WHAT THE COURTS OWE THE PROCESS



NOBODY IS ASKING judges to rubber-stamp the LACC or fast-track cases in a way that tramples a defendant’s rights. Due process cuts both ways, and it is not this paper’s place to prejudge any individual’s guilt, including in the Margibi case. But due process for the accused cannot be the only interest a court weighs when a docket fills up. The public has an interest in these cases too, and prosecutors who do their part — who file, who write, who ask, on the record, for a hearing — deserve a system that credits that effort rather than one that quietly erases it.



THAT MEANS LIBERIA’S circuit courts need an honest accounting of how corruption cases are prioritized against everything else competing for courtroom time, and it means the judiciary, the Ministry of Justice and the Legislature need to treat docket congestion as the structural crisis it has become rather than an excuse that arrives after the fact, case by case, dismissal by dismissal. A dedicated calendar for LACC prosecutions, firmer rules for how “good cause” gets weighed when the delay traces back to the court rather than the state, and basic transparency about why cases sit for terms at a time would cost far less than what Liberia is currently losing every time one of these cases dies untried.

THE LACC CANNOT do its job if the courts will not give its cases a trial date. That is not a defense of any defendant or any prosecutor. It is a minimum condition for an anti-corruption fight that Liberians have been promised for years and are still, mostly, waiting to see delivered. The courts do not have to decide anyone’s guilt to fix this. They only must decide that a case is worth trying.

World.title: Liberia: CDC, NPP Ties Rumbling as Word of War Ensues Between Top Executives Amid Call for Opposition Unity
World.content:
MONROVIA – As political actors are readying to get the stage set ahead of the 2029 Presidential and Legislative Elections, the call for unity is now at the forehead of the opposition bloc, but with only one of the key parties expressing critical view of how the arrangement is being done, and that’s the National Patriotic Party (NPP).

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

The NPP, a former ruling party and co-ruling establishment, declined endorsing the called opposition roundtable meeting convened by the Congress for Democratic Change (CDC).

The NPP’s response to the opposition gathering and reply from the CDC signals of a souring relationship between the two political allies.

NPP Not Respected

Atty. George Sylvester Mulbah, Chairman of the NPP; a party which led the country from 1997-2003 and then awarded the Vice President position from 2017-2023 in a similar arrangement of the Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC) government, contends that the party is not being accorded due respect in the process.

Mulbah asserted that the NPP is prepared to support a broader opposition alliance, provided the party receives respect and meaningful participation in the alliance’s decision-making process.

The NPP Chairman emphasized that his party is no longer willing to operate as a follower, insisting that it wants to play a significant role in shaping decisions within any opposition coalition.

While stating that NPP remains open to working with like-minded opposition parties, Chairman Mulbah warned that mutual respect would be critical to sustaining any political collaboration.

In the view of Atty. Mulbah, the manner and form the invitation was carved to the NPP angles on reducing the well-recognized political party to an “auxiliary” of another party for electoral purposes, alleging that it was the case of the previous collaboration with the CDC.

‘Sour Relationship’

During the reign of the CDC government, Atty. Mulbah averred that there was a sour or strained relationship between their political leader, former Vice President Jewel Howard Taylor and former President George Weah, something he narrated the VP for a protracted period of years in the leadership.

Unnecessary Grandstanding, Koijee Replies Mulbah

In an apparent move to “set the record straight,” the Secretary of the CDC, former Monrovia City Mayor Jefferson Tamba Koijee, dismissed claims by the NPP Chairman.

In a write-up on his Facebook page, the former Monrovia City Mayor clarified that at no time did the Congress for Democratic Change extend an invitation to the National Patriotic Party or its national leadership to participate in the proposed opposition roundtable discussion as claimed by its Chairman.

Koijee intoned that any announcement of rejecting an invitation that was never extended amounts to unnecessary grandstanding and political posturing.

For the avoidance of doubt, a few outstanding, uncompromising individual members of the NPP were invited in their individual capacities. Neither the NPP as an institution nor its National Chairman, Mr. George Mulbah, was invited.

“The National Chairman should therefore immediately cease and desist from creating the impression that the CDC sought the institutional participation of the NPP and was subsequently rejected,” writes the CDC SG.

CDC SG Raises Red Flag Of Mulbah’s Independence Over Alleged Employment With VP Koung

The CDC chief scribe alleged that the NPP Chairman is cut in the middle of neutrality on grounds that he is reportedly working in the office of Vice President Jeremiah Koung.

Based on the alleged employment with the Vice President, he questions the NPP Chairman’s independence, timing and motivation of statements directed against opposition solidarity.

“Even more troubling was the response of the NPP leadership when its own distinguished Standard Bearer and former Vice President, Chief Dr. Jewel Cianeh Howard-Taylor, faced serious criminal allegations and incarceration. At that defining moment, the statement attributed to the party leadership was, in our view, one of the weakest responses in the history of a party once renowned for its fighting spirit, political potency and revolutionary character.”

“The mighty Congress for Democratic Change has no room for political distractions, manufactured controversies or attempts to fracture genuine opposition solidarity. We will remain vigilant and respond firmly, lawfully and politically to any effort to undermine legitimate democratic cooperation among opposition forces.”

Atty. Mulbah Fires Back At CDC’s SG, Thrashes Employment With VP Office

Reaction to the allegation attributed to Mr. Koijee regarding his employment with the Office of the Vice President, Chairman Mulbah termed the information as a product of falsehood that lacks all elements of truth.

Mulbah threw out an open challenge to the CDC chief scribe to go beyond just posting and use the controlling law – Freedom of Information Act to subpoena the payroll of the VP office.

“As a licensed lawyer I am qualified to provide legal service for anyone including the Vice President if he so requests. But this is not the case now. On the issue of NPP rejecting invitations, let me submit and say during my monthly podcast journalists wanted to know whether the invitation of other stalwarts of NPP mean the party will participate in the CDC round table? In response I said no because our party constitution clearly established the procedure of inviting the party. I was also cleared to remind our Partisans that this is the same strategy Congress used to keep our party in crisis for six years,” Atty. Mulbah clarified.

Carry Your CDC And Leave Our NPP

On the incarceration of the NPP Standard Bearer, Atty. Mulbah explained that the CDC through Koijee reached out to him for a joint press statement, which he declined to do so that the “false claim” of an existing coalition won’t be validated.

Mulbah contended that the so-called weak statement resulted to granting of a compassionate leave to the former Vice President.

“You talked about the issuance of weak statement but our weak requested government to grant compassionate leave for our SB and it was honor.

SG Koijee, why didn’t you use the strong statement to change the legal opinion that evicted you since strong statement could have an impact on judicial opinion? Stop the Showmanship. In a reasonable man standard what you can’t do for yourself you can’t do it for others. You carry your CDC and leave our NPP.”

“Jefferson didn’t you place a call to me a day after [MadamTaylor] was arrested and pleaded with me for NPP and CDC to issue a joint statement and I rejected it?

I rejected it because to do so will validate your false claims as Coalition. Jefferson are you not the same person in 2023 unilaterally seized the candidates registration fees of USD 103,000 against my advice as the then Coalition Secretary General who signed all the candidates nomination forms?” Mulbah asked.

“I am encouraging everyone wishing to verify these allegations to contact Atty. J. Allison Barco to confirm the truthfulness of my assertion. Do you think I am a fool that easy to forget all of these ill treatments? As long as former President Weah continues to use character like you as a face of the Congress Liberian of sound minds will never forget the past.”

Several NPP Stalwarts Endorse Opposition Despite Rejection From Party

The core of matter remains, the NPP itself seems divided and fragile.

During the weekend’s gathering of opposition leaders and supporters, a group under the umbrella of Concerned partisans of the National Patriotic Party (NPP), comprising members of the party’s National Executive Committee, endorsed opposition unity and the Congress for Democratic Change (CDC)-called consultative meeting.
