The group called on opposition parties to put aside personal ambitions, resolve differences through dialogue and work toward a broad-based platform capable of providing a credible alternative.

The partisans criticized individuals within the NPP whose statements and conduct they claimed, have contributed to the challenges facing former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor and the party.

They furthered that the NPP is bigger than any individual and urged its members, opposition leaders and supporters to remain calm, focused and committed to democratic principles.

The statement, according to OK FM Reporter Nyantee Togba, was signed by Mr. Emmanuel Goll, National Chairman of the Concerned Partisans of the NPP and national vice chairman for international affairs, and approved by Partisan C. Neileh Daitouah, vice chairman for inter-party affairs.

World.title: Liberia: ANC Youth Congress Calls for IGP Coleman’s Resignation, Endorses Cummings
World.content:
MONROVIA — The Alternative National Congress (ANC) Youth Congress, headed by Chairman Alieu Kadii, has called for the immediate resignation of Inspector General of Police Gregory Coleman, accusing him of presiding over alleged impunity, selective law enforcement and declining public confidence in Liberia’s security and justice institutions.

By Francis G. Boayue

The youth wing made the call Saturday during a press conference in Monrovia, where it presented its State of the Youth Report, criticizing the Boakai administration over security, corruption, drug abuse, unemployment and worsening economic conditions.

The group alleged that police shootings resulting in the deaths of Bangalie Kamara, Essah Massaley and James Kandy have not led to prosecutions. It also accused the police of excessive use of force during incidents in the Kinjor concession area and at ArcelorMittal.

The allegations were presented by the group as part of its broader criticism of the government’s security and justice policies.

The ANC Youth Congress also questioned the government’s handling of Liberia’s cocaine investigation, alleging that police vehicles have been used to escort cocaine into and out of the country.

The group called for greater transparency regarding references to “very, very senior government officials” allegedly linked to the investigation and questioned why those individuals have not been publicly identified or prosecuted.

It further accused the government of pursuing opposition figures more aggressively than members and allies of the ruling Unity Party, describing the situation as evidence of selective justice.

The Congress expressed concern over what it described as Liberia’s growing drug and substance-abuse crisis, claiming that more than 100,000 young people have been affected.

It called for greater investment in rehabilitation facilities, youth employment and entrepreneurship rather than what it described as an emphasis on political activities.

The group also criticized rising living costs, taxation, the demolition of structures belonging to low-income residents and limited access to financing for small businesses.

Beyond its criticism of the government, the ANC Youth Congress endorsed ANC political leader Alexander B. Cummings as its preferred alternative ahead of the 2029 presidential election.

Kadii and members of the youth congress described the ANC as a “Third Lane” outside Liberia’s traditional political establishment and urged Liberians to consider Cummings based on his private-sector and international management experience.

The group said a Cummings administration would prioritize job creation, investment attraction, support for small businesses and entrepreneurs, and reforms to ensure Liberia derives greater benefits from its natural resources.

The youth congress argued that Liberia’s development challenge is less about the availability of resources than how those resources are managed and distributed.

It said its proposed political alternative is centered on jobs, accountability, dignity and opportunity.

The press conference comes as political parties and interest groups begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2029 elections, with the ANC Youth Congress urging young Liberians to take a more active role in determining the country’s political and economic direction.

World.title: Annual Kalumbila Sports event bags over 3 million
World.content:
The annual Kalumbila Sports event organised by First Quantum Minerals (FQM) Trident Limited has raised over K3 million from last year’s event with the funds going towards the construction of a theatre at Wumi Mini Hospital.

Speaking during the 2026 Kalumbila challenge, FQM Trident Limited Assistant General Manager Frederic Wouters says the event was another way in which the company was contributing to the development and wellbeing of the community.

Mr Wouters said this year’s proceeds from the challenge will go towards community livelihood initiatives and continued improvement of social infrastructure in Kalumbila.

“For us as First Quantum Minerals, the Kalumbila challenge has become much more than a sporting event. It is about health, wellness, inclusion and bringing people together,” he said.

He said the challenge was also demonstrating what could be achieved when a community came together with a shared purpose.

“This year, 2,200 people have taken up the challenge, up from the 1,500 people who took part last year, with close to 4,000 people expected here today,” Mr Wouters said.

He said the growth in participation was encouraging because behind every number was someone choosing to get active, challenge themselves and be part of the experience.

Mr Wouters said the K3 million raised last year has been channelled towards the construction of a theatre at Wumi Mini Hospital.

“That theatre is now under construction, giving us a tangible example of how an event like this can translate community participation into lasting social impact,” he said.

Meanwhile, Mr Wouters said the challenge has also helped create business linkages and investment opportunities within the community.

He said the growing interest in the event has further helped inspire other projects and strengthened goodwill around development partnerships across Kalumbila.

“As the town grows, our ambition should be about more than economic development. It should also be about creating a vibrant community where people want to live, work and raise their families,” he said.

And speaking at the same occasion, Kalumbila District Commissioner Brenda Sankisa who was represented by District Administrative Officer (DAO) Frank Siatwinda said government appreciates the role the private sector continues to play in promoting sporting activities.

Ms Sankisa said the government recognised that a healthy population is an important part of a strong and productive community, adding that events such as the Kalumbila challenge encourage people to remain active, make healthy choices and take greater responsibility for their wellbeing.

“What is particularly encouraging today is the variety of activities on the programme. From cycling and running to football, chess and aerobics, there is an opportunity for people of different ages, interests and abilities to participate,” she said.

Ms Sankisa said this was why partnerships between government, the private sector, community organisations and residents were important.

“As Kalumbila continues to grow, we must also think about the kind of community we want to build. Development is not only about infrastructure, businesses and economic activity. It is also about ensuring that the people who live here have opportunities to lead healthy, active and fulfilling lives,” she said.

World.title: Access Bank channels farmer payments
World.content:
Access Bank Zambia has disbursed more than K2 billion to over 113,000 farmers under the 2026 crop marketing season.

The payments have been made through a digital platform developed in partnership with the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) to facilitate faster payment to farmers.

Access Bank Zambia says the digital payment system, which was activated five weeks ago, has recorded a 99.5 percent success rate, with farmers able to receive payments within 24 hours.

Access Bank Zambia Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Iheanyi Nwogu says the initiative is part of the efforts to improve the efficiency of farmer payments and expand access to financial services.

Dr Nwogu says the bank supported more than 311,000 farmers last year through its branch network, an experience which helped it develop the current digital payment system.

He says the system has reduced manual intervention and improved the delivery of payments to farmers.

He disclosed that the partnership between the public and private sectors demonstrates how technology can be used to address practical challenges and support the agricultural sector.

This is contained in a press statement issued to the media today in Lusaka today by Access Bank Head of Corporate Communications, Alice Mwila.

World.title: Public cautioned against harming vultures
World.content:
Game Rangers International Community Outreach Ranger, under the Rufunsa Conservation Project Chrispine Tembo, is appealing to community members in Luangwa District not endanger the lives of vultures when they come across them.

Mr Tembo says vultures are social animals that play a critical role in the ecosystem by cleaning up carcasses of dead animals and any other meat substances that may be rotting in the environment.

Speaking during a World Vultures Day local language programme at Adroit Radio in Luangwa District, Mr Tembo explained that the commemoration that takes place on September 5th annually, is meant to educate children between 4 and 12 years old on what the vultures are and their characteristics.

“The purpose of targeting the children is to inculcate a sense of responsibility towards these vultures as they grow into adulthood,” he said.

Mr Tembo explained that vultures are not hunters but depend on dead and rotten meat substances that either die on their own or are killed by other animals.

He said the vultures have a high sense of smell and sight of over two kilometers, giving a sense to always fly high above thermal winds which is necessary to move long distances.

“These animals are scavengers but they do not allow themselves to be stained with blood, while eating, making them a unique species,” he explained.

He further said that the vultures are in 23 species, stating that they are not dangerous as can be seen on their blunt claws.

He however warned that their beaks are more dangerous because they are sharper than a sharp knife.

Mr Tembo appealed to members of the public to desist from endangering the species for whatever reason they may have, including myths.

World.title: NW Met dept. tightens weather advocacy
World.content:
Solwezi District Agricultural Coordinator (DACO) Mutinta Zulu says the department will intensify sensitisation to farmers on the likely change in weather patterns.

Ms Zulu says following an advisory from the Zambia Meteorological Department on the likelihood of some parts of North-western Province to experience rainfall, the department will work with Extension Officers to sensitise the farmers.

Ms Zulu said she was aware that not all farmers have sold their produce to the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) as such, in case of a heavy downpour, farm produce will go to waste.

“We know that farmers still have stock of their produce at their homes, some of it unsecured, our role is to sensitise them about this important information so that we prevent produce from going to waste.” Ms Zulu said.

Ms Zulu appealed to farmers to ensure that farm produce is well secured to prevent losses, urging farmers to remain abreast with latest information on the El Nino and its effects.

The Zambia Meteorological department has issued a weather alert indicating that a low pressure over Angola is expected to draw a moist and unstable North-westerly airflow mainly affecting the Western half of Zambia .

The advisory has explained that this will result in isolated rainfall over Western, North-western, Copperbelt and Southern Provinces as well as the Western parts of Lusaka and Central Provinces.

World.title: Govt. encourages youth participation in Karate
World.content:
Government has called for increased youth participation in karate and other sporting disciplines, saying sport remains a critical tool for youth empowerment, discipline and national development.

Ministry of Youth, Sport and Arts Permanent Secretary Kangwa Chileshe says martial arts such as karate can help shield young people from crime and other destructive behaviours by instilling resilience, self-discipline and respect.

He made the remarks during the closing ceremony of 15th Japanese Ambassador’s Karate Cup jointly hosted by the Embassy of Japan and Kyokushin Karate International.

He says karate has grown significantly in Zambia since its introduction in the 1970s, with about 8,000 Zambians now participating in various styles, including Kyokushin and Shotokan.

Mr Chileshe has also commended the Embassy of Japan for its continued support towards the development of karate in Zambia, noting that the Japanese Ambassador’s Karate Cup has grown into one of the biggest martial arts tournaments in the SADC region.

He says the tournament has also provided opportunities for young karatekas to pursue careers in the defense and security sector, with some joining the Zambia Army, Zambia Air Force, Zambia National Service and Zambia Police Service.

Speaking at the same event, Japanese Ambassador to Zambia, Mikami Akiteru said karate has evolved beyond sport to become a powerful bridge strengthening cultural ties between Zambia and Japan.

Ambassador Mikami said Zambia’s growing karate community demonstrates that cultural exchange between the two countries is no longer one-way, with Zambian instructors now teaching the Japanese martial art to Japanese children living in Zambia.

Meanwhile, Kyokushin Kenbukaikan International, Executive Director, Simba Mangaba has honoured President Hakainde Hichilema with a masters-degree black belt and a full karate uniform in recognition of his perseverance, discipline and commitment throughout his life.

Kyokushin Kenbukaikan International Executive Director, Simba Mangaba, says the honour is not merely about a belt or uniform, but represents discipline, courage, endurance and the determination to rise after every setback

World.title: Schools ready for new term-Mando
World.content:
Ministry of Education, says schools countrywide are ready to reopen for a new academic term on Monday, September 7, 2026.

Ministry of Education Assistant Director and Head of Communications Kunda Mando says all the 13,991 schools in the country’s 116 districts are ready to receive learners.

Ms Mando told journalists in Lusaka today that preparations for the reopening have been complete, preceding the opening of schools.

She said teachers have also been oriented on the implementation of the new curriculum, which is currently being phased in at Grade One, Grade Two, Grade Four, Form One and Form Two levels.

The Assistant Director explained that Head Teachers have also assessed the preparedness of teachers, including the progress made on schemes of work and class registration in preparation for the new school term.

.

She has since urged parents and guardians to ensure that learners report to school tomorrow, saying the government wants all children to resume learning without delay.

And Ms Mando has revealed that schools have been provided with grants to meet operational needs, including cleanliness and other services.

Ms Mando has further disclosed that her ministry disbursed K794 million for the third quarter, to facilitate the effective running of schools.

She said the funds are subject to monitoring by Standards Officers and other mechanisms to ensure that they are used for their intended purpose.

Meanwhile, Ms Mando has announced that September is literacy month, with the national commemoration to be held in Kalumbila district, in North-western Province.

She said the latest demographic and health survey indicates that 81 percent of males aged between 15 and 49 can read and write, compared to 70 percent of females.

Ms Mando said the figures demonstrate the need to continue investing in literacy for both boys and girls, particularly among women and girls who remain behind.

Ms Mando said this is in line with the competency-based curriculum, which seeks to equip learners with practical skills and the ability to apply knowledge in solving real-life challenges.

She said the activities include adult literacy programmes, aimed at encouraging people of all ages to acquire reading and writing skills.

The literacy month is themed, “literacy for people, the planet, and prosperity.”

World.title: Schools ready for annual JETS Fair
World.content:
National Science Centre Assistant Director for Training and Collective Support Anecetus Moonga says more than 600 learners from across the country are expected to participate in this year’s JETS and TEST National Fair to be held in Lusaka.

Mr Moonga says the fair will be held from September 7 to 11, 2026, under the theme “Promoting Innovation and Competence Development in STEM Education.”

Mr Moonga said the fair will focus on five major categories, namely sustainable systems and environment; health, food and wellbeing systems, digital, robotics and artificial intelligence systems.

He named others as engineering, design and production systems and mathematical modelling and investigations.

Mr Moonga said learners will also participate in various skills categories, including mechanical and civil engineering, cosmetology and other disciplines.

The Assistant Director revealed that the fair is expected to showcase innovations from young people and contribute to improving the lives of Zambians.

World.title: One dies, three injured in Rufunsa
World.content:
One person has died, while three others have sustained injuries in a road traffic accident (RTA) involving a public service bus in Rufunsa district, Lusaka Province.

The accident occurred today in Lukwipa area along Great East Road around 12:20 hours.

Zambia Police Service Public Relations Officer Godfrey Chilabi, confirmed the accident to the media in a statement issued in Lusaka.

Mr Chilabi identified the deceased as Shadrick Mukuka aged 27, of an unknown address.

He said Mr Mukuka sustained serious injuries and later died while receiving treatment at Mpanshya Mission Hospital.

He said the body of the deceased has been deposited in the hospital mortuary awaiting postmortem examination.

He explained that the accident involved a Yaxing public service bus, registration number AIF 9348 ZM that was driven by Francis Chisanga, aged 35 of Chainda Compound in Lusaka.

The bus which was travelling from Lusaka to Chipata in Eastern Province had 54 passengers on board.

Mr Chilabi stated that 26 of the passengers were pupils from Mbwindi Secondary School in Sinda district, while the other 28 were travelling to Chipata.

He revealed that preliminary investigations indicate that the accident occurred when the driver attempted to overtake an unidentified motor vehicle which allegedly swerved into his lane.

Mr Chilabi said the driver lost control of the bus while trying to avoid a collision causing it to veer off the road and hit several trees.

He said the driver sustained serious injuries and was admitted to Mpanshya Mission Hospital, where he is receiving treatment.

Mr Chilabi added that two other passengers sustained minor injuries and are also receiving treatment at the same hospital while 51 passengers escaped unhurt.

He said the bus was extensively damaged at the front, adding that investigations into the accident are continuing.

The Police Spokesperson has since advised motorists to exercise caution, avoid excessive speed and overtake only when it is safe to do so.

Mr Chilabi further urged motorists in the country to remain alert and observe all road traffic regulations to prevent loss of life and injuries.

World.title: Angola: Cotton Revival In Busia - Hope Grows Amid Small Farms, Dry Spells And a Silent Ginnery
World.content:
The roads leading into the interior of Busia County tell a story of a region that is slowly changing, but perhaps not fast enough.

From Luanda to Bumala and Finyula, the journey is punctuated by dusty roads, boda bodas and stretches where getting to the farms is an exercise in patience. Away from the main roads, infrastructure remains a challenge, with motorcycles often providing the only practical means of reaching some farming areas.

It is here, amid small farms and modest homesteads, that cotton is quietly making a comeback.

But unlike Lamu County, where cotton farmers are taking advantage of the revival of the industry to expand production, farmers in this part of Busia are still growing the crop on very small pieces of land.

Most farmers cultivate no more than two acres, according to Bonventer Barasa, an accountant and manager at Luanda Farmers Cooperative Union.

“Currently, not more than two acres. Very small acreage hence low production despite what our modern ginnery can handle,” Barasa says.

For a crop whose revival is being seen as an opportunity to reconnect farmers to a market that once supported entire communities, the small acreage presents a major challenge.

Without enough cotton coming from farmers, the ginnery cannot operate at full capacity. And without a reliable market and attractive returns, farmers have little incentive to increase production. It is a cycle that the region is still trying to break.

For Vincent Okumu, however, cotton is more than just another crop. The farmer has grown cotton for more than two decades, taking over the enterprise from his parents. What began as a family livelihood became an important investment in his own future. Cotton proceeds helped him pursue his education. Today, he is using the same crop to educate his children. Two of his children have already graduated from university, while another is preparing to enrol.

For Okumu, this is proof that even small-scale cotton farming can change a family's fortunes when the crop performs well and farmers receive a fair return.

He farms about one and a half acres and expects to make at least Sh100,000 in profit from the current crop.

He also chairs Bwiri Farmers Cooperative Society, where he says the benefits of cotton are becoming visible beyond individual households. Livelihoods in his village, he says, have improved, with the gradual disappearance of thatched-roof houses among families whose incomes have increased. The transformation may not be dramatic, but it is visible. The same crop that helped one generation access education is now helping another pay school fees and improve their homes.

Yet Okumu's experience also exposes the limitations holding cotton farming back in Busia. He would like to increase his acreage from one and a half acres to five. But expanding production is easier said than done.

One of the biggest challenges is mechanisation. Land preparation is still largely done manually, making cotton production expensive and time-consuming. The county's available machinery cannot meet the demand from the number of farmers seeking the service.

The problem is particularly important in cotton because timing matters. Okumu says delayed distribution of seed affects production because farmers are working within a narrow planting and growing window.

By the time some farmers receive seed and prepare their land, they may have already lost valuable time.

It is a challenge that echoes concerns raised by the cooperative leadership.

Bernard Ojiambo, chairman of the Luanda Farmers Cooperative Union, says the cooperative has been seeking machinery, including tractors that farmers can hire to prepare their land. Without tractors and other equipment, farmers can fall behind the rains. “When it reaches time for planting farmers can hire, they go and plow to make it earlier plantation. We delay because we don't have machines like tractors and other things to support farmers,” Ojiambo says.

The consequence is a chain reaction of delays in planting and harvesting. The rains hold the key This year's crop has also had to contend with insufficient rainfall.

The cotton plants are about two months old, but the season has not been ideal. The dry conditions have affected the crop, with farmers now looking to the rains for a turnaround. During the visit, temperatures climbed to around 30 degrees Celsius. The heat was compounded by dusty roads and the dry conditions in the interior. Yet farmers remain hopeful. Ojiambo says the area's soils and climate can support cotton when rainfall comes at the right time. “It is the soil itself and the climate, though we don't have much rain, but once we get it between April and August, the harvest comes out well,” he says.

AllAfrica Vincent Okumu, a cotton farmer from Busia County inspecting his crop at his one and a half acre farm

For farmers like Okumu, a good harvest could provide the incentive to expand.

He praises the cooperative's buying price of Sh76 per kilogram, saying the price offers farmers a reason to remain in the crop. His own target of at least Sh100,000 in profit from one and a half acres shows why the crop continues to attract interest despite the difficulties.

At Luanda Ginnery, however, there is currently little evidence of the activity associated with harvest. The machines are silent. The last season ended about four months ago, and the ginnery is now waiting for the next crop to mature.

Inside the modern facility, the process is straightforward. Once cotton arrives, it is weighed and stored before being fed into the machinery. A suction system moves it from the store to a bale opener, where compacted cotton is loosened.

The cotton then passes through a pre-cleaner that removes dust and separates poor-quality cotton from the good lint. The good cotton is taken to the ginning machine, where the lint is separated from the seed.

The seed moves through a conveyor while the lint is transferred to a press, where it is compressed and tied into 200-kilogram bales ready for collection. But the ginnery's ability to operate depends entirely on what farmers bring from their fields. “If they don't grow cotton, then we don't have raw materials. That means we won't move on,” Barasa says. It is a simple relationship: the strength of the ginnery depends on the strength of the farmer.

Cotton has a long history in Busia. Ojiambo says cotton growing in the region dates back decades, when the crop was promoted among local farmers. But the industry eventually declined, with farmers becoming discouraged by delayed payments and poor returns. When cotton lost its appeal, many turned to maize. But maize also requires adequate rainfall, while cotton, Ojiambo argues, remains better suited to the area's conditions. “Cotton is more of a value than maize,” he says. With maize, the small acreage available to farmers is often used to feed the household. Cotton, on the other hand, is primarily a cash crop. Once harvested and sold, the money can be directed towards school fees, food and other household needs. That distinction is important in an area where many families are still farming on very small plots.

The challenges extend beyond production. Barasa says farmers also struggle with access to chemicals and implements, while limited working capital makes it difficult for both farmers and the ginnery to operate efficiently. The ginnery has also struggled to add value to cotton seed. A machine supplied by the Agricultural and Food Authority to process cotton seed has not performed efficiently, according to Barasa. He says a better-performing machine could allow the facility to produce cottonseed oil, seed cakes and soap. Such value addition would give the crop additional economic importance and potentially create more income from the same harvest.

The ginnery has, however, received a major boost through investment in solar energy. Barasa says the government provided solar panels worth Sh40 million. The move has reduced the facility's monthly electricity bill from about Sh150,000 to approximately Sh75,000. But the question remains whether there will be enough cotton to keep the machinery busy.

Busia's cotton revival is therefore a work in progress. The crop has a history here. Farmers know it. Cooperatives understand it. The ginnery has the machinery to process it. What is missing is scale. Farmers are still cultivating small pieces of land. Seed distribution needs to be timely. Mechanisation remains inadequate. Rainfall is unpredictable. And the market needs to offer farmers sufficient confidence to invest more.

For Vincent Okumu, however, the argument for cotton is already settled. The crop paid for his education and is now paying for his children's education. He believes the same opportunity exists for his neighbours. As chairman of Bwiri Farmers Cooperative Society, he is encouraging other farmers to return to cotton and take advantage of the improving fortunes of the crop. His own ambition is to move from one and a half acres to five. But for that ambition to become reality, the tractors must arrive, seed must reach farmers on time and the market must remain attractive.

For now, the cotton plants are still young. The ginnery remains quiet. The roads remain dusty and difficult. But the clouds are gathering, and with them comes the possibility of a better harvest. In the small farms of Busia, cotton may not yet be the booming commercial enterprise seen elsewhere. But for farmers like Okumu, it has already proved that a small farm can produce something much bigger than cotton—a pathway to education, better homes and a more hopeful future.

World.title: US restricts government travel to Mexican border city over threat concerns

Travel restrictions have been placed on U.S. government employees in the Mexican border city of Nogales, Sonora, according to officials.

The U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Mexico on Saturday issued a warning restricting government activity over an unspecified threat in Nogales, Sonora, in Mexico.

"Due to threat information, U.S. government activities in, and travel to, Nogales have been restricted to essential movement during daylight hours only," the U.S. Consulate General in Nogales said in a statement.

STATE DEPARTMENT URGES AMERICANS TO AVOID MEXICAN CITY JUST ACROSS TEXAS BORDER

Sonora's State Security Board said it contacted U.S. consular officials after the alert was issued but did not provide information identifying a specific threat. State authorities said they had no information establishing a concrete risk to the public, though they would continue preventive security operations in Nogales.

The alert also reminded Americans that the U.S. Travel Advisory designates Sonora as a Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" area.

Anyone in the area is urged to exercise increased caution and be aware of their surroundings, seek shelter in the event of an incident, notify friends and family of their safety in the event of an incident, follow instructions from Mexican law enforcement, and monitor local media for updates.

U.S. lawmakers also encouraged people in the area to pay attention to the warnings issued by the U.S. government.

"For Americans in or near Nogales - or who may have family members or friends there: please heed the guidance and warnings from the U.S. government," Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., said on X.

Barbara Eden sparked concern among fans after abruptly dropping out of a Los Angeles film festival due to what was described as a "sudden illness," but the 95-year-old actress later shared a reassuring update on social media.

The "I Dream of Jeannie" star was set to be honored during the Cinecon Classic Film Festival at the Landmark Nuart Theatre on Saturday but pulled out shortly before the event was scheduled to begin.

"We’re sorry to share that, due to a sudden illness, Barbara Eden will no longer be able to appear in person at Cinecon tonight," festival organizers announced in a Facebook post on Saturday.

ROD STEWART CALLED 'TONE-DEAF' FOR ATTENDING WORLD CUP GAME A DAY CANCELING CONCERT DUE TO HEALTH ISSUES

"Barbara is deeply regretful that she had to cancel at the last minute, as she had been very much looking forward to seeing everyone and celebrating with us," they continued.

"We know how many of you were excited to welcome Barbara. We appreciate your understanding and join you in sending her our best wishes for a speedy recovery," they added.

'YOU'RE SO VAIN' SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON'S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE

Eden later took to Instagram to clarify the circumstances around her absence and update fans on her condition.

"It’s okay everyone! I’m okay!" she wrote alongside a photo in which she was seen standing in front of a painting and smiling. "Oh, my goodness there has been a bit of miscommunication," Eden continued. "I’m not suffering from an illness; my doctor very recently prescribed a brand-new medication that turned out to have some nasty side effects. Due to the discomfort, my doctor ordered me to remain at home until it can be sorted out."

MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS

Cinecon is a classic film festival in Los Angeles that celebrates vintage movies, rare screenings and stars from Hollywood’s Golden Age. This year’s Cinecon marked the festival’s 62nd edition.

CURATORS AT LIBRARY OF CONGRESS DISCOVER LOST FILM BY LEGENDARY CINEMA PIONEER AFTER SPOTTING 'SUBTLE CLUE'

RICK MORANIS, CAMERON DIAZ AND LINDSAY LOHAN AMONG STARS WHO LEFT FAME BEHIND BEFORE RETURNING TO HOLLYWOOD

Her film credits include "Flaming Star" opposite Elvis Presley, "Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea" and "Harper Valley P.T.A." and she has also starred in the hit TV shows "Dallas" and "Sabrina the Teenage Witch."

Eden earned two Golden Globe nominations for her performance in "I Dream of Jeannie" and was honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1988. She was honored with the Legend Award for Lifetime Achievement at the National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards in 2023.

Her last film role was in 2019's "My Adventures with Santa," in which she played Mrs. Claus. The movie's cast also included Denise Richards, Patrick Muldoon and Jamie Luner.

World.title: Time is now, Clemson Tigers and Dabo Swinney need to call it quits after historic run
World.content:
It happened again.

It's no secret that I was fairly high on the Clemson Tigers this offseason, at least relative to the nonexistent expectations many pundits had for them this year.

I wasn't picking them to make a deep College Football Playoff run or win a national title, but I figured they would compete for an ACC Championship and be a darkhorse Playoff pick.

THREE TEAMS RANKED OUTSIDE THE TOP-12 OF THE COACHES POLL WHO WILL MAKE THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

Then the LSU game happened.

It seemed like the pieces were in place for them to at least surprise some folks, but alas, that doesn't appear to be the case.

I blame myself for getting sucked back into the Clemson hype machine, but this article isn't about me.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHES ON HOT SEAT: BILL BELICHICK, MIKE NORVELL AND OTHERS FACING MAKE-OR-BREAK 2026

This article is about how it might be time for the Tigers and their all-time winningest head coach, Dabo Swinney, to amicably and gracefully part ways.

Saturday night's 51-10 debacle in Death Valley isn't a reason for panic in a vacuum.

LSU and Lane Kiffin will probably do that to a lot of teams far better than Clemson this year.

But the fact that, once again, the Tigers and Swinney are starting their season off on the wrong foot is a cause for concern.

It seems like ever since Trevor Lawrence moved on to the NFL, Clemson can't seem to sustain any momentum to start the season.

And some of you Dabo defenders may point at the fact that they had to play teams like Georgia and LSU in recent years as a way to hand wave these brutal starts.

HAS NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP PICTURE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL ALREADY CHANGED AFTER A STUNNING FIRST WEEK?

While that does explain some of it, Clemson should still be measured as peers of these programs, so the fact that they are getting embarrassed in these contests is a sign things are slipping out of Swinney's hands.

Of course, these game one losses aren't just happening against title contenders either, as the Tigers famously waltzed into Wallace Wade Stadium to take on an unranked Duke squad in 2023, only to get pounded into submission in a 28-7 loss.

Clemson was a top-ten team that year heading into the season, and though they ended their campaign with nine wins and a Gator Bowl berth, that hardly sounds like something fans of the dynastic program would have signed up for just a few years earlier.

Dabo still has enough talent on his roster to compete in the ACC, and this loss to LSU, while humiliating, does nothing to dash their conference title aspirations, but it is indicative that it's starting to trend in the wrong direction in the western end of South Carolina.

RANKING THE TEN BEST COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHES IN THE COUNTRY AHEAD OF THE 2026 SEASON

His resistance toward the transfer portal would be more forgivable if Swinney was still landing top-five recruiting classes, but that isn't the reality anymore.

The last time Clemson signed even a top-ten class was in 2022, and there have been a few ranked outside the top-20 in that time frame.

That won't get this program where they want to be come January, but I guess that's the better question to ask here.

Where do the Tigers want to be in the grand scheme of college football?

Do they still view themselves as one of the premier powers in the sport? Or are they content with winning eight or nine games a year and occasionally threatening to make the CFP?

Because if they want to be the latter, they may need to start having some tough conversations about the man in the team-issued polo tucked into his khakis.

I'm not breaking any news here, but it might be time for a change at Clemson.

We can all recognize the greatness of Dabo Swinney - as I have done before - while simultaneously admitting that the game may have passed him by.

His recruiting classes are starting to falter. His transfer portal hauls are virtually nonexistent. And several other power players in college football have lapped the Tigers in just a few short years.

I won't speculate what will happen to Dabo or the Tigers the rest of this season.

For all I know, they could rattle off 11 straight victories and make me look like a fool.

It's not likely, but it is possible.

With that being said, all signs point to Swinney and Clemson trending down, and I wouldn't be surprised if this was the last dance between legendary coach and program.

That might have sounded like blasphemy just half a decade ago, but college football is always evolving, and Swinney is a man stuck in time.

And he's hurting the very program he helped take to the mountaintop.

World.title: Michael Rapaport slams 'clown' Macklemore for anti-Israel performance
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Michael Rapaport slammed Macklemore as a "clown" after the rapper brought his pro-Palestinian message to Ed Sheeran’s concert stage.

Macklemore, 43, repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind's Hall" while opening for Sheeran, 35, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey during shows on Friday and Saturday nights.

On Saturday, Rapaport, 56, who is Jewish and has become one of Hollywood’s most outspoken pro-Israel voices since Hamas' Oct. 7 attack, ripped Macklemore, born Benjamin Haggerty, in a blistering post on X.

BLACK CROWES FACE BACKLASH AFTER CHRIS ROBINSON SHUTS DOWN U.S.A. CHANT AND CALLS FANS 'IGNORANT'

'Imagine going to see Ed Sheeran & this absolute no talent none singer non rapping non dancing clown Macklemore is opening & because he actually has no act or specific skill set he’s jumping around like dkc carrying on about a genocide that never happened in Gaza," Rapaport wrote, adding "This is a nightmare."

In another critical post on X, the comedian questioned Sheeran’s decision to bring Macklemore on as an opening act.

ED SHEERAN CONCERT WORKERS HOSPITALIZED AFTER FORKLIFT INCIDENT IN DETROIT: REPORT

"So Ed Sheeran is ok with this p--- stain opening up for him? Sweet Ed Sheeran?" Rapaport wrote.

Rapaport also reposted an article about the backlash to Macklemore's political messaging following the concerts, writing, "Calling this dude a ‘Rapper' is disrespectful to any actual ‘Rapper.’"

ISRAEL, JEWS TARGETED WORLDWIDE AS WELL-FUNDED LEFTIST, ISLAMIST GROUPS JOIN FOR ‘NAKBA 78’ PROTESTS

Fox News Digital has reached out to Macklemore and Sheeran's representatives for comment.

In a video that Rapaport posted from the Friday night show, Macklemore, who wore a keffiyeh tied around his neck, was seen repeatedly chanting "Say free, free Palestine!" while music played as he walked around the stage and held up his microphone.

Macklemore, who will be opening for Sheeran during the U.S. leg of the "Shape of You" singer's Loop Tour, also delivered a speech in which he said that he wanted to use stages across America to advocate for Palestine.

ISRAELI PM NETANYAHU ARGUES PUBLIC OPINION SHIFT ON ISRAEL 'CORRELATES ALMOST 100%' TO SOCIAL MEDIA

"A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine," Macklemore said in a video shared on social media.

"I said, ‘Free Palestine!’ I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them," he continued.

"I have an 11-year-old daughter, her name is Sloan, she’s here tonight. And if any of you guys are parents, then you know that that love that you have for your kids cannot be put into words, right? I want to see her grow up, I want to see her go to school, to fall in love, to figure out meaning, purpose, joy, her existence on this planet. I want it to be the most beautiful possible."

"And I think that every single human being that walks this earth deserves that exact same feeling. To know safety and peace before they know the sound of violence, to know the sound of laughter on a playground before planes and bombs, for parents to be able to say bye to their kids in the morning and not have to wonder if this is going to be the last time they kiss their child goodbye."

"And if I let that fear I felt on the plane yesterday stop me from speaking my heart in order to keep my own comfort and the audience’s comfort, that is the day I no longer continue to be on stage," Macklemore added. "So, I say, ‘Free Palestine!’"

RAGE AGAINST THE MACHINE'S TOM MORELLO FACES BACKLASH AFTER SINGING AT NYC ICE PROTEST RALLY

Macklemore concluded his speech by calling for the freedom of other countries including America and blasting U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

"I say, free America, free Cuba to the Congo to Sudan to Iran, and all the people in America who have to live in fear because of this terrorist organization ICE," he said.

HAMAS, HEZBOLLAH FLAGS FLY AT ANTI-ISRAEL PROTEST MINUTES AFTER MAMDANI CONDEMNS TERROR PLOT AGAINST JEWS

Following his speech, Macklemore performed "Hind's Hall," a song inspired by the 2024 pro-Palestinian campus demonstrations," as footage from Gaza, pro-Palestinian protests, images of Israeli soldiers and pro-Palestinian messages were displayed on the stadium’s large screens.

The title of the song refers to Hamilton Hall, the Columbia University building that pro-Palestinian students occupied in April 2024 and renamed in honor of a 6-year-old Palestinian girl killed in the Israel-Gaza war. The lyrics in "Hind's Hall" praised the anti-Israel encampments and protests on college campuses across the country and called out President Biden, the police and the music industry.

RAPPER FACES $2.8M LAWSUIT AFTER AXING OPENING ACT FROM TOUR FOLLOWING HER POLITICAL RANT

Macklemore also repeated his pro-Palestinian messaging during Sheeran’s second MetLife Stadium show Saturday night, again calling for "Free Palestine" and performing his protest song "Hind’s Hall."

While some audience members cheered Macklemore's comments and joined the "Free Palestine" chant, the rapper's performance was met with backlash from other attendees.

One concertgoer said on X that he brought his wife and two daughters to Friday’s show as longtime Sheeran fans, but left disappointed after Macklemore’s set turned political. The fan said his daughters looked "completely confused" when Macklemore began chanting "Free Palestine," adding that he had taken them to "an Ed Sheeran concert, not to have an opening act lecture them about Middle East politics."

He said his family left their seats during Macklemore’s performance and returned after the rapper finished, praising Sheeran’s show as "phenomenal" but criticizing the singer for allowing Macklemore to perform again Saturday. "Friday might have been Macklemore’s decision. Saturday was yours," the concertgoer wrote, adding, "Tonight, you lost four of them. And I suspect plenty more."

Another concertgoer said he attended Saturday’s show in a company suite with 35 other people and was "embarrassed" and "shocked" by Macklemore’s set. The attendee said he had "always been a Macklemore fan," but after the rapper’s "political stunt," he could no longer support him or his music.

"When you go WOKE, you have to be prepared to lose fans," he wrote.

The concertgoer also denounced Sheeran for allowing Macklemore to return to the stage Saturday after the backlash from the previous night.

"After it happened on Friday, it should have immediately been stopped," he wrote, adding that he went to the show to hear "amazing music," not "Free Palestine" rants.

Two other concertgoers told Ynet, the English edition of Israel's largest new website, that they were unfamiliar with Macklemore before the show and unaware that he would be performing.

"We only found out there and we were in shock. It was really horrifying," they said.

"We immediately thought about everything our people have been through and how even when we’re abroad we still have to feel this antisemitism," they continued. "It was even harder because friends of ours were killed in the war and murdered at Nova. It was like a knife in the heart to hear him sing that way and hear people cheering."

The concertgoers said that some of the members in their group began crying and left the show before Sheeran's performance.

However, some social media users praised Macklemore for speaking up and expressed their support for the rapper's message.

"Huge respect for Ed Sheeran, but seeing Macklemore use his voice for Palestine made this moment mean so much more," one fan wrote on Instagram. "Respect to every artist who refuses to stay silent and uses their platform to speak up for humanity. Macklemore, we hear you."

"LOVE Macklemore, and good on him using his platform to speak out….his messaging is always spot on. Peace," another agreed.

"Free free Palestine. Love to Macklemore. Stay true," one fan chimed in.

"this was from last night!! I hope you get to perform this again tonight too!" a fan wrote alongside a clip from Macklemore's set.

"So happy we get to witness such history!" one fan commented.

"Honestly I loved this part of the concert !" another wrote.

"Music has always been a vital platform for human rights advocacy, not just mindless escape," wrote one X user. "Calling for peace, safety, and equality for Palestinians, Congolese, and Sudanese isn't antisemitic—it's pro-humanity. Macklemore explicitly stands for collective liberation and love."

"Art has always been political, why are you annoyed at an artist giving context to a song he released about the current state of the world you live in?" another fan commented on X. "Also, he was an opener, they could’ve just skipped his set! Although I hope Macklemore sings it louder next time!"

Meanwhile, the Israeli-American Council launched a petition calling for Macklemore to be removed from Sheeran’s remaining tour dates.

"This was an Ed Sheeran concert – not a political rally, not a protest, and not an activist event," the petition read. "The issue is not whether Macklemore has the right to hold political views. The question is where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda."

Macklemore has been outspoken in his support for Palestinians since the start of the Israel-Hamas war. In November 2023, Macklemore spoke at a pro-Palestinian rally in Washington, D.C., where he said, "I don’t know enough. But I know enough that this is a genocide."

The rapper's political messaging has also sparked backlash before. In 2024, he addressed criticism after saying "f--- America" during a pro-Palestinian charity concert in Seattle, later writing that he remained "unwavering in my support for a Free Palestine."

World.title: Germany’s far-right party AfD surges to historic victory in state election
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The far-right party Alternative for Germany, or AfD, was projected to win a strong victory in a regional election on Sunday, in a major blow to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's center-right party, the Christian Democratic Union.

Merz's party was projected to be hit with a disastrous result in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.

AfD had sought to form the country’s first far-right state government since the end of World War II in 1945, although it was not immediately clear whether it would be able to fulfill that ambition.

Ulrich Siegmund, AfD's anti-migration candidate for governor, said that "we have written history."

ANTI-MIGRANT AFD SEEKS TO BREAK GERMANY'S POLITICAL 'FIREWALL' IN HISTORIC STATE ELECTION

Siegmund, 35, told public broadcaster ARD that voters had sent a message that "things cannot carry on like this," adding that it was "also a signal toward Berlin."

"A very good campaigner for us in this election campaign was Friedrich Merz. Every day this man is in the chancellery is one too many," he said of Germany's unpopular leader.

The election comes amid widespread public discontent with the national government, which has yet to convince many voters it can get the country's sluggish economy back on track.

AfD aimed for an absolute majority in the state legislature to govern on its own and overcome the so-called firewall of mainstream parties’ refusal to work with it. But it was unclear long after polls closed whether that goal would become reality.

"AfD is a right-wing extremist party. It wants to leave the euro; that would be economic downfall ... it works closely together with Russia, it wants a completely different social model," said Franziska Hoppermann, the national general-secretary of Merz's party. "We will not work with them."

Achieving its first state government would be the biggest victory in the anti-migration party’s 13-year history.

Regardless of whether AfD forms its own government, the projected result is still a blow to Merz, whose center-right party has led Saxony-Anhalt for 24 years. Unlike several other European countries, modern Germany has not had a far-right or right-wing populist party leading a national, state or major-city government.

AfD is the largest opposition party in Germany’s national parliament and is strongest in the formerly communist and less prosperous east, where Saxony-Anhalt sits.

Its regional branch in Saxony-Anhalt is one of several classified as a confirmed right-wing extremist group by the domestic intelligence agency, which cites members' disparagement of migrants from Muslim countries among other things.

The party promotes "remigration," which pushes for the deportation of immigrants.

Siegmund has said his top priorities include "a deportation offensive" and ending incentives for people to come to Germany and "exploit our social system." He also wants to initiate a process to pull Saxony-Anhalt from the regional public broadcaster over allegations of "disinformation."

Germany’s 16 states have extensive powers, including overseeing security matters and running the education system.

An AfD leader in a neighboring state appealed two convictions for knowingly using a Nazi slogan.

The party has pushed back on accusations of extremism as politically motivated.

GERMANY BLAMES RUSSIA AFTER EXPLOSIVE-LADEN DRONE FOUND NEAR UKRAINIAN CARGO PLANES AT MAJOR AIRPORT

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Projections for ARD and ZDF public television, based on exit polls and partial counting, have AfD at just over 44% of the vote, more than double its showing five years ago in the region of 2.1 million people west of Berlin.

Merz's Christian Democratic Union was significantly behind, polling 18% and losing about half its support. The Left Party, the center-left Social Democrats and Greens were seen polling around 9% each.

It was unclear whether the BSW party would reach the 5% of the vote needed to win seats. The projections put AfD at least marginally short of an absolute majority for now, but that could change.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

World.title: As Trump pushes for data centers, voters in key midterm races say they don’t want them
World.content:
DES MOINES, Iowa — Dawn Vogel, a Republican county supervisor in rural Buchanan County, Iowa, doesn’t have a lot in common with the leading democratic socialists in Congress. But on this bit of policy they agree: Data centers are proliferating across the American landscape too fast.

Vogel voted earlier this year for a moratorium that temporarily bans data centers from setting up shop in her heavily Republican county, which favored President Donald Trump 63% to 35% in 2024. In Washington, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt. — the nation’s two most prominent democratic socialists — have proposed a similar moratorium that would cover the entire country.

“I don’t think this is a Republican or Democratic issue,” Vogel said on the sidelines of the Iowa State Association of Counties’ annual conference here in late August, adding that she hasn’t talked to a single voter at home who wants data centers.

Dawn Vogel, a Republican supervisor in Buchanan County, Iowa, voted for a temporary moratorium on data centers in the county. Frank Thorp V for NBC News

“It’s an issue of what’s the best use for the land, what’s the best use for our natural resources,” she said. “You can have all the data you want to in the world, but if you don’t have water to drink, you don’t have humans to use the data.”

That point of view places Vogel in a loose, but very large, populist coalition that is fighting the rise of data centers at the ballot box, with yard signs, in courts and at all levels of government as November’s midterm elections approach.

An NBC News Decision Desk Poll powered by SurveyMonkey, conducted from Aug. 20 through Sept. 1, found that 69% of respondents oppose the construction of AI data centers in their local area, with 45% saying they “strongly oppose” the idea.

They are all at odds with President Donald Trump.

“The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post at the end of August. “If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign.”

But it’s more about backyards than being seen as backward, according to voters who spoke to NBC News on a recent road trip along Interstate 80 from Nebraska to New Jersey — a swath that includes eight swing districts key to determining which party will control the House next year and two marquee Senate races. These voters, who span the political spectrum, said they don’t want data centers anywhere near their communities.

For some, the issue has become a touchstone for the feeling that the powerful are taking advantage of the powerless.

“All of the data centers that are starting to pop up in areas, I find that troublesome because it drives utility costs for citizens in the area,” said Tamara Clark, 49, a Democratic voter who works in the healthcare industry. “I don’t feel like the rich should continuously get rich while we have to grovel for what we need in our everyday necessities.”

In Clark’s congressional district, Rep. Marcy Kaptur, D-Ohio, a 22-term incumbent, is using the issue against her rival, Republican Derek Merrin, who cast a 2017 vote in the state Legislature that helped extend tax breaks to companies that build data centers in the state.

Tamara Clark, an Ohio Democrat, said she finds it "troublesome" that data centers drive up utility costs for nearby residents. Frank Thorp V for NBC News

Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, who is seeking to hold his seat against Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown, was a full-throated advocate for data centers when he was the state’s lieutenant governor. But in July, he introduced legislation in the Senate that would require utility companies to charge large-scale data center operators enough money to cover the costs of increased electricity and water use.

His change of tune reflects a broader shift among elected officials who embraced data centers as a way to bring jobs and tax revenue to their cities, counties and states. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, D-Pa., who is on the ballot in November, signed a new batch of data center regulations in August after having encouraged companies to locate them in his state.

While Republican voters are more supportive of data centers than Democrats and independents, the majority of them remain opposed — 57% to 43% — according to the NBC News Decision Desk poll. The survey found that 81% of Democrats and 71% of independents are against data centers being built in their communities.

While supporters have been less demonstrative, their ranks extend beyond the AI companies building data centers and the politicians who have looked to them as economic development engines.

National and local labor unions involved in the construction and maintenance of data centers tout them as a boon for workers, both as a source of jobs and for high rates of pay. Several data center workers in Ohio spoke to NBC News about those benefits on the condition of anonymity because, according to one of them, they have agreed not to discuss their jobs with the media.

That worker said he can make as much as $5,000 in a week, including overtime, at a relatively low-level union job.

“It’s helping a lot of people — a lot of work going on, a lot of people benefiting from it,” the data center worker said, adding that he was warned by friends about problems, from overuse of water resources to weird ringing sounds, that he has not witnessed at his workplace.

“It’s scary,” he said. “You got a lot of people that say all these horrific things. I was told all these negative things about data centers, and then I started working at one, and I didn’t see any of the things I was told about.”

He said he would like to see proponents and critics work together to fix any problems with data centers so that they can continue to be built and operate without disruption to the surrounding communities.

Jordan Cloe, an electrician, is concerned about a data center's water consumption in Altoona, Iowa. Frank Thorp V for NBC News

But Jordan Cloe, 47, an electrician from Bondurant, in Iowa’s hotly contested 3rd Congressional District, said he’s worried about the resources used by a data center in neighboring Altoona.

“Did we have any data on what the implications were about water consumption or anything? Like, we just built a power grid where that thing sits,” he said. “Did we get to use that? No, they gobbled that up.”

Cloe, who said he aligns more with Democrats, said he doesn’t know anything about Sarah Trone Garriott, the Democratic challenger to Republican Rep. Zach Nunn, but that he plans to vote for her in November.

For Vogel, the county supervisor, the unresolved questions are enough reason to keep data centers out of her county — at least for now.

“We need to do what’s best for Buchanan County and then, you know, if the companies want to come knock on the door,” she said, “then we’ll talk.”

World.title: Armed man confronts Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton at event; suspect arrested
World.content:
An armed person “lunged” at Amy Acton, Ohio’s Democratic nominee for governor, and injured several people at a fair, a spokesperson for her campaign said Sunday.

A suspect, Patrick Havas, 38, was arrested, according to the Mahoning County Sheriff’s Office.

The incident, according to a statement from the sheriff’s spokesperson, Gerry Ricciutti, occurred around 2:30 p.m. Sunday while Acton visited the annual Canfield Fair in Canfield, a suburb of Youngstown. Acton, a physician, was not hurt and remained on-site to attend to one of the injured people, according to a photo a person at the event shared with NBC News.

The extent of injuries to others was not immediately known.

Acton and her husband, Eric, “are grateful for the swift and decisive action of law enforcement and are praying for the recovery of those injured,” said Addie Bullock, the campaign’s spokesperson.

“This kind of violence has no place in Ohio,” Bullock added. “Dr. Acton will always stand up to the chaos, hate and vitriol that pits us against one another.”

Acton was speaking to a crowd in the Mahoning County Democratic Party’s tent at the fair when Havas, who lives in Canfield, approached with a cellphone set up to record the visit, Ricciutti said.

“As he was entering the tent, Havas started pushing his way through the crowd,” Ricciutti added. “Dr. Acton’s security detail, which was made up of Ohio State Highway Patrol troopers, confronted Havas, and as that was happening, two people were knocked to the ground.”

After law enforcement officials arrested Havas, they recovered two handguns and a set of brass knuckles, Ricciutti added. In a separate statement, the Ohio State Highway Patrol, which provides protection to Acton because she is a candidate for governor, said officials also found that Havas had a Taser. Havas did not brandish the weapons or remove them from their holsters, according to investigators.

Havas was booked at the Mahoning County Jail “on charges of disorderly conduct and two counts of assault,” according to the Highway Patrol statement.

“The Ohio State Highway Patrol and Mahoning County Sheriff’s Office are conducting an investigation into what led up to the incident [and] no other details are available at this time,” the statement added.

Acton faces Republican nominee Vivek Ramaswamy, a businessman who ran for president in 2024, in the November general election to determine DeWine’s successor. Polls have indicated a close race.

Ramaswamy also had been scheduled to visit the fair Sunday afternoon.

“Candidates should be able to meet with voters without having to worry about threats or violence,” Ramaswamy spokesperson Connie Luck said in an emailed statement. “What happened today is completely unacceptable and has no place in politics, and we hope ... that no one was hurt.”

Acton was Ohio’s health director under term-limited Gov. Mike DeWine, a Republican, in the early days of the Covid-19 pandemic.

DeWine said in a statement Sunday that he and his wife had spoken to Acton and that they were grateful she was not hurt.

“Violence or the threat of violence at political or public events is always unacceptable,” DeWine said. “This case is now in the hands of law enforcement and will be investigated thoroughly.”

Sen. Jon Husted, a Republican who in his previous role as lieutenant governor served with DeWine and Acton, posted on X that he and his wife were “disturbed by the attempted attack.”

“We are grateful for law enforcement’s quick response,” Husted added. “There is no place for this kind of behavior, and it must never be tolerated.”

Mahoning County Democratic Party Chair Christopher Anderson, whose group hosted Acton on Sunday, wrote on Facebook: “What happened at our tent today during today’s visit from Dr. Acton is reprehensible and should be condemned by leaders on all sides of the aisle. MCDP is grateful for the quick response by our local law enforcement officials as well as the Ohio State Highway Patrol providing Dr. Acton security.”

World.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to allow mail ballot restrictions to move forward for a third time
World.content:
The Trump administration Sunday asked the Supreme Court to temporarily allow the U.S. Postal Service to exert some control over mail-in voting in the upcoming midterm elections, just two days after a federal judge blocked the USPS from doing so.

It’s the third time the Trump administration has escalated the matter to the Supreme Court, as North Carolina last week became the first state to begin sending mail-in ballots to voters less than 60 days before the midterm elections.

On Friday, U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani issued an order preventing the administration from carrying out the Trump-directed USPS regulation on mail-in ballots.

The directive is the president’s latest attempt to impose new forms of federal control over elections, which are typically run by states.

It would allow the USPS to track mail-in ballots and potentially reject ballots that are sent to and from voters not included in a federal database.

This application to the court comes after Talwani issued a preliminary block on enforcing the USPS rule, saying it’s likely unlawful and unconstitutional for the federal government to dictate how mail-in ballots are handled.

In her order Friday, Talwani also cited the rushed nature of the rule, writing that the “immediate implementation of the Final Rule issued less than seventy days before the November 2026 election threatens disenfranchisement of millions of United States citizens who seek to vote by mail.”

In Sunday’s filing to the Supreme Court, the Trump administration argued: “Contrary to the claims of the district court and respondents that the Postal Service is trying to federalize the rules for mail-in voting, the Postal Service’s final rule imposes only modest envelope-design and addressee-information requirements for federal-election ballots sent via U.S. Mail.”

Specifically, the filing argues, the rule “requires States to upload the name, address, and barcode information of intended recipients of ballot mail in an online portal — information that election officials would necessarily already possess to send ballot mail under the Rule to those recipients.”

“The Rule ensures that States remain responsible for determining voter eligibility and eligibility to vote by mail, and it does not dictate ballot content, mailing or receipt deadlines, or ballot-counting procedures. The Rule thus plainly does not seize control of States’ administration of elections — it simply imposes reasonable preparation requirements for certain election-related mail,” the filing adds.

Sunday’s application to the Supreme Court comes after the Trump administration already twice asked the highest court to intervene in this case. The Justice Department withdrew its previous pending request after submitting Sunday morning’s application related to Talwani’s most recent order.

The rule stems from a March executive order signed by President Donald Trump.

It came just weeks after the president suggested that Republicans should “nationalize” elections, a comment that drew criticism from local election officials and lawmakers from Trump’s own party.

World.title: Here’s the biggest news you missed this weekend
World.content:
Dawn Vogel, a Republican county supervisor in rural Iowa, doesn’t have a lot in common with the leading democratic socialists in Congress. But on this bit of policy they agree: Data centers are proliferating across the American landscape too fast.

Vogel voted earlier this year for a moratorium that temporarily bans data centers from setting up shop in her heavily Republican county, which favored President Donald Trump 63%-35% in 2024.

“I don’t think this is a Republican or Democratic issue,” Vogel said on the sidelines of the Iowa State Association of Counties’ annual conference in late August, adding that she hasn’t talked to a single voter at home who wants data centers.

An NBC News Decision Desk Poll powered by SurveyMonkey, conducted from Aug. 20 through Sept. 1, found that 69% of respondents oppose the construction of AI data centers in their local area, with 45% saying they “strongly oppose” the idea.

They are all at odds with Trump.

U.S. strikes 3 Iranian oil tankers, military says

Kharg Island in the Persian Gulf off Iran in a satellite image. Gallo Images / Gallo Images via Getty Images file

The U.S. military said its forces struck three Iranian oil tankers Saturday after Iran launched ballistic missiles toward two Navy ships.

A U.S. aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer evaded multiple attacks by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and no American personnel were harmed, Central Command said.

CENTCOM said U.S. forces retaliated by permanently disabling one crude oil carrier off the coast of Kharg Island and one near Jask. Forces also destroyed a third vessel near the Gulf of Oman.

“If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours,” CENTCOM’s commander said. “We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet.”

Iran’s Foreign Ministry strongly condemned the U.S. strikes, calling them “illegal and aggressive” and accusing Washington of waging a naval blockade and economic war.

‘Meet the Press’

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., criticized Republican leadership on a number of issues including the Trump administration’s handling of the Ukraine peace process.

Kennedy told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” he believes the Trump administration should take a different approach to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The Louisiana Republican also said his party should do something about inflation ahead of the midterm elections but that it’s “not likely.”

Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., told “Meet the Press” in a separate interview that Trump has “undoubtedly” committed impeachable offenses but that Democrats would also focus on issues like healthcare if they win back the House.

“Everybody on our side understands that impeachment is a critical tool in the toolbox for constitutional self-defense against a president acting like a king, an imperious, lawless, arrogant king,” Raskin said, responding to a question about whether Democrats would move to impeach Trump if they retake the House.

Rescuers in Nepal pull two more people out alive after devastating floods

Rescuers in Nepal pulled a man and a woman alive in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of people still missing.

The man, a Chinese national, was rescued from a hydropower tunnel, according to a social media post from the prime minister’s office, bringing to three the number of workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project.

A photo released by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed two rescuers carrying the man out of the tunnel. He was undergoing a health assessment, the army said.

In flood-hit Nuwakot, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal’s army spokesperson said. She was airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment. Images released by the army showed rescuers finding the woman covered in mud inside the damaged house.

Five dead after Amazon-branded cargo plane overruns runway at Miami airport, striking multiple vehicles

Five people are dead and five others are injured after an Amazon-branded cargo plane crashed just outside Miami International Airport on Sunday afternoon, officials said.

The Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft overran the runway while it was landing, according to officials. The plane was arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico, the Federal Aviation Administration said.

Three people are in critical condition and were taken to a trauma center, and two others were taken to a local hospital, according to the Miami-Dade fire chief.

U.S. envoys meet with Zelenskyy in Kyiv after peace talks in Moscow

U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv on Sunday, a day after meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow to discuss efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

Witkoff and Kushner were greeted by Zelenskyy in Kyiv after arriving in the Ukrainian capital by train from the Polish border, having flown there from Moscow.

“Ukraine has always been and will remain constructive. We are interested in bringing the end of the war closer,” Zelenskyy said in a post on X, adding that Ukraine’s “proposals are ready.”

Putin, for his part, did not publicly signal any movement from his previous steep demands, which seek major concessions from Ukraine.

The renewed talks appear to be Washington’s latest effort to end the nearly five-year war after months of stalled momentum amid the conflict with Iran.
